1.title: Vision and Core Invariant
1.intent: sprag is an extensible terminal platform exposing each pane as structured cell data, not pixels, so plugins read and drive AI tools.
rationale_bullets: AI reads the screen as structured cell data, never pixels — the platform's reason to exist
Core stays closed for modification; AI-tool features attach as swappable plugins
scene-as-data is an invariant every plugin upholds, not a replaceable feature
Built on pinion as consumer and dogfood, reusing its scene-as-data RPC surface
caveats_bullets: no-pixels binds the core AND every plugin; it is the platform's purpose, not a default

alternatives_rejected.alternative: Screen-scrape a TUI multiplexer like tmux
alternatives_rejected.reason: state only visible as pixels, no extension points

alternatives_rejected.alternative: Hardcode AI loops into the core
alternatives_rejected.reason: violates open/closed; the AI ecosystem changes fast

2.title: Architecture: Core and Plugin Split
2.intent: The core owns scene-as-data consumption and the plugin extension API; AI-tool adapters, loops, and policies are swappable plugins.
rationale_bullets: Plugin extension API is the #1 core design task per README, above PTY and the cell grid
Core is the stable foundation; plugins extend it without modifying the core
The first dogfood consumer (terminal) informs the extension API; no speculative design
caveats_bullets: Extension API core is not built speculatively this iteration; the terminal slice informs it first
Statechart/codegen logic uses SCE (scxml-core-engine); pinion-forge already builds on it

alternatives_rejected.alternative: Design the extension API with no consumer

alternatives_rejected.reason: no plugin boundary; fails the platform purpose

3.title: pinion Consumer Contract
3.intent: sprag owns terminal state and projects it into pinion's GridBuffer each frame; pinion is a read-only projection, not an emulator.
rationale_bullets: pinion R969: the producer owns authoritative state; pinion projects with no per-cell mutation
Single owner of terminal state is the SSOT; GridBuffer is a one-directional derivation
Scene::TextGrid (pinion 5.41, d9f8d39) is delivered: cells, cursor, attrs, color, screen, damage
winsize SSOT: cols/rows derive from layout rect; sprag sets PTY TIOCSWINSZ from the snapshot
outputs_bullets: Per-frame GridBuffer projected into Scene::TextGrid, served over scene/snapshot
caveats_bullets: Scrollback beyond the visible screen is not modeled by pinion (R1.4 gap); the producer projects it
Glyph paint is deferred (paint-opaque); the headless data path does not need it
Headless winsize (R3): producer sets grid rect from dims x CellMetric; compute_layout is windowed
RPC server read-only (R4): scene/key does not reach the PTY; key->PTY encoding deferred (R2.6)
Winsize (R5, corrects R3): scene() leaves rect unset; authoritative dims = buffer_cols/rows
R16: scrollback is modeled producer-side via Screen::full_text (corrects the R1.4-gap above).
Screen text is single-source: in-process capture and the RPC full_text query both read full_text.

alternatives_rejected.reason: breaks producer/projection; sprag loses the state SSOT
not how TextGrid works; the buffer is replaced wholesale each frame

4.title: VT Strategy: termwiz Parser plus Owned Emulator
4.intent: Embed termwiz as the verified escape parser and cell/input primitives; sprag owns the emulator state machine behind a VtPort.
rationale_bullets: README mandate: embed a verified VT parser, do not implement it (the max-risk point)
termwiz (published, semver) supplies the verified parser, Cell/color types, and input encoding
The emulator state machine (cursor, scroll, modes, alt-screen) is sprag core IP on termwiz
VtPort isolates the VT library (open/closed) so the choice stays reversible
inputs_bullets: termwiz crate modules: escape parser, surface/cell, color, input
outputs_bullets: sprag-vt crate: VtPort trait plus a termwiz-based emulator owning screen state
caveats_bullets: termwiz gives no full emulator state machine; that layer is sprag's responsibility
Self-owned emulator reintroduces VT risk; mitigate via a conformance harness behind VtPort

alternatives_rejected.reason: effectively abandoned, fork-dependent, missing SGR attrs; fails the standard
published full emulator but API churn; less input-encoding surface
most complete but unpublished (git-rev/fork only); dependency-hygiene smell

R100.decision_summary: Round 100: consume PINION-PR47 (winit-free RPC transport-injection seam, delivered pinion R1263). Pin-bump 7 pinion-* 03e0c5a7 (R1200) to 24409c46 (R1263); SCE 3078f8bf unchanged (pinion's own SCE pin matches, one Engine instance). sprag-gui mounts an always-on fixed-path Unix-domain RPC socket (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sprag-gui.sock) through the shell's on_rpc_ingress hook, replacing the per-session stdin=FIFO wiring: the endpoint is execution-independent and the socket plus pinion's still-present stdin reader share one RpcIngress into one dispatch core (purely additive). Transport policy is sprag's (PR-47 third layer): rpc.rs owns path resolution, boot state (SPRAG_RPC), and runtime on/off via SIGUSR1 flipping TransportControl::set_enabled; the reusable UnixSocketTransport adapter is pinion-provided (pinion-rpc-transport, seam-only dep). This delivers the user ask (always-open RPC without per-session setup, plus runtime on/off) and matches the PR-47 three-layer design (dispatch=pinion, transport mechanism=reusable adapter, transport policy=consumer). Live-verified end to end.

R101.decision_summary: Round 101: extract the pane-command assembly to a single SSOT. A 3-lens adversarial session review found the CommandBuilder + TERM=xterm-256color + $SHELL-fallback + program-label logic re-encoded across every frontend (gui pane_command, host workspace.rs build_command/default_shell_command, sprag-term build_command/default_shell). New sprag_terminal::command_from_parts + default_shell_command are the one home for that assembly (sprag-terminal owns CommandBuilder and is a dep of every frontend); each frontend now keeps only its spec-parsing POLICY (which env var / JSON argv / CLI flag the spec comes from) and delegates the build. Behavior-preserving, unit-tested. This restores the SSOT the review flagged as violated; it is the first remediation round after reverting a redundant host-server binary the same review caught (reverted before push, no net history).

R102.decision_summary: Round 102: fix the two smells the session review found in R100's rpc.rs. (1) The runtime on/off control was a SIGUSR1 blind toggle (set_enabled(!is_enabled())) -- not idempotent or assertable, since a lost or duplicated signal inverts the intent. Replaced with LEVEL semantics: SIGUSR1 enables, SIGUSR2 disables, so the outcome is deterministic regardless of current state (kill -USR2 always withdraws). (2) The ENDPOINT process-global was OnceLock<Arc<TransportControl>> whose doc claimed the signal thread reached the control through it -- false, the thread used its own captured Arc. Made ENDPOINT the sole owner (OnceLock<TransportControl>, no Arc): it is both the liveness anchor and where the control thread reads the control to switch exposure, so the doc is now accurate and endpoint liveness no longer depends on the control thread having spawned. Live-verified idempotency with real signals.

R103.decision_summary: Round 103: extract sprag's RPC transport policy into a new frontend-agnostic crate sprag-rpc, resolving the anticipatory duplication the session review flagged (Agent 1 #4) BEFORE the headless host gains its own socket. sprag-rpc owns the always-on Unix-socket mechanism over pinion's PR-47 RpcIngress seam: path resolution, boot state, the SIGUSR1(enable)/SIGUSR2(disable) level control, and the process-lifetime TransportControl ownership. It is GPU-free (deps: pinion-rpc + pinion-rpc-transport + signal-hook only), so both the windowed GUI and the headless host reuse it without pulling in a shell/GPU. Callers pass an Arc<dyn RpcIngress> and a SocketOpts (their socket name + env vars): the GUI's ingress comes from pinion-shell's on_rpc_ingress hook; the host's (next round) will be a channel funnel into its single dispatch owner. sprag-gui/src/rpc.rs is now a thin wrapper naming the GUI policy and delegating to sprag_rpc::mount, and sprag-gui drops its direct pinion-rpc-transport + signal-hook deps. Behavior-preserving, live-verified.
changes_bullets: New GPU-free crate sprag-rpc: the frontend-agnostic RPC transport policy -- always-on Unix socket + SIGUSR1/2 level control + process-lifetime TransportControl owner, over pinion's PR-47 RpcIngress seam. mount(ingress, SocketOpts). 5 policy unit tests.

R104.decision_summary: Round 104: give the headless host (sprag-term) the always-on Unix socket, fixing the sequencing inversion the review flagged (Finding 6 -- the north-star server had only stdin while the GUI got the good transport). sprag-host now provides a single-dispatch funnel: FrameIngress (an RpcIngress that pushes frames into an mpsc channel) + dispatch_frames (the one owner thread that pulls frames and dispatches each through the existing handle_request core) + stdin_frames (the stdin producer). sprag-term mounts the socket via the shared sprag_rpc::mount with a FrameIngress, spawns the stdin producer, and runs dispatch_frames, so the socket and stdin funnel into one dispatch owner and share a consistent HostState view -- no concurrent-dispatch races, the same single-owner discipline pinion's UI thread gives the GUI. The old serve() (stdin-only, ended on EOF) is removed; the host is now a server that runs until SIGINT/SIGTERM (which cancels + joins in-flight plugin runs so a slow AI turn reaps). GPU-free throughout. Live-verified with stdin=/dev/null: the socket serves the full platform (panes+mux+plugins), SIGUSR1/2 toggle it idempotently, SIGTERM exits cleanly.

R105.decision_summary: Round 105: begin the GUI-as-client-of-host increment. Topology DECIDED (user, cost-no-object "most long-term-correct"): B -- the GUI is a PURE transport-abstracted WIRE CLIENT of the host (tmux/mosh pattern; the read-data-not-pixels invariant becomes STRUCTURAL, not a shared-Arc convention; enables multi/remote/alt-frontend clients + fault isolation). This round is the topology-neutral first step of the prescribed sequence (unify scene-assembly SSOT -> host owns Workspace -> GUI attaches): decouple the pane-node ASSEMBLY from live-Screen PROJECTION. New pub pane_view_scene_from_cells(tag, cells, metric, font_size_px) is the Screen-free pane-node SSOT (focus-stop Container + composite {tag}#grid click anchor + R1002 font pin) that assembles the node from an already-projected GridBuffer alone; pane_view_scene(tag, spec) is now a thin live-Screen convenience over it (project_scrolled + overlay_preedit, then delegate), signature unchanged so the in-process GUI caller (build_pane_scene) is untouched. This is the exact seam the future wire client shares -- it will feed cells reconstructed off the host's served data model to build the byte-identical pane node without ever touching a live Screen. Behavior-preserving.

R107.decision_summary: Round 107: increment 2, step 1 of the GUI-as-client-of-host arc = PROVE the wire-fidelity assumption before any wiring (test-the-risky-assumption-first). New sprag-host test wire_round_trip_preserves_the_pane_cell_buffer establishes topology B's load-bearing guarantee: the paint-authoritative pinion GridBuffer (serde-able since PR-49/R106) survives a serde_json round-trip byte-for-byte on REAL projected production data -- indexed + truecolor + default colours, bold + reverse attrs, a wide (CJK) head+trailer cluster, the cursor (position/shape/visibility), the Alternate screen kind, and per-row damage generations. It asserts the whole buffer is Eq after round-trip (the strongest claim), plus position-independent per-field spot-checks so a dropped field names itself, plus that the CLIENT node assembled from the round-tripped buffer (pane_view_scene_from_cells, the R105 seam) carries the same cells as the direct projection -- i.e. a wire display client paints identically to the host. If serde ever drops a field the human/GUI path would render differently from the host's served data and the read-data-not-pixels invariant would break silently in the GUI; this fails HERE, in the crate that owns the wire seam, instead. Pure test addition: zero production change, zero render risk. Next (R108): the actual wiring -- host pane_cells data query + GUI reroute through pane_cells + client-side overlay_preedit + pane_view_scene_from_cells + removal of the now-superseded pane_view_scene/PaneViewSpec, live A/B-verified.

R109.decision_summary: Round 109: increment 3 round 1 of the GUI-as-client-of-host arc = the in-process CLIENT SEAM. Introduced sprag-gui/src/host.rs LocalHost: the GUI now reaches its panes ONLY through a typed client protocol (pane_count, pane_cells, pane_dims, pane_pty_size, pane_id, resize, pane_handle, pane_full_text, pane_command_label), encapsulating the single Workspace it owns. TerminalView changed from a public workspace: Workspace field (reached into directly across the GUI) to host: LocalHost (Workspace private) + the client's own rendering config (metric, font_size_px -- deliberately NOT host state). Rerouted all ~8 production coupling sites across 6 files (view build_pane_scene -> pane_cells + pane_dims; reflow -> pane_pty_size + resize; a11y pane_node -> pane_full_text + pane_command_label; dock undock size -> pane_pty_size; main create_external(s) -> pane_handle + reconcile_frame -> pane_dims; input scroll_view -> pane_dims, cycle_focus -> pane_count) plus the test call sites. The Workspace still lives in the GUI process (behind LocalHost) so this is behaviour-preserving and reversible; it is the exact method surface a wire transport backs in the later transport step, WITHOUT the call sites changing. Per the user's cost-no-object decision, this validates the client protocol against a real in-process consumer FIRST; the HostClient trait is extracted when the wire adds the second consumer (an interface designed against two impls is more correct than one). Input still flows through pane_handle/SpragPaneExternal (round 2 moves it over the client); the single-owner unification + wire transport land in later rounds.

The GUI touches the Workspace ONLY through it.

R110.decision_summary: Round 110: increment 3 round 2 of the GUI-as-client-of-host arc = INPUT over the client. The GUI's keyboard + IME-commit now go through the host client (LocalHost::send_key/send_text) instead of finding+invoking the pane's SpragPaneExternal in its own paint scene -- topology B: the GUI's input is a client SEND, not a mutation of its own scene (over the wire it becomes an RPC to the host; the GUI's scene will not hold the host's externals). Extracted the key->PTY encode+write SSOT into sprag_host::send_key/send_text (shared by the RPC input surface SpragPaneExternal::invoke AND the in-process client), so the human keyboard path and the AI scene/invoke path encode IDENTICALLY. LocalHost gained send_key(index, key, Modifiers) / send_text(index, text); route_key/route_composition drop their &mut Scene param (input no longer reads the paint scene) and call use_terminal().host.send_key/send_text; apply_key/apply_key_repeat/apply_composition (the WidgetCore trait methods) keep the trait-required scene param as _scene and pass nothing to the route fns. Added sprag-input as a direct sprag-gui dep (the Modifiers type + the meta->sup conversion to_input_mods). The pane input SpragPaneExternals STAY registered in the GUI's model scene (its RPC input surface); removing them is a later step. Behaviour-preserving (same encode+write SSOT). Reworked the 2 scene-inject tests into deterministic LocalHost tests + a focus-gate test; the chord tests are unaffected.
changes_bullets: sprag-host/pane.rs: new pub send_key(session, key, mods)->bool + send_text(session, text)->bool = the key->PTY / text->PTY encode+write SSOT; SpragPaneExternal::inject_key/text reuse them; exported from lib.rs.

sprag-gui: LocalHost gained send_key/send_text (call the host SSOT on the pane's handle); route_key/route_composition DROPPED their &mut Scene param and now call use_terminal().host.send_key/send_text (input is a client SEND); apply_key/apply_key_repeat/apply_composition keep the trait scene param as _scene. Added sprag-input dep (Modifiers + to_input_mods meta->sup).

Tests: the 2 scene-inject tests became deterministic LocalHost tests (send_key_routes_to_the_named_pane_only + send_text_writes_committed_text_to_the_named_pane, cat) + apply_key_gates_on_a_pane_focus + apply_composition_overlays_preedit_without_touching_the_pty (PTY-free). Chord tests unaffected. Fixed the stale route_key/route_composition/module scene-inject doc links.

This is the exact SSOT the keyboard path (route_key->LocalHost::send_key) now uses.

R111.decision_summary: Round 111: adversarial session review of the R105-R110 GUI-as-client-of-host arc (3 independent lenses -- architecture/SSOT, refactoring/smell, correctness/behaviour -- run in parallel, every finding cross-checked against the actual code before acting), then remediation. VERDICT: the load-bearing structure + SSOT are at the textbook bar (send_key/send_text single encoder SSOT shared by the RPC SpragPaneExternal AND the client; grid_node kernel; pane_cells/overlay/assemble split; runtime encapsulation verifiably enforced -- no GUI path touches Workspace/session outside host.rs) and NO reroute changed behaviour (all delegations byte-identical old-vs-new; the suspected TOCTOU is the pre-existing two-lock gap unchanged, the modifier mapping and empty-commit guard are identical). The real gaps were doc-honesty + test-coverage that slipped from moving fast -- exactly what the review exists to catch. Remediated ALL: (A) host.rs module header still said input flows through the SessionHandle post-R110 -> rewrote to enumerate send_key/send_text as protocol + honestly scope pane_handle as the one non-wire method + dual-authority/retirement transitional notes; (B) stale pane_view_scene name in the sprag-host pane_grid test helper (a dangling intra-doc link hidden in cfg(test)) -> pane_view_scene_from_cells; (C) route_composition non-empty Commit->send_text was covered by NO test -> restored an end-to-end apply_composition Commit test; (D) route_key multi-pane inject-through-apply_key untested -> restored an end-to-end apply_key routing test; both via a new #[cfg(test)] terminal::seed_terminal seam (deterministic cat panes, not shell-echo); (E) LocalHost::pane_id was pub protocol but only self-called -> private; (F) LocalHost::send_key/send_text dropped the host SSOT #[must_use] hiding route_composition discarded write -> #[must_use] + explicit let _ with rationale; (G) PaneDims/pane_dims -> PaneScrollFacts/pane_scroll_facts (scrollback_len is a depth, not a dimension); (J) pane_pty_size -> pane_grid_size (reads the emulator, not the PTY winsize); (K) resize swallowed error now traced; (N) trimmed a two-frontends-share plurality overclaim; plus removed the inert Scene::External boilerplate from the chord tests. Moved the single Workspace owner + typed client protocol out of the GUI (sprag-gui/src/host.rs LocalHost, deleted) into sprag-host as pub Host: it owns Arc<Mutex<Workspace>> (the shape the headless HostState and the topology-B end state already use), boots panes via spawn(command,label,cols,rows,on_dirty) taking an optional pinion-free Box<dyn Fn()+Send> wake hook (the GUI passes the RepaintSink closure, the headless server passes None), and serves the same protocol LocalHost did (pane_count/pane_cells/pane_scroll_facts/pane_grid_size/resize/send_key/send_text/pane_full_text/pane_command_label/pane_handle). R115a.decision_summary: Round 115a: the headless host serves the async change-notification contract (PR-50 consumed) -- increment 3 round 4 (WIRE transport) sub-step 1, additive, in-process GUI untouched. A wire client repaints on a pane's output by blocking on scene/waitFor instead of busy-polling scene/snapshot; this round makes sprag-term serve exactly that. HostState now holds a shared Arc<SceneRevision> (the ONE scene-version token, shared with the pane on_dirty bumpers) + an Arc<WaiterRegistry>, and installs the wake observer in new() (revision.set_observer(move |n| waiters.wake(n))). dispatch_frames is split into a per-frame dispatch_one that intercepts an async scene/waitFor {since} through pinion's try_async_wait_for BEFORE the synchronous handle_request: it parks the RpcReply (fires later, off the dispatch thread, on the scene bump that wakes it) or answers immediately if the scene already advanced; a non-waitFor / since-less frame hands the reply back for normal dispatch, so parking never builds the workspace scene. scene/revision + scene/waitFor added to SUPPORTED_METHODS (scene/revision is pinion's non-blocking read the client bootstraps its `since` from). sprag-term boot creates the revision BEFORE spawning and wires the initial pane's on_dirty to bump it, so the pane's output wakes parked waiters. This is the wake half only; serving pane cells as GridBuffer over the wire (R115b) and the GUI wire client + irreversible cutover (R115c) are later sub-steps. No pinion change (consumes R1269/R1270 WaiterRegistry/try_async_wait_for/SceneRevision::set_observer, delivered + bumped R114).

R115b.decision_summary: Round 115b: the headless host serves pane cells as a GridBuffer FRAME over RPC -- increment 3 round 4 (WIRE transport) sub-step 2, additive, in-process GUI untouched. This is the wire display client's per-frame DATA read (topology B): SpragPaneExternal gains a read-shaped `cells` invoke action -- invoke("cells", {offset}) -> IntrospectValue::Json({cells: <GridBuffer>, scrollback_len, visible_rows}). It is an invoke rather than a query because it carries the `offset` scrollback parameter, which pinion's path-only scene/query cannot (the open design point of R115b, settled: invoke is the only RPC method that carries args and returns a value). The three fields are read under ONE screen lock -- an atomically consistent snapshot (cells + scroll facts describe the same screen state, no torn read across two locks, unlike the in-process Host which takes pane_cells + pane_scroll_facts as two separate locks) -- and the GridBuffer is serialized AFTER the lock is released, so the CPU-bound serialization never holds the producer's screen. offset==0 is the live view; a larger offset windows into history (sprag_grid::project_scrolled self-clamps to the retained depth). The GridBuffer is serde-able since PINION-PR49, so the client reconstructs the EXACT buffer the host projected and feeds it to pane_view_scene_from_cells (the R105 client-assembly seam) to paint byte-for-byte -- "read data, not pixels" reaches the human path. Additive: the in-process GUI reads cells via Host::pane_cells directly (never this action); only the wire client (R115c) uses it. No pinion change.
changes_bullets: sprag-host/pane.rs: SpragPaneExternal gains a `cells` invoke action (CELLS_ACTION). read_cells(args) parses the scrollback offset, projects the scrolled GridBuffer + reads scrollback_len/visible_rows under ONE screen lock, then (off the lock) serializes to Json({cells, scrollback_len, visible_rows}). parse_offset_arg accepts null/absent (->0 live), a bare non-negative int, or {offset:N}; a negative/non-integer offset is TypeMismatch (project_scrolled self-clamps over-large offsets). CELLS_ACTION added to schema + the invoke match. Module doc documents the read-shaped invoke + why-invoke-not-query. Imports serde_json::json; calls sprag_grid::project_scrolled (both already deps of sprag-host).

R115c.decision_summary:
Round 115c: the GUI becomes a pure wire client of a sprag-term host PROCESS (topology B, the round-4 wire step; user-confirmed B+na -- spawn-or-attach, wire is the GUI default). The single Workspace/PTY owner now lives in a separate process and the GUI owns none of it. Extracted the host's typed surface into pub trait HostClient (pane_count / pane_cells / pane_scroll_facts / pane_grid_size / resize / send_key / send_text / pane_full_text / pane_command_label) with two impls: the in-process Host and a new WireHost. Added a blocking JSON-RPC HostConn client to sprag-rpc (connect-with-readiness-retry + call), the client twin of the existing server mount. WireHost spawns a sprag-term child (per-pid socket, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG + kill-on-Drop) or attaches to SPRAG_GUI_HOST_SOCK, boots n_panes over the sprag_mux spawn, maps tile index to PaneId, and runs a background poll thread that parks on the async scene/waitFor change-notification, refetches every pane's live cells into a shared cache, and calls request_repaint -- the off-thread-producer to repaint shape hello-live-data proves. view reads the cache (never a blocking socket call on the paint path); a scrolled-history read (offset > 0) is the one synchronous fetch. pane_grid_size reads GUI-tracked dims (the GUI is the resize authority) so the reflow guard sees a resize immediately with no round-trip and no resize loop. No pinion change (the client is a sprag concern; PINION-PR50 already cleared the repaint-over-wire blocker). Unit tests default to the in-process Host (a test cannot spawn a real child); production defaults to wire; SPRAG_GUI_HOST=inprocess is the escape hatch.

R116.decision_summary:
Round 116: adversarial 3-lens session review of R112-R115b (the GUI-as-client-of-host / round-4 wire work) + remediation, at the user's cost-no-object textbook bar. Three independent lenses ran in parallel (architecture/SSOT, refactoring/smell, correctness/concurrency); every finding was cross-checked against the actual code before acting (the R111 discipline). VERDICT: structure is long-term-correct toward topology B, the concurrency is sound (no bug/deadlock/reachable panic -- the correctness lens confirmed no-lost-wakeup, one-directional WORKSPACE->SCREEN lock order, wake-outside-lock, and read_cells' atomic snapshot against pinion's WaiterRegistry/SceneRevision source), and NOTHING was given up for cost -- EXCEPT one real SSOT blemish R115b introduced by hand-writing the wire frame's JSON instead of reusing the typed facts. Remediated all real findings; two were deliberately deferred to R115c with explicit rationale (not skipped for convenience). This changed CODE STRUCTURE only -- the wire JSON contract and all behaviour are byte-identical (re-verified live over the real socket).

Fixed: (SSOT, both lenses) the pane cell-frame's non-cell field set was defined twice -- the typed PaneScrollFacts struct AND a hand-built json! literal in SpragPaneExternal::read_cells -> now ONE type: PaneScrollFacts gains serde derive + a single from_screen population site, and read_cells serializes a CellFrame that #[serde(flatten)]s PaneScrollFacts, so the field names ARE the wire keys and the population is single-sourced. (silent-failure guard, correctness lens) HostState::new discarded SceneRevision::set_observer's install-once bool -> a future revision-reuse would hang every waitFor with no error; now assert!ed. (DRY, both lenses) dispatch_one parsed then handle_request re-parsed every frame -> extracted a handle_parsed core that dispatch_one calls with the already-parsed Request (parse-once on the hot path); handle_request stays the string entry for tests + the malformed path. (SSOT) method_not_supported hand-listed the methods SUPPORTED_METHODS already defines -> SUPPORTED_METHODS.join. (SSOT/invariant) the "spawn a pane whose output bumps THIS revision" boot recipe was hand-wired in sprag-term.rs AND the test -> one pub bump_on_dirty(&revision) helper both use. (doc-honesty) two stale LocalHost references the R112 comment-sweep missed (pane.rs send_key pub doc + sprag-gui/Cargo.toml) -> Host::send_key. (cleanup) a dead handle binding in a host test. Deferred to R115c (documented): the per-pane cells action vs the workspace-level waitFor granularity (the "batch is the natural wire shape" call, made when the wire client is built); and collapsing the in-process GUI's 2-lock cells+facts read to the wire path's 1-lock atomic frame (the GUI's offset math needs scrollback_len first -- it resolves structurally when the GUI becomes a wire client). No pinion change; no behaviour change.
changes_bullets: SSOT frame unification: PaneScrollFacts (host.rs) gains #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] + a pub(crate) from_screen(screen) single population site; Host::pane_scroll_facts calls from_screen. pane.rs read_cells builds a CellFrame { cells: GridBuffer, #[serde(flatten)] facts: PaneScrollFacts } via from_screen under one lock and serializes it -- the wire keys {cells, scrollback_len, visible_rows} now come from the types, not a hand-built json! literal. Removed the now-unused top-level serde_json::json import from pane.rs; added pinion_core::GridBuffer + crate::host::PaneScrollFacts imports.

rpc.rs: HostState::new asserts revision.set_observer(...) returned true (install-once silent-failure guard). Extracted pub handle_parsed(state, Request) as the dispatch core; handle_request(state, &str) parses then delegates (string entry + malformed parse-error path); dispatch_one parses once and calls handle_parsed with the parsed Request on the non-waitFor path (no re-parse). method_not_supported uses SUPPORTED_METHODS.join(", "). New pub bump_on_dirty(&Arc<SceneRevision>) -> Box<dyn Fn()+Send> helper (the pane on_dirty->revision.bump recipe); exported from lib.rs alongside handle_parsed.
sprag-term.rs boot + the rpc.rs host_with test helper both use bump_on_dirty (one recipe, prod == test). host.rs test send_text_reaches_the_pane_pty dropped a dead pane_handle binding.

Deps: added serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] } to the workspace + sprag-host (matches pinion's serde; the one instance is shared). Stale LocalHost -> Host in pane.rs send_key doc + sprag-gui/Cargo.toml comment.
verification_bullets: Review method: 3 adversarial lenses (architecture/SSOT, refactoring/smell, correctness/concurrency) ran in parallel; every finding cross-checked against the actual code before acting (2-of-N candidate concerns from my own pre-read were confirmed real; the concurrency lens found NO live bug -- it verified the park/wake, lock order, and atomic-snapshot against pinion's waiter.rs/revision.rs source). No finding was manufactured; the deferred items carry explicit rationale.

cargo test --workspace 241 passed / 0 failed (unchanged count -- pure refactor + one dead-binding removal); clippy --workspace --all-targets clean; RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps clean (fixed 3 now-redundant GridBuffer explicit link targets + a public->private dispatch_one link introduced by the refactor); rustfmt clean.

Behaviour-preserving, RE-VERIFIED LIVE over the real sprag-term socket after the refactor: (1) R115a async scene/waitFor still parks then wakes on a pane's output (parked -> injected pane output on a 3rd connection -> woke at revision 2); (2) R115b cells frame keys are byte-identical {cells, scrollback_len, visible_rows} with the GridBuffer nested (serde flatten produces the same wire shape as the old hand-built json); (3) scene/query works and method-not-found now lists the SUPPORTED_METHODS-derived set including scene/waitFor. The wire JSON contract did not change -- only the code that produces it.
carry_forward_bullets: R116 = adversarial 3-lens review of R112-R115b + remediation. VERDICT: topology-B structure is long-term-correct, SSOT holds (after this fix), concurrency sound, nothing given up for cost. All real findings fixed; wire contract byte-identical (behaviour-preserving).

The frame SSOT is now: PaneScrollFacts (serde, one from_screen population) is the ONE non-cell field-set; the wire CellFrame flattens it; the in-process Host::pane_scroll_facts reads it. handle_parsed is the dispatch core (parse-once); bump_on_dirty is the one pane-output->revision-bump recipe.

DEFERRED to R115c (documented, NOT skipped for convenience): (a) per-pane cells action vs workspace-level waitFor -- decide batch-vs-per-pane when the wire client is built (a woken client re-queries which pane? -- a workspace batch may be the natural shape given one revision for the whole scene). (b) the in-process GUI reads cells+facts under 2 locks (torn read, self-corrects next frame, single-threaded-safe -- confirmed not a live bug) while the wire path is 1-lock atomic; unify when the GUI becomes a wire client (its offset math needs scrollback_len first, so a single atomic frame is natural only once the GUI long-polls).

NEXT is still R115c (the GUI wire client, IRREVERSIBLE -- confirm before): HostClient trait (2 impls: in-process Host + socket client), GUI spawns/attaches a host process, try_async_wait_for long-poll -> request_repaint -> re-query the cells frame, retire pane_handle + the GUI's own SpragPaneExternal. The host now serves the full wire contract (change-notification + cells frame + input + pane list/plugins). serde is now a workspace dep (derive) for sprag's wire DTOs.

R118.decision_summary:
Round 118: attach-mode tmux-mirror, Round 1 of a user-confirmed cost-no-object decomposition (Round 1 -> 2a -> 2b). END STATE: the GUI is a live mirror of the host's pane set in BOTH spawn and attach modes, built on ONE host-PaneId <-> tile-slot abstraction; attach mode stops forcing the GUI's fixed pane count onto the host (the R117 deferral). Round 1 lays the host-side notification rail the live mirror needs, and closes a latent bug on today's default wire path.

The gap: only the BOOT pane's on_dirty was wired to bump the shared SceneRevision. A mux-spawned pane -- the path the GUI already uses to reach pane_count > 1 -- got the plain Workspace::spawn (on_dirty = None), so its own output never bumped the revision, and neither did a pane-set change (spawn / close). A wire client long-polling scene/waitFor thus could not learn the host gained or lost a pane, and a 2nd pane's independent output under-notified the repaint poll (it repainted only when the boot pane also produced output).

The fix (host-side only, additive, reversible): WorkspaceExternal now holds the shared Arc<SceneRevision>, threaded through workspace_scene from the ONE token HostState observes. spawn creates the pane via spawn_with_dirty(..., bump_on_dirty(&revision)) so the new pane's output bumps the SAME revision the boot pane's does, then bumps once more for the set-change (a mirror learns the pane exists before its first output). close bumps for the set-shrink. The in-process Host path is untouched (Round 1 is wire / dispatch only). No pinion change.
changes_bullets: Notification rail (sprag-host): WorkspaceExternal now holds the shared Arc<SceneRevision> (threaded through workspace_scene, cloned per scene-assembly from the one token HostState observes); its spawn / close are the only new writers of that token beyond the boot pane.

spawn wires the new pane with bump_on_dirty (spawn_with_dirty, not the plain spawn) so a mux-spawned pane's OWN output bumps the shared revision exactly as the boot pane's does, then bumps once for the set-grow; close bumps for the set-shrink.
Latent-bug closure on the default wire path: a 2nd (mux-spawned) pane's independent output now advances change-notification, so it repaints without waiting for the boot pane to also produce output.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace green; clippy --workspace --all-targets clean; RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps clean; rustfmt clean. +4 host tests (54 in the host crate; the workspace suite is otherwise unchanged).

New unit + dispatch coverage: workspace tests assert spawn / close bump the revision deterministically and a mux-spawned pane's own printf output bumps it (race-free +2 over the pre-spawn baseline); an rpc test drives a mux spawn through the REAL dispatch and confirms it wakes a parked scene/waitFor.

Real-socket integration (tests/wire_client.rs, against a spawned sprag-term binary): a mux spawn over the OS socket + real /sprag_mux dispatch grows the set and advances the notification, AND the mux-spawned pane's own echoed output advances it (the latent-bug closure) -- both read via the non-blocking scene/revision, no parked-read hang risk.
carry_forward_bullets: R118 = attach-mode tmux-mirror Round 1 of 3 (host notification rail). SceneRevision now bumps on ALL pane lifecycle (boot + mux spawn / close + every pane's output), not just the boot pane -- the live-mirror rail plus a latent 2nd-pane under-notification fix on the default wire path.

NEXT: Round 2a = the unified host-PaneId <-> tile-slot mirror abstraction (HostClient gains occupied-slot enumeration; WireHost gains the slot allocator + reconcile-from-panes-list; the boot count routed through the host so attach ADOPTS the host's set). Designed for the live-delta consumer from the start (no boot-only shortcut); then Round 2b feeds it live deltas.

Design invariant for 2b: the poll thread never touches reactive Signals -- it mutates a plain Arc<Mutex<MirrorState>> + requests repaint; a UI-thread Effect reconciles the dock topology Signal + focus to the mirror slot set. pinion change: none (the 8 static slots are reused + R1020 refreshes focus per frame). MAX_PANES = 8 is the honest attach bound.

R119.decision_summary:
Round 119: attach-mode tmux-mirror, Round 2a -- the unified host-PaneId <-> tile-slot mirror abstraction (the load-bearing round). Designed for the live-delta consumer from the START (no boot-only shortcut), so Round 2b feeds it deltas with no rework.

The core decoupling: the GUI conflated host pane IDENTITY (PaneId, monotonic, never reused) with GUI tile SLOT (&'static tag, MAX_PANES=8, tile index). A close would shift per-slot GUI state (scroll / preedit / focus, all keyed by index) onto the wrong pane. Round 2a separates them via a stable PaneId <-> slot mapping: the slot pool is fixed at 8, occupancy is dynamic, and a pane keeps its slot for its whole life.

HostClient gains occupied_slots() + is_pane_occupied() (default = the dense 0..pane_count(), which the in-process Host inherits; the wire client OVERRIDES it with its stable, possibly-non-contiguous set). WireHost folds its three parallel fields (panes / dims / cache) into ONE slot-indexed Arc<Mutex<Vec<Option<PaneEntry>>>> mirror + a PURE plan_slots allocator (survivors keep slots, a closed pane frees its slot, a newcomer takes the lowest free slot / reuses a hole) + a reconcile SSOT (boot = its all-new path, laying contiguous slots 0..N). boot_panes: attach mode ADOPTS the host's live set (clamped to MAX_PANES); spawn mode keeps spawn-to-N (the GUI is the operator). Every GUI consumer (view / input / a11y / reflow / main / split) iterates occupied_slots() / guards on is_pane_occupied(); next_focus cycles the occupied set (skipping holes); the boot dock topology routes its count through the host (the last structural env read closed). Behaviour-preserving in 2a (the boot set is contiguous 0..N). No pinion change.

WireHost (sprag-gui): the panes / dims / cache fields fold into ONE slot-indexed Vec<Option<PaneEntry>> mirror + a pure plan_slots allocator (stable PaneId<->slot -- survivors keep slots, a closed pane frees its hole, a newcomer takes the lowest free slot) + a reconcile SSOT (boot = the all-new path); boot_panes attach-ADOPTS the host set, spawn keeps spawn-to-N.

The user chose the purest fix (Option A) over the cheaper honest-doc patch: make the HostClient trait speak the HOST's language (stable PaneId), and move the slot<->PaneId mapping into ONE GUI adapter (SlotView) over any HostClient.

Both impls become pure IDENTITY clients: the in-process Host reads its Workspace by id; the wire WireHost holds a Vec<WirePane> data cache (host order, PaneId-keyed) + its poll, with NO slot concept. R122.decision_summary: Round 122: attach-mode tmux-mirror, Round 2b -- LIVE pane-set deltas, seated cleanly on R121's SlotView. The GUI now mirrors a host-side spawn/close at runtime (retiring the fixed pane count) in both attach and spawn modes. The mechanism was verified in pinion source before building: the wire poll thread may only mutate the plain Vec<WirePane> cache + request_repaint (Owner::cache / Signals are UI-thread-only, so it can never touch them); on the resulting frame, pinion's reconcile_frame pre-view hook -- which already runs every real paint in the root Owner to reconcile off-thread PTY producer state (scrollback depth) -- is the sanctioned place to fold the set change, NOT a bespoke Effect (a bare request_repaint re-runs no Effect) and NOT create_extra_externals. reconcile_frame calls SlotView::reconcile (now returning freed + added slots), then for each freed slot evicts its dock leaf + floating window and resets its per-slot Owner::cache state, and for each added slot admits an index-relative docked leaf; the post-view create_extra_externals then rebuilds the external set (scrollbars / dock panels / splitters) from the updated occupied set on the SAME frame. SlotView.slots became a RefCell (reconcile runs through the shared Rc<TerminalView>). The dock-leaf ops are surgical (not a rebuild) so user reorg / ratios / a co-existing float survive an unrelated pane's close; remove_pane_leaf / insert_pane_leaf are extracted as mode-neutral SSOT primitives shared by the collapse float/dock AND the new close/open (a gone pane can hold neither placeholder nor window, so eviction is unconditional of DockMode). Per-slot state is reset by MUTATION (pinion has no Owner::cache evict), which also keeps the boot-captured primary-scrollbar Rc<ScrollState> valid across a slot reuse. R123.decision_summary:
Round 123: adversarial 3-lens review of R122 (the Round 2b live-delta round) + remediation, at the user's cost-no-object textbook bar (the R111 / R116 / R117 / R120 cadence). Three independent lenses ran in PARALLEL over the R122 diff (3af61d8..HEAD) -- architecture/SSOT, refactoring/smell/doc-accuracy, correctness/concurrency -- and every finding was cross-checked against the actual code (and pinion source) before acting: real ones fixed, non-issues dismissed with rationale.

VERDICT: no BLOCKER and no functional bug. The correctness/concurrency lens VERIFIED IN SOURCE the three properties R122 rests on: (a) RefCell borrow discipline is panic-free (SlotView::reconcile calls host.pane_ids() BEFORE self.slots.borrow_mut(), pane_ids never re-enters the slots RefCell, and nothing borrows slots across reconcile_frame's post-reconcile evict/admit/reset/scroll steps); (b) merge_panes-vs-concurrent-resize has no lost update (the survivor-dims read + the Vec swap are one atomic lock hold, resize writes by identity under the same lock -- verified across every interleaving); (c) the windows-signal write from reconcile_frame is safe because pinion applies it DEFERRED (the signal Effect only posts AppEvent::WindowsDirty; the winit add/drop runs later with &mut self), so no synchronous window op happens mid-render. Monotonic PaneIds and all edge cases (>8 panes, 0-pane, spawn+close same wake, inert sentinel, frameless newcomer) were traced safe.

Fixed (the one real defect + a conceptual bug + doc drift): (1) the freed-slot reset was INCOMPLETE -- the per-slot scrollbar INTERACTION signal (hover/drag, keyed by slot) was not reset, so a pane closing mid-hover/drag leaked a stale brightened/dragging highlight onto a reused slot, contradicting the docs' clean-reuse promise; reset_pane_scroll now resets it (to Idle) too, and is the ONE home for all scrollbar-owned per-slot state, with reconcile_frame documenting the full per-slot reset registry (the scattered-reset smell was the root cause of the miss). (2) merge_panes conflated the two authorities: a survivor kept prior.label, but the label is HOST-authoritative (spawn-set, GUI never mutates it) -- now survivors keep GUI-tracked dims but ADOPT the query's label (forward-correct if host titles ever go dynamic). (3) three docs still called pane 0's scrollbar the primary -- falsified by R122's own re-home -- now corrected to the non-pane sentinel model.

Also: build_cache now routes through merge_panes (the empty-existing case) via a shared fetch_frames helper, and refresh_known was deleted (the query-fail fallback folds into refresh_to_set with a cache-derived seed snapshot) -- one fetch path + one merge SSOT for boot and steady-state. The HostClient::pane_ids membership contract ("renderable-now": in-process immediate, wire client one wake late) is documented. The one medium finding -- evict_pane can empty the main dock while a floater survives -- was resolved by SCOPING float_would_empty_the_dock as a float-GESTURE guard (a host close is authoritative and may legitimately empty the dock; force-redocking the user's floater would be worse), a doc-only clarification with no behavior change. Deferred (documented, safe today): unifying the two dock-tree construction paths (build_boot_topology vs insert_pane_leaf) -- a fragility, not a bug (a duplicate-leaf tolerance + a factory-fires-after-new ordering keep it safe; a comment now pins it). No pinion change.
changes_bullets: Fixed the one real reset gap: reset_pane_scroll now also resets the per-slot scrollbar INTERACTION signal (to Idle), so a slot reused by a pane closing mid-hover/drag no longer inherits a stale highlight; it is the ONE home for all scrollbar-owned per-slot state, and reconcile_frame documents the full freed-slot reset registry (the scattered-reset root cause).

merge_panes splits the two authorities: a SURVIVOR keeps its GUI-tracked dims but ADOPTS the host-set label (host-authoritative); build_cache routes through merge_panes via a shared fetch_frames helper and refresh_known is deleted (query-fail folds into refresh_to_set) -- one fetch + one merge SSOT. Corrected three retired pane-0-primary scrollbar docs to the sentinel model.

Scoped float_would_empty_the_dock as a float-GESTURE guard (a host close may authoritatively empty the dock, doc-only, no behavior change); documented the HostClient::pane_ids renderable-now membership contract; added a boot-race duplicate-leaf tolerance comment + delta/eviction tests.
verification_bullets: Review method: 3 adversarial lenses (architecture/SSOT, refactoring/smell/doc-accuracy, correctness/concurrency) ran in parallel over the R122 diff; every finding cross-checked against the code before acting. Dismissed with rationale: the inert primary sentinel (verified sound -- never painted, never routed), the one-wake frame/dims skew (pre-existing, benign), focus-crossing on same-slot reuse (desirable).

The correctness lens VERIFIED IN SOURCE (pinion + sprag), not assumed: RefCell borrow discipline is panic-free (pane_ids before borrow_mut, no re-entry, no cross-op live borrow); merge_panes-vs-resize has no lost update (atomic read+swap under one lock + identity write-back, all interleavings); the reconcile_frame windows-signal write is deferred via AppEvent::WindowsDirty (no sync winit op mid-render); monotonic never-reused PaneIds; >8 / 0-pane / spawn+close-same-wake all safe.

Re-verified LIVE on :0 (attach): boot adopt + spawn add (1->2 tiles, both reflow) + close remove (survivor reclaims full width) -- no regression from the build_cache/merge_panes refactor.
carry_forward_bullets: R123 = adversarial 3-lens review of R122 (Round 2b live deltas) + remediation. VERDICT: no BLOCKER, no functional bug; the concurrency properties R122 rests on VERIFIED in source. Fixed: the incomplete freed-slot reset (the scrollbar interaction signal), the merge_panes label authority, the retired pane-0-primary doc drift; scoped the empty-dock guard (doc-only).

The attach-mode tmux-mirror ARC (R118 rail -> R119 slot abstraction -> R120 review -> R121 root-cause identity refactor -> R122 live deltas -> R123 review) is COMPLETE + reviewed. The GUI is a live mirror of the host's pane set in both spawn + attach modes.

R124.decision_summary: Round 124: a cost-vs-textbook session review of R122+R123 (the user asked directly whether it is textbook with no hacks/smells, whether cost ever beat the long-term-correct structure, whether SSOT holds, whether it heads to the north star — the lifetime-portfolio bar) + remediation. Two FRESH unanchored adversarial lenses ran in parallel over the whole session diff (3af61d8..HEAD) — a north-star/SSOT architect + a cost-compromise auditor — not given my rationalizations; every finding cross-checked against sprag + pinion source before acting. VERDICT: the north star HELD (topology B, both frontends pure identity clients, SlotView the one slot owner, NO pinion change) and concurrency correctness held (verified R123). But cost HAD beaten textbook in three places, all now fixed. (1) TWO dock-tree construction paths — a real SSOT violation deferred in R123 for cost (build_boot_topology's recursive build_row_node vs insert_pane_leaf both encoded the same tree-shape policy with two divider-id schemes; the slotview docs even CLAIMED one unified path while the code kept two). FIXED: one pure insert_leaf(tree, index, mint_id) primitive; build_boot_topology folds it (minter reproduces the former boot_split_id dividers EXACTLY, behaviour-preserving), runtime admit folds it; build_row_node retired; the float_pane/dock_pane forwarders collapsed so callers use remove_pane_leaf/insert_pane_leaf directly. (2) The primary-scrollbar SENTINEL is a local workaround of pinion's MANDATORY create_external/tag (no Option; compose_root always composes a primary at index 0; the sentinel violates the R55.G.17 painted-tag convention). Per sprag's own never-work-around-pinion ground rule, FILED PINION-PR51 (optional primary); the sentinel stays as the interim (behaviour correct). (3) The freed-before-added ordering + the per-slot reset registry were guarded only by COMMENTS (the scattered-reset smell that let the R122 interaction miss slip). FIXED: a single reset_freed_slot owner enumerating the full registry, and a reconcile_frame_reuses_a_slot_with_one_leaf test pinning evict-before-admit; also abstracted the HostClient::pane_ids trait doc. Dismissed with rationale: the sentinel is behaviourally correct (never painted/routed); reconcile_frame's set+scroll is the correct off-thread-producer seam; the slot-map+tree redundancy is inherent. Deferred NIT: no Owner::cache evict -> orphaned per-divider ratio signals grow over a churny session (bounded, no correctness impact).

Filed PINION-PR51 (optional primary External) + REQUIREMENTS index entry per the never-work-around-pinion ground rule; the primary sentinel is a local workaround of pinion's mandatory create_external/tag, kept as interim (behaviour correct), the pinion PR is the north-star-clean resolution.

R127.decision_summary: Round 127: CONSUME PINION-PR51 — sprag declares NO primary surface, and the R122 inert primary-scrollbar SENTINEL is RETIRED. This closes the last known pinion-gap workaround in sprag (filed R124 by the cost-vs-textbook review as the one place a local workaround stood in for an upstream fix; delivered by pinion R1304-R1308; bumped in R126; consumed here). sprag's TerminalViewer now overrides WidgetCore::primary_surface() -> None: every routable surface is a per-pane / per-split DYNAMIC extra (scrollbars, splitters, dock-panel handles; external_set_is_dynamic() == true), so there is no single canonical primary to name. create_external() / tag() become unreachable! markers -- they stay REQUIRED on the trait (so the has-primary majority keeps its compile-time guarantee) but the substrate never reaches them, exactly the shape pinion's own hello-no-primary reference consumer uses. Consumed against the ACTUAL delivered API (the primary_surface() Option descriptor, R1306) rather than the PR51 draft's proposed create_external/tag -> Option, which pinion deliberately rejected as it would have polluted ~150 existing impls. Effects: the state scene composes from the EXTRAS ALONE (no phantom index-0 node), the R55.G.17 painted-primary-tag convention no longer applies (sprag was deliberately violating it with a tag nothing paints), and the bare /external RPC shorthand now rejects with NoExternalAtPath (pinion R1307) instead of silently resolving an arbitrary pane extra as "the primary". Behaviour-preserving for the user: pane focus was already paint-derived (R1020 collect_focusable_tags), never tag-derived. The three contract obligations pinion places on a None binding were verified in sprag BEFORE the change: keybinding() is not overridden (default empty -- a keybinding event would otherwise reach the no-op send_to_primary and be dropped), apply_key never calls forward_key_to_external (which would re-derive Self::tag()), and nothing depends on Scene::primary_external().

R128.decision_summary: Round 128: the terminal's OSC window title becomes the pane's DISPLAY title — the full data path (PTY -> VT -> host -> wire -> GUI) plus the one surface sprag controls today (the floating window's header); the DOCKED header + the OS window title are blocked on a NEW pinion gap, FILED as PINION-PR52 (never worked around). sprag previously DROPPED OSC entirely (sprag-vt's apply() handled only Print/Control/CSI). Now the emulator parses the window-title family (OSC 0 SetIconNameAndWindowTitle, OSC 2 SetWindowTitle + termwiz's Sun spelling) into a live `title: Option<String>` exposed as VtPort::title; OSC 1 (icon name only) is correctly NOT treated as a window title. The title deliberately does NOT bump the emulator's `generation` — that stamp is ROW DAMAGE and a title carries no cells, so bumping it would force a needless cell re-render on every prompt; consumers still learn of the change because the OSC bytes arrive as PTY output, which already fires the session's on_dirty -> SceneRevision bump -> the GUI's waitFor poll re-queries the pane list. (The R96-era plan had said "gen-bump"; that predates topology B and conflated the damage stamp with a change signal.) The title rides to the client on the EXISTING host-authoritative pane-list channel as a NEW `title` field (null until the child sets one) — deliberately NOT overloading `command_label`, which names what was LAUNCHED, never changes, and is the a11y node name; conflating them would silently rewrite the a11y name and let a live child-controlled string masquerade as spawn identity. In the GUI, `title` is host-authoritative AND genuinely dynamic, so `merge_panes` re-adopts it every poll wake (including back to None when the child clears it) rather than freezing the first-seen name — the exact dynamic-title case the R123 label doc was written to be forward-correct for. ONE display policy (`view::pane_display_title`): prefer the child's live OSC title, fall back to the stable `panel_id` when it is absent OR BLANK (a child must not be able to blank the header). IDENTITY never derives from the title (dock-leaf panel_id, scene tags, focus, RPC paths stay put) — a child rewrites its title every prompt, so deriving identity from it would let a pane rename its own address (R70). Verified live on :0: the floater header shows the shell's live title (`coin@...:~`) instead of `terminal-0`, and it TRACKS a retitle (bash's PROMPT_COMMAND overwrote a test title at the next prompt), while the docked header still reads `terminal-1` — precisely the pinion-gated boundary PR-52 names.

R129.decision_summary: Round 129: pin-bump all 8 pinion-* crates d74e0775 (R1308) -> 688241a0 (R1325), which makes PINION-PR52 (filed by R128 the same day) AVAILABLE -- and carries ONE FORCED MIGRATION. pinion DELIVERED both halves of PR-52: (A) R1318 "a panel's display title is not its identity" = a `DockPanelChrome` carrying per-panel TITLE + STYLE providers (`with_title(|panel_id| Cow)`, `None` = identity so the title defaults to the panel_id) consumed by a new `view_dock_surface_chrome`, with the walker still OWNING the tag (a customizer that changes the tag now PANICS via `walker_owned_tag`) -- exactly the identity-preserving seam the PR asked for; plus R1320, which closed a naming leak R1318 left. (B) R1319 "a live window title, not a create-time one" = a `window_title_changes` diff + `set_title` pass in `reconcile_windows` (the twin of R1087's move pass), so an OPEN window's OS title can change; R1321 then fixed a swallowed retitle (the spec cache was only patched for position) and re-applies title on suspend/resume. NB pinion's own audit found `WindowSpec::title`'s rustdoc had CLAIMED the forwarding it did not do -- the doc-vs-code drift sprag hit from the outside. The FORCED MIGRATION: `view_floating_placeholder` gained a `display: &str` param (R1320) so the torn-off slot's painted label is SEPARATE from its tag -- the tag stays `{panel_id}_placeholder` because it is LOAD-BEARING (`resolve_drop` recovers the panel id from it to redock), while the label takes the display name. sprag passes its existing `pane_display_title(&slots, i)` (R128), so a floated pane retitled `vim README` no longer leaves a slot reading "(terminal-0 torn off)" beside a floater header reading "vim README" -- the precise mismatch R1320 names. sprag source change is that ONE call site; the pane-title data path (R128) already exists. SCE unchanged (pinion@688241a0 pins 3078f8bf = sprag's, so the single Engine<StatePolicy> holds). The REST of the PR-52 consumption -- routing the DOCKED header + tab labels through `view_dock_surface_chrome`'s title provider, and driving `WindowSpec.title` from the focused pane -- is a follow-up round; both are now unblocked, and R128's policy fn is the ready input for both.

R130.decision_summary: Round 130: CONSUME the rest of PINION-PR52 — the DOCKED panel's header + tab label, and every FLOATING window's OS title, now show the child terminal's live OSC window title. This finishes the R128 feature: a pane's display name is what the program calls itself (`vim README`, `coin@host:~`, an ssh remote), on every surface, while its ADDRESS stays `terminal-{i}`. (A) The docked header/tab: `view_main` swaps pinion's plain `view_dock_surface` for the new `view_dock_surface_chrome` and hands it a `DockPanelChrome::with_title(...)` provider that maps `panel_id -> pane_display_title` (the R128 policy fn, fallback included) and returns `Cow::Borrowed(panel_id)` — the walker's identity default — for a leaf with no live pane. The walker still OWNS the tag (pinion PANICS on a customizer that changes it), so this supplies only the string it PAINTS: the dock-leaf id, scene tag, RPC path and `DockPanelExternal` key stay `terminal-{i}`, and two panes may safely share a display title because only the ADDRESS must be unique. (B) The floating window's OS title (taskbar / alt-tab): new `dock::sync_floating_titles`, called from the pre-view `reconcile_frame` (the UI-thread seam that already folds the off-thread pane-set + scrollback deltas), tracks each floater's `WindowSpec.title` to its pane's display title behind a stable "sprag terminal — " app prefix (a bare `vim README` in a taskbar loses the app). It DIFFS and only `set`s the windows signal when a title actually changed — a `set` posts `AppEvent::WindowsDirty`, so a blind per-frame `set` would drive a winit window-reconcile on every paint. `undock_window_spec` now opens the window with that same title, so a floater never flashes a create-time name the first sync replaces. This is the consumer of pinion R1319's live `set_title` pass (pre-R1319 `WindowSpec::title` was create-time-only). The MAIN window's title is DELIBERATELY untouched: it would want the FOCUSED pane's title (the tmux convention), and the binding cannot read focus in the paint path — focus reaches it only through `apply_key`'s argument (keystrokes only, so a click-to-focus would leave a stale title) or the a11y hook (a layering violation, and the AT tree is not built every frame). Both workarounds are wrong, so per the ground rule this is FILED as PINION-PR53 (a binding-readable focus accessor) rather than hacked. sprag's `panel_id` doc is corrected accordingly: since R130 it is IDENTITY only, and a painted string solely as the no-title fallback.

The docked header AND the tab label now paint the child's OSC title; identity (tag/leaf/RPC/DockPanelExternal key) is untouched — the walker still owns the tag.

The latter diffs the windows signal and only `set`s on a real change (a `set` posts AppEvent::WindowsDirty), and skips the MAIN window.
sprag-gui main.rs: `reconcile_frame` step (3) calls `dock::sync_floating_titles()` — the pre-view UI-thread seam that already folds the off-thread pane-set + scrollback deltas.

sprag-gui split.rs: `panel_id`'s doc corrected — it is IDENTITY (leaf id + scene tag + RPC address + DockPanelExternal key) and, since R130, a painted string ONLY as the no-OSC-title fallback; every title surface now shows `pane_display_title`.

R131.decision_summary: Round 131: pin-bump all 8 pinion-* crates 688241a0 (R1325) -> b3e9883c (R1333), which makes PINION-PR53 (filed by R130 the day before) AVAILABLE. pinion DELIVERED it as R1327 "focus is readable, not only requestable": a new pinion-core module `focus_state` whose `focused() -> Option<String>` mirrors the shell-internal `FocusManager`'s focused tag into a core Signal, published from ONE funnel that every focus mover reaches (click / Tab / RPC / focus_request / modal / blur-restore). This is exactly the read side PR-53 asked for -- and the reference editor consumer in the same commit titles its MAIN window after its FOCUSED pane (the tmux rule R130 was blocked on). `focused()` auto-subscribes the calling reactive scope, so a `reconcile_frame` (root Owner scope) read re-runs and repaints on a focus change with no extra wiring. It agrees with `apply_key`'s `focused` argument on the GUI shell and with `focus/get` over RPC (same SSOT). NB pinion delivered a sibling module (`focus_state`), not the `focus_request` read-side extension PR-53 sketched as option (A) -- a cleaner shape (the request mailbox stays write-only; the read is its own thing), so consume `pinion_core::focus_state::focused()`. The bump also carries R1328 (a focus drop mid-paint now repaints; window_focused restore notifies observers) and R1329 (pane focus stops are named WAI-ARIA group nodes in the AT tree, plus a release-miscompile fix pinning pinion-a11y to 1 CGU) -- both internal to pinion, no consumer API change (proven: sprag compiles unchanged). This is an ENABLING bump (the R126 pattern): the actual consumption -- driving the MAIN window title from the focused pane's display title, the last surface R130 left as the PR-53 boundary -- is a follow-up round. R132.decision_summary: Round 132: CONSUME PINION-PR53 — the MAIN window's OS title now tracks the FOCUSED pane's display title (the tmux / gnome-terminal rule that the active pane names the window). This is the LAST title surface, and closes the whole window-title arc: R128 built the OSC-title data path (PTY -> VT -> host -> wire -> GUI) + the display policy; R130 lit the docked header/tab and the floater OS title (needing no focus); R132 lights the main window (which tiles several panes, so "which pane's title" is decided by FOCUS). The binding could not read focus in the paint path until pinion R1327's `focus_state`; R131 bumped it in. New `dock::sync_main_title(focused_pane: Option<usize>)`: sets the MAIN WindowSpec.title to that pane's `pane_display_title` behind the shared "sprag terminal — " prefix (via `window_title_for_pane`, factored out of the floater path so both read one format), or the plain app name `MAIN_WINDOW_TITLE` when focus is off any pane. Called from `reconcile_frame` step (4), which reads `pinion_core::focus_state::focused()` (the focus manager's own tag -- same SSOT as `apply_key`'s `focused`, reflecting click / Tab / request alike) and maps it to a pane index via `terminal::pane_index_of`. R133.decision_summary: Round 133: adversarial 3-lens session review of the R128-R132 window-title arc + remediation (the R111/R116/R120/R123/R124 cadence). Three FRESH parallel lenses (architecture/SSOT/north-star, refactor/smell/doc-honesty, correctness/concurrency/edge-cases) read the ~700-line arc diff cold (not given my rationalizations) over sprag + the pinned pinion; every finding was then re-verified against source by the orchestrator before acting. VERDICT: no BLOCKER, no panic, no repaint loop, no lost-title race -- the correctness lens CONFIRMED the reactive plumbing safe (diff-before-set + focus equality-skip + deferred WindowsDirty => quiescent steady state; no RefCell double-borrow; title propagates without a generation bump via unconditional per-batch on_dirty; merge_panes re-adopts incl clear-to-None; hostile chars can't inject -- vtparse drops C0 controls, serde escapes, set_title takes &str). But TWO real defects surfaced (both missed by the R132 tests), plus cleanups. FIXED: (1) MAJOR robustness -- the child-controlled title was UNBOUNDED in length (vtparse caps the OSC param COUNT, not the payload byte length), so a hostile/runaway child could grow an arbitrarily large String that is stored, re-cloned every poll wake, and shipped over the wire; the arc's own sibling buffer (RAW_CAPTURE_CAP) sets the project's bar. Now clamped in Emulator::osc to MAX_TITLE_BYTES (2048) on a char boundary (clamp_title), +test. (2) MAJOR/MINOR correctness -- sync_main_title titled the MAIN window after a focused FLOATING pane: focus is binding-wide and a torn-off pane keeps its slot OCCUPIED, so the guard `is_pane_occupied(i)` alone let a focused floater (painted in its own window, already titled by sync_floating_titles) leak its title onto the main window. Added the `!is_pane_floating(i)` guard (the sole float authority, the "which window is that pane in" check pinion's focus contract requires); a focused floater now leaves the main window at the app name. Extended the R132 test with the floated case it never covered. Cleanups: factored the diff-before-set discipline into ONE retitle_windows helper (both sync_main_title + sync_floating_titles use it); deleted the vestigial floating_window_title one-line forwarder (callers use window_title_for_pane); single-sourced the app-name token as APP_NAME + corrected MAIN_WINDOW_TITLE's overstated "cannot drift" doc; removed the dead SessionHandle::title (zero callers, YAGNI); fixed the stale pane_display_title doc (it framed the shipped docked-header/OS-title surfaces as future PR52 work) + 6 stale `view_dock_surface` prose refs (now `view_dock_surface_chrome`). Dismissed with rationale: the re-query-failure keeps-last-known-title (self-healing + documented, strictly better than blanking); the null-vs-empty-string wire representation (both fall back identically via pane_display_title's trim().is_empty()). SCE + pinion pin unchanged; no pinion change.

R134.decision_summary: Round 134: FILED PINION-PR54 (outer-dock redundancy widening) — a report-only round (no code change; the fix is pinion-side per the never-work-around-upstream ground rule). A sprag user observed that in a 2-pane side-by-side layout, dragging one pane toward the top/bottom of the other offers an OUTER full-span dock (a thin 22% strip at the window edge) instead of the inner 50/50 split they expect. Traced against pinion b3e9883c: `resolve_drop` classifies the OUTER perimeter FIRST, and `DockReorganizer::outer_dock_is_redundant` — which would suppress a pointless outer via SnapBack — only fires when the outer result is `same_shape` as the CURRENT tree (a literal no-op, e.g. dragging the right pane to the right edge). It MISSES the case where the outer result, though a different shape than now (Row->Column), is IDENTICAL to a plain inner split: `outer_dock_next` does `remove_leaf(source)` then `split_root(source, .., 0.22, ..)`, so when removing the source leaves a single leaf L (ALWAYS true with 2 panes), the result Split[source|L] is the same tree as inner-splitting L (just at the 0.22 outer ratio vs the 0.5 inner ratio) — a worse-ratio duplicate with zero added capability. Outer is only genuinely distinct when >=2 panels remain to be spanned (>=3 panes). The user's framing ("outer only when genuinely possible") is the correct, minimal, GENERAL fix and SUPERSEDES the earlier A/B/C options (disable outer entirely for terminals): outer keeps its real value (multi-column full-span at >=3 panes) and is suppressed only where it duplicates a split. Requested fix = widen `outer_dock_is_redundant` to also return true when `remove_leaf(source)` leaves a single leaf (equivalently: total leaves <= 2); the wiring already threads this predicate through `resolve_drop_checked` (same-window preview + release both consume it), so sprag code change is 0 and preview==result holds by construction. R138.decision_summary: Round 138: give an AI PEER a first-class agent surface — sprag-mcp, an MCP stdio server letting a model running INSIDE a sprag pane read and drive its SIBLING panes as data (list_panes / read_pane / write_pane / send_keys). It is a pure CLIENT of the existing always-on host wire (the R100-R104 socket + R115's HostConn), so it adds NO host surface and no new authority: everything it does an operator could already do over the socket — the round's value is making that reachable from a model's tool-call vocabulary instead of a hand-rolled JSON-RPC script. Installed to ~/.cargo/bin, registered user-scope as `sprag`. This is the north star's scene-as-data / RPC-as-primary-path contract paying out at PRODUCT level: the terminal is not merely observable by an agent, it is drivable by one. Shipped alongside an unrelated input fix found by dogfooding it: the named "Space" key never reached the PTY because the key router matched only single-char keys while "Space" is a NAMED key in pinion's W3C vocabulary — so a space typed mid-IME-composition was swallowed silently. Both sprag-side; no pinion gap.

No host-side change: it speaks the same wire the GUI and an operator speak, so it introduces no second control plane and no new authority.
crates/sprag-input: the named "Space" key now encodes to the PTY. The router matched single-char keys only, so pinion's W3C named key "Space" (as delivered mid-IME-composition) was dropped silently.

R139.decision_summary: Round 139: mouse-drag TEXT SELECTION with copy + paste — the first pointer gesture sprag owns end-to-end inside a pane (previous pointer work was pinion's dock/splitter). Press-drag-release over a pane's grid selects a cell range, release copies it, and paste writes to the focused pane's PTY via the existing `text` action (the IME-commit path, not the key encoder — a paste is literal UTF-8, never a keystroke). Clipboard access is pinion's `use_app_clipboard` (arboard behind pinion's platform seam: X11 PRIMARY/CLIPBOARD + Wayland + mac + Win), so sprag adds no platform code and "pixels/platform are pinion's" stays intact. Selection state is CLIENT state by design: what is highlighted is a view concern, not session state, so it never approaches the host — the same seam the layout arc draws in the other direction (WHICH panes are tiled IS session state; what is selected is not).
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-gui: mouse press/drag/release over a pane's grid selects a cell range; release copies the selected text via pinion's `use_app_clipboard`; paste writes literal UTF-8 into the focused pane's PTY through the existing `text` wire action.

Selection lives in client state only — the host is never told, because a highlight is a view fact, not session state (the deliberate mirror of the layout seam, where WHICH panes are tiled is the host's).
Paste deliberately routes through the `text` action (literal UTF-8, the IME-commit path), NOT the R2.6 key encoder: a paste is not a keystroke and must not be re-encoded as one.

R140.decision_summary: Round 140: right-click CONTEXT MENU (Copy / Paste / Select all) over a pane — the discoverable surface for R139's clipboard verbs. One `ContextMenuExternal` at a CONSTANT tag rather than one per pane: pinion R689 preserves a live external's open state across the per-frame external rebuild by tag, so a constant tag is what keeps the menu from closing every time the external set is reconciled. `apply_secondary_click` opens it; item activation arrives as the menu's `"command"` intent and is handled in the reducer BEFORE the dock-panel tag routing (a menu command is not a panel tag, so the panel routing below would drop it). Two pinion-shaped lessons landed here and are worth keeping: a menu click BLURS focus, so the acting pane must be captured when the menu OPENS rather than read at activation time (fixed properly in R141); and an empty flex child collapses to h=0, so the dismiss barrier must be a full-cover scrim rather than a sibling.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-gui/src/ctxmenu.rs: a right-click context menu with Copy / Paste / Select all, registered as ONE `ContextMenuExternal` at a constant tag (pinion R689 preserves its live open state across the per-frame external rebuild — a per-pane tag would close the menu on every reconcile).
Reducer: `ctxmenu::handle_command` runs FIRST in `TerminalViewer::update` and returns early — a menu `"command"` intent is not a dock-panel tag, so the panel routing below would silently drop it.
Dismiss barrier is a full-cover scrim: an empty flex child collapses to height 0, so a sibling-shaped barrier catches nothing.

R141.decision_summary: Round 141: FIX — the context menu's Paste / Select-all acted on the wrong pane. R140 read the focused pane at ACTIVATION time, but opening the menu BLURS the pane that was right-clicked, so by the time the user picked an item the "focused pane" was no longer the one they had aimed at. Fixed at the root: snapshot the acting pane when the menu OPENS and carry it in the menu's own state, rather than re-deriving focus at activation. The general shape is worth naming — a menu's action belongs to the moment of INVOCATION, not the moment of activation, because the act of opening a menu is itself a focus event. Re-deriving ambient state at activation time is the bug; capturing intent at invocation is the fix.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-gui/src/ctxmenu.rs: the acting pane is captured when the menu OPENS (carried in the menu state) instead of being re-read from focus when an item is activated — opening the menu blurs the right-clicked pane, so activation-time focus names the wrong pane.

R142.decision_summary: Round 142: the FOCUS INDICATOR became a dim scrim over the INACTIVE panes, replacing the abandoned thin-bar accent. Reasoning: a terminal is mostly text, and a 1-2px accent on a pane border is easy to lose against shell output — whereas dimming everything that is NOT focused reads instantly and needs no colour vocabulary the user must learn. It also degrades correctly on a single pane (nothing to dim = no chrome at all), which the accent bar did not. Implementation is a full-cover scrim per unfocused pane composed in the view; focus itself is read from pinion's `focus_state::focused()` (the R132 / PINION-PR53 consumer), so sprag keeps ONE focus source and does not maintain a parallel notion of which pane is active.

Focus is read from pinion's `focus_state::focused()` (the R132 / PINION-PR53 consumer) — one focus SSOT, no parallel active-pane state in sprag.

R144.decision_summary: Round 144: OPEN THE DETACH/REATTACH ARC — increment A: the host grows the session/window tree above its pane pool (`SessionRegistry -> Session(named, the attach unit) -> Window(named, the layout unit) -> Workspace(pane pool) -> Pane(PTY)`). WHY the arc: tmux's core value is that state outlives the client, and sprag was only half-there — the host already survives stdin EOF and an attach mode exists, but (1) a spawned host dies with its GUI, (2) there is no named/discoverable session, and (3) THE CRUX: the split LAYOUT lives in the GUI while the host's Workspace is a flat Vec<Pane>, so a naive reattach restores the pane SET but LOSES the arrangement. North star: a durable SERVER owns the state tree and clients are thin projections; the LOGICAL layout tree is host DATA while the pinion Scene/pixels stay client-composed (this preserves "pixels are pinion's" — the host serves data, clients project it). Rejected "session = one host process": it loses layout on reattach, shatters the AI-queryable single surface into N sockets, and windows/tabs would force the tree in later anyway. KEY OWNERSHIP CALL (minimal blast radius): `Arc<Mutex<Workspace>>` STAYS the currency for scene assembly, WorkspaceExternal, PluginsExternal and all of sprag-plugin — a plugin operates on a WORKSPACE, not a session tree (Interface Segregation) — so the hierarchy sits ABOVE and `Host::workspace()` returns the CURRENT window's Arc per call; scene+externals rebuild per request, so window switching (increment D) will need no re-plumbing.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-terminal/src/registry.rs: NEW module — Session / Window / SessionRegistry, the tree above the pane pool. Exported from lib.rs.

GLOBAL PaneId (load-bearing): Workspace.next_id is now Arc<AtomicU64>; SessionRegistry::new seeds the boot window via the new Workspace::with_id_source, so every window shares ONE counter → ids are unique across the WHOLE registry, monotonic, never reused. Public Workspace::spawn* API UNCHANGED (it self-mints), so the plugin layer gets globally-unique ids with zero registry coupling. The mint happens AFTER a successful spawn (a failed spawn consumes no id). The registry does NOT store the counter — it lives with the workspaces, its SSOT.

Host { registry: Arc<Mutex<SessionRegistry>> }; Host::workspace() / HostState::workspace() return the CURRENT window's Arc<Mutex<Workspace>> (cloned per call). workspace_scene / externals signatures UNCHANGED.
Lock discipline: the registry lock is released BEFORE the workspace lock (clone the Arc out) — sequential, never nested.

Windows/tabs UX deferral is SAFE and deliberate: the LAYER went in at A (not deferrable — B attaches the layout under Window, so A-before-B is invariant); the UX (2nd window, switching, tab strip, break/join-pane) is purely additive later. The per-pane wire path needs NO session/window dimension (global PaneId), so D adds optional params + actions = backward-compatible, never a breaking migration. A therefore changed the wire by NOTHING.

NEXT = B (lift the logical layout tree into Window) — the crux. Then C (daemon lifetime), D (detach/reattach UX + CLI), E (adversarial review).

R145.decision_summary: Round 145: increment B1 — Window owns a PINION-FREE logical LayoutTree. New `sprag-terminal::layout`: LayoutTree / LayoutNode{Leaf(PaneId) | Split{id,dir,ratio,first,second}} / SplitDir / SplitId, leaves keyed by GLOBAL PaneId (never a GUI tile index — slots are the client's SlotView concern, per R121). sprag-terminal must never depend on pinion, and nothing here has a rect. KEY DESIGN CALL — RECONCILE, DON'T CO-MUTATE: pane lifecycle runs through Workspace DIRECTLY (externals + the whole plugin layer hold Arc<Mutex<Workspace>> and spawn/close without ever seeing a Window), so the layout can NEVER be the membership authority — it would drift the instant a plugin spawned. It is an ARRANGEMENT that self-heals via reconcile(&[PaneId]): a gone pane's leaf collapses into its sibling, a new pane is appended right-nested. This preserves A's ownership decision exactly. `reconcile` is PURE (takes the id list, holds no lock) so a caller reads panes under the WORKSPACE lock then reconciles under the REGISTRY lock — never nested.
