R213.decision_summary: R213 = pin bump c237da6e -> 89f39fbd (pinion R1463-R1470), taken because R1469 delivers PINION-PR48, the last upstream item sprag had open - filed 2026-07-09 and re-verified still open only five days ago at R210. Zero break sites across the whole delta: pinion added serve_with_exposure and an Exposure enum while keeping serve, set_enabled and is_enabled, so the bump alone compiled untouched. SCE step 3 was a no-op, CHECKED rather than assumed: pinion at 89f39fbd pins 201783c4, the rev sprag already had. sprag's consumption is one call - mount now declares Exposure::from_serving(boot_enabled(opts)) TO the bind instead of serving first and withdrawing after. THE FINDING IS ABOUT WHAT COULD NOT BE PROVEN. The old shape's hazard was real and upstream states it plainly: a client landing between serve and the withdraw is accepted WHILE SERVING, and withdrawing deliberately leaves in-flight connections alone, so it stays served for its whole session by an endpoint the operator asked to be withdrawn. But racing a client against the bind could not witness that window from sprag's side - 30 trials refused 30/30 with the old post-bind withdraw and 30/30 with the new declared bind. That number only means something because the harness was proven able to see the difference: the same race against a boot-SERVING endpoint reports 30/30 SERVED. So what this bought is correctness BY CONSTRUCTION plus a call site that says what it means, not a reproduced bug fixed, and the code comment says exactly that so no future round goes hunting for a failing case that does not exist. The other seven rounds need no sprag code: R1463/R1464 (a focus request reaches every painted window, and the enumeration is now reported), R1465 (the mirror an agent reads settles like its paint - sprag's scene/snapshot path benefits passively), R1467/R1468 (chrome and viewport geometry), R1470 (a paint assertion no longer opens an audio device).
changes_bullets: Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock: all nine pinion-* revs c237da6e -> 89f39fbd; the SCE block stays 201783c4, matching pinion@89f39fbd's own workspace pin.

sprag-rpc mount(): UnixSocketTransport::serve_with_exposure with Exposure::from_serving(boot_enabled(opts)), replacing serve followed by control.set_enabled. The doc records both the hazard the old shape carried and the honest fact that sprag cannot externally witness it.
docs §5: a correcting caveat appended - the UPSTREAM OPEN line for PINION-PR48 is superseded, since the store is append-only and the stale line stays readable beside its correction.
verification_bullets: Consumption measured, and its LIMIT measured too: boot-withdrawn refused 30/30 both before and after the change, on a harness whose detector was proven by a boot-serving run reporting 30/30 SERVED. No revert-proof exists for the window itself and none is claimed.
Live headless smoke 63 passed / 0 failed, three runs identical - the same 63/0 as the previous pin, so eight upstream rounds moved nothing sprag observes.
Gates GREEN: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, the rustdoc private-items gate, workspace tests 1112 passed / 0 failed (unmoved by the bump).

R214.decision_summary: R214 = the owner rejected the evidence R213 rested on - "grep and read do not prove it, a test does" - and testing overturned two of its claims. R213 said the other seven pinion rounds needed no sprag consumption, and it said so from READING commit subjects. Querying scene/frame_timings live instead showed two new blocks sprag was ignoring: mirror{scenes_total,passes_total,shape_misses_total,unsettled_total} from R1465 and focus{derivations_total,retries_total} from R1464. So R1465's "sprag benefits passively" was not a passive benefit at all, it was an unread instrument, and the claim that nothing needed consuming was simply wrong. Two smoke checks now read them. The mirror one matters most for sprag specifically: scene/snapshot is how the CLI, the MCP surface and the smoke itself see anything, so an unsettled mirror is not cosmetic here, it is every assertion in the smoke reading a scene the client had not finished deriving - measured 52 scenes stored, 0 unsettled. The focus one turns the number R1462's round dug out with a temporary eprintln into a standing check, asserted as PRESENCE rather than a budget because the R1462 failure mode was a leg that made no request at all. Both are ordered late in the run so neither can pass vacuously, and scenes_total is checked BEFORE unsettled_total because zero-unsettled is trivially true when no mirror was ever stored. Separately, R213's "SCE unchanged, checked" rested on grepping pinion's Cargo.toml, which only re-states what was typed; the resolved LOCKFILE is the honest witness, since it is the lock and not the manifest that decides how many copies get linked. Three tests now assert one pinion rev, one SCE rev, and full-length shas.

R215.decision_summary: R215 = the carry-forward R214 left - mirror.shape_misses_total and produce.* are still unread - closed by measuring, and measuring killed two hypotheses I held before writing a line. First: I expected scene/snapshot from:state to run the RPC scene producer, since upstream says only from:paint is served from the committed frame. It does not; both from-values read a STORED scene, and across six calls each the producer stayed at zero. Second: I expected scene/layout {width,height} to be the clean read-only producer driver, because a hypothetical viewport cannot be answered from a stored scene. It measured zero across six calls too, so it would have proved nothing. The only driver that actually re-derives is PATH RESOLUTION - scene/click {path} - at exactly +1 per call, and that is what makes the zero a measurement instead of a dead counter. The finding for sprag is that its whole agent surface reads for free: the CLI, the sprag-mcp tools an AI in a pane drives its siblings with, and every assertion in the smoke go through scene/snapshot, and none of them costs a view+layout settle. The mirror half is the other consumer-honoured bound. A shape miss is a LayoutCache miss at 18.5us against a 118ns hit, and upstream says plainly that a binding which ignores the bound still measures every row and nothing notices - this is what notices. Measured flat at 76 while four mirrors were genuinely stored, and moving +2 to +4 the moment novel text is written, so sprag re-shapes nothing it has already shaped. The miss is accounted SYNCHRONOUSLY in the dispatch, so neither check contains a sleep, a wait or any timing at all. What the checks do NOT establish is stated in the code: the detector writes a field, and a field is chrome, so the terminal cells are unproven either way.

R216.decision_summary: R216: give the last unread frame_timings producer a reader, and answer the question R215 could not. `last.shape_misses` is the PER-FRAME half of pinion's shaping instrument; `mirror.*` and `produce.*` got readers at R215 but the frame's own count did not, and R215's carry-forward recorded that what its green tick demonstrably priced was sprag's CHROME, leaving "a terminal's biggest text surface is its cells" an untested assumption. The decision was to answer it by MEASUREMENT rather than to reason from the grid's shape. Two facts were measured before any check was written, and the first one dictated the whole design: a mutating scene RPC stores its mirror SYNCHRONOUSLY in the dispatch, and that store walks the same text and warms the same LayoutCache -- so text written over the scene socket is already shaped by the time a frame paints it and the frame reports zero. Every RPC-driven driver therefore produces a green tick that prices the mirror, not the paint. The driver has to reach the DAEMON instead and let the client find out on its own poll, which is why this one check drives the `sprag` CLI and a second connection to the host socket while every other check in the file drives the client's scene. The claim landed: novel terminal OUTPUT reaches the painted grid across twelve independent frames without handing pinion's shaper a single run, while one novel window name costs 2. What the claim does NOT say is that the cells are free -- sprag paints its grid from the rows the host serialises rather than from text nodes pinion lays out, so this instrument cannot see whatever that path costs; it says terminal output does not scale the cost pinion R1454 measured at 18.5us a miss against a 118ns hit.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-gui/src/bin/sprag-smoke.rs: new live check `check_terminal_output_never_reaches_the_shaper` -- the reader for `last.shape_misses`, the last frame_timings producer with none. Detector before claim, as at R215, but the detector is a HOST-driven window rename (novel chrome text over the CLI) rather than a scene write, because a scene write pre-warms the paint and would make the claim vacuous.

Harness: `Painted::rows` + `subtree_rows` give the smoke its first ability to read what a terminal pane is SHOWING (the grid's serialised rows, not text nodes); `Smoke::pane_rows`, `Smoke::frame_count`, `Smoke::cli` (the `sprag` CLI against this run's daemon) and `Smoke::daemon` (a second connection to the host socket, the only place a pane's input external lives) are the new ingresses; `daemon_panes` discovers pane ids from the daemon's own scene instead of guessing a mapping from tile indices.

`FrameWatch` samples every frame across a change and reports `contiguous`: a frame number that jumps means one was painted and never read, so a claim quantified over "every frame" refuses to cover a frame it does not have. Misses stay `Option`, so an absent field can never read as a zero. Module docs corrected to `cargo build -p sprag-gui -p sprag-host`, since the smoke now spawns and drives three binaries.
verification_bullets: Live smoke 78 passed / 0 failed, eight runs across the round (was 72). Every run: detector frame reports Some(2), the twelve claim frames report Some(0), contiguous true, daemon [5] / painted [0].

MEASURED BEFORE WRITING, and both measurements changed the design: novel text written over `scene/intervene` moved `mirror.shape_misses_total` by +4 while every frame that painted it reported `last.shape_misses` 0 -- the mirror store pre-warms the paint, so an RPC-driven check would have priced the wrong half. The daemon-driven path moved the frame counter and left the mirror counter still, which is the inverse and is what makes the claim about the paint.

NON-VACUITY IS ON THE WIRE, not inferred: the novel line is read back out of `scene/snapshot from: paint` as a painted grid ROW before the frame counts are judged, so "shaped nothing" cannot be true of a pane that never printed.

REVERT-PROVED BY TWO INDUCED FAULTS. (1) Aim the same watcher at chrome -- twelve CLI renames instead of twelve pane writes -- and exactly the claim line fails, 12/12 frames reporting Some(2), with every detector and non-vacuity guard still green; that also proves the sampler catches a per-frame miss on every one of twelve consecutive frames. (2) Misspell the field and BOTH the detector and the claim fail with None, never a silent pass.

What the grid path itself costs is unmeasured and no counter on this wire can see it -- sprag serialises rows and paints them, so pricing that is a sprag-side instrument nobody has built.

The claim covers the frames the sampler SAW. `contiguous` makes a missed frame fail the check rather than hide, and eight runs missed none at ~4fps under lavapipe, but a client painting far faster than the poll would fail this check rather than lie -- the honest failure mode, and the one to remember if it ever goes red on faster hardware.
Every frame_timings producer now has a reader. The next unread instrument, if one is wanted, has to come from a new pinion round rather than from this block.

R217.decision_summary: R217: price sprag's OWN grid path, the half R216 left unmeasurable. R216 proved terminal output never reaches pinion's shaper, which is true and is only half an answer: sprag does not paint its cells through pinion's text path at all -- it projects a whole GridBuffer per served frame -- so pinion's instrument being idle says nothing about what sprag pays. Nothing outside the process could see that cost, so this round built the meter. `sprag_grid::work` counts projections and cells at the ONE site that does the work, so the cost cannot be paid without being counted, and the host serves it at the mux `grid_work` slot -- data a peer asks for, the same scene-as-data form the rest of the surface takes, and the only shape a live check could revert-prove. Counts and not timings, deliberately: the round that repaid the emulator's throughput debt found wall-clock drifting more than 20% run to run and counted allocations instead. WHAT THE METER FOUND IS NOT WHAT THE QUESTION EXPECTED. The projection is not driven by output; it is driven by REQUESTS. Any call on the daemon's socket -- measured with `scene/revision`, which mutates nothing and merely reports a number -- costs a full re-projection of EVERY pane's entire grid. Steady state, three panes: an idle two-second window costs one pane set, twenty spaced reads cost twenty-one. The same twenty reads driven at the CLIENT's socket cost nothing, which pins it to the daemon hop rather than to polling in general, and that matters for sprag specifically because the sprag-mcp tools an AI in a pane drives its siblings with talk to exactly this socket. The cost is `workspace_scene` rebuilding the whole pane tree to answer any request. This round measures; whether the fix is a damage-driven fetch, a cache keyed on the row generations the host already sends, or nothing at all, is a decision this number is the input to.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-grid: `GridWork` + `work()` + a private `meter()` called from `project` and from `project_scrolled`'s non-delegating tail -- metered at the work site so no caller can pay without counting, and metered AFTER the early returns so the commonest call in the system is not double-counted. Two integration tests in a binary of their own, because the counters are process-wide and a delta taken in the parallel unit harness would be measuring whichever tests were in flight.

crates/sprag-host: `GRID_WORK_SLOT` on the mux control external (`{projections_total, cells_total}`), registry-wide and unscoped, since the counters are process-wide and scoping them would name a session for work every session shares.

crates/sprag-gui/src/bin/sprag-smoke.rs: `check_the_host_projects_panes_in_whole_sets` reads it live. Splits until the pane set is ASYMMETRIC, because two equal panes make "both projected once" and "one projected twice" the same number; then prices eight reads of a number and attributes the result by divisibility. Smoke 78 -> 86, workspace 1115 -> 1117.
verification_bullets: Live smoke 86 passed / 0 failed, five runs, byte-identical every run: 8 reads -> 27 projections / 11322 cells = 9 whole sets of the 1258-cell pane set, and NOT a multiple of the named pane's 646.

THE ATTRIBUTION IS ARITHMETIC, not assertion. Every projection adds one pane's whole area, so a host that re-projected only the pane a request concerned would leave a total that is a multiple of THAT pane's area and never of the set's. Measured, it is the exact opposite. The check asserts the set is asymmetric enough for that argument to hold rather than assuming a layout, and asserts the geometry did not move under the measurement.

ISOLATED IN STEADY STATE, three panes, two-second windows: no calls +3 projections; 20 `grid_work` queries +63; 20 `scene/revision` calls +63 (identical, so it is not the slot but the hop); 20 GUI-socket snapshots +3 (no perturbation at all).

REVERT-PROVED BY A SYSTEM FAULT, not an arithmetic one: skip the named pane in `workspace_scene` when three or more are open, and EXACTLY the two claim lines fail (5508 cells = 9 x the two silent panes' 612) while attribution, settle, geometry and non-vacuity all stay green.
The meter itself is revert-proved: move the count to the top of `project_scrolled` and the delegation test fails 2 vs 1, while the plain-projection test stays green.

TWO WRONG READINGS WERE CAUGHT BY MEASURING. A first probe using sleeps reported ~1 set per 1.5s idle and was mistaken for the whole story; polling the meter at 10Hz then showed one set per sample, which looked like the client's fetch fan-out. Inducing a single-pane fan-out in the CLIENT changed the number not at all -- which is what moved the cost to the daemon's request path.
Gates green: fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, rustdoc --document-private-items, workspace 1117 tests.
carry_forward_bullets: The instrument PERTURBS what it measures: reading the meter is itself a request, so it costs a pane set of its own. Harmless for this claim precisely because the perturbation has the same shape as the claim -- a whole set -- so it inflates the count without ever breaking the divisibility the verdict rests on. Any future reader has to keep that property or lose the argument.

NOT MEASURED: what a projection costs in TIME or in allocations. This meter counts cells and projections, which is what makes it reproducible; converting that into a budget needs a second instrument and a machine nobody else is using.

NOT DECIDED: whether any of this should change. A damage-driven fetch, or a cache keyed on the per-row generations the host already puts on the wire, are the obvious shapes, and both are a separate round with their own measurement.

The post-split churn is the one stretch whose projections are not whole sets -- panes are resizing, so a buffer built mid-resize belongs to an area no pane has any more. The check waits it out on the client's revision; anything else measuring this path has to as well.

R218.decision_summary: R218: decide what R217 measured, and build the first lever. R217 found that ANY call on the daemon's socket re-projects every pane's entire grid and deliberately decided nothing. Reading the live code named the mechanism R217 could only infer arithmetically: `handle_scoped` assembles the whole scene BEFORE it looks at `request.method`, so `scene/revision` -- one integer, no node walked -- pays a full projection per pane exactly as a snapshot does. THE DECISIVE FACT IS THAT ONLY ONE METHOD CAN READ THOSE CELLS. pinion's `snapshot` REQUIRES an empty scene path, so `scene/snapshot` reads the whole tree and cannot be narrowed; `scene/query` and `scene/invoke` resolve to an External (`NoExternalAtPath`) and can never reach a TextGrid; `scene/revision` and `scene/waitFor` never walk the scene at all. One of five. And the discriminator is the METHOD STRING this layer already holds, not a path prefix -- so sprag does not re-implement, or guess at, pinion's path resolution, which is the same refusal `handle_parsed` makes about a malformed scope. `PaneCells` + `pane_cells_for` gate the assembly on that; an unrecognised method PROJECTS, because the cheap answer is the one that can be silently wrong. The client's poll wake drops from N^2+N projections to N, and every surviving projection produces the reply it was asked for. THE ROUND ALSO REJECTS one of R217's two candidate shapes: a host-side cache keyed on row generations is strictly worse than fixing the client's fan-out, because after this gate every projection answers a distinct question, a hit still owes pinion an owned buffer, and its key needs the same axis matrix a damage-driven fetch does -- but where that fails as a visibly frozen pane, a stale cache serves wrong cells that look right. NO UPSTREAM ITEM: lazily-materialised cells in pinion's TextGridNode was the obvious ask, and the one method that reads them needs all of them, so laziness would buy nothing this does not.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-host/src/lib.rs: `PaneCells{Projected,Omitted}` threaded through `workspace_scene` -> `pane_container`. Omitted keeps the tree's exact SHAPE -- the pane still carries its tagged TextGrid child, holding an empty 0x0 buffer -- so the only observable difference between the modes is cell content, which is what makes the equivalence guard a sharp instrument rather than a shape comparison. It also takes no screen lock: the input External is built from the pane's handle alone.

crates/sprag-host/src/rpc.rs: `pane_cells_for(method)` beside SUPPORTED_METHODS, because it is a statement about the method table; `handle_scoped` applies it at ONE site and `handle_scoped_with_cells` is the seam a test drives both ways. The malformed-request path assembles Omitted -- a reply about the envelope reads no node. `_ => Projected` is load-bearing: a method added later is merely slow, never silently served empty cells.

crates/sprag-host/tests/grid_cost.rs (new) + the smoke's check re-pointed from asserting the defect to asserting its absence, with a `scene/snapshot` positive control that keeps R217's divisibility argument alive. Workspace 1117 -> 1120; smoke stays 86.
verification_bullets: THE CLAIM, in-process and exact: 8 `scene/revision` reads over three panes move the meter 24 -> 0 projections; 8 `cells.0` queries cost 8 projections (one per reply) and exactly pane 0's area, not the set's; a `scene/snapshot` still costs 3 projections / one whole pane set.
THE SAME CLAIM LIVE, over a real socket with the real client attached: 8 reads -> 0 projections / 0 cells (was 36 / 15096). Smoke 86 passed / 0 failed, five runs.

REVERT-PROVED IN FOUR DIRECTIONS. Forced Projected: the count claims fail at 24 vs 0 -- the pre-gate number exactly -- and live at 36 projections, while the equivalence guard stays green. Forced Omitted: the snapshot non-vacuity fails 0 vs 3, the classification test fails, and the tightened snapshot test fails. No single fault passes both sides.

THE EQUIVALENCE GUARD is the safety half: every method x a representative path answers BYTE-IDENTICALLY under either policy, except `scene/snapshot`, which must DIFFER. If a future pinion ever lets a query reach a TextGrid, that fails at the pin bump rather than in production. The pane's child is EOF'd first so the two dispatches of one request cannot differ because live output landed between them.

FOUND WHILE BUILDING, and it had already cost a real assertion: `scene/snapshot` serializes every External's introspect fields, and a pane's include `full_text`, so its screen text is in the response by a path unrelated to the grid. `serve_answers_scene_snapshot_with_live_screen` asserted `result.contains("hi")` and therefore PASSED with the cells removed entirely. Tightened to read `grid_rows` structurally; it now fails under a forced-Omitted fault, and before the tightening it did not.

AN R217 BOUND IS GONE: the instrument no longer perturbs what it measures. Reading the meter is a `scene/query`, which after the gate projects nothing, so the numbers are exact instead of exact-modulo-a-pane-set. The reverted run shows the old perturbation plainly -- the snapshot control measured two sets, one for the snapshot and one for the meter read that priced it.
Gates green: fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, rustdoc --document-private-items, workspace 1120 tests.
carry_forward_bullets: L2, NOT BUILT: `sprag_grid::term_cell` does `cluster.to_string()`, so every cell allocates a String even though pinion's TermCell.cluster is a `Cow<'static, str>` whose own `blank()` borrows a static. Borrowing for blanks, wide trailers and single printable-ASCII clusters would make a projection -- and every CLONE of one -- near allocation-free. That matters past the daemon: the GUI's `WireHost::live_cells` deep-clones the mirrored buffer per pane per painted frame. Measure it by counting allocations, not wall-clock.

L3, NOT BUILT: the client still refetches ALL panes on every poll wake, so after this gate the remaining waste is the client's fan-out, not the host's. A per-pane projection epoch would gate it -- but `Emulator::generation` is deliberately NOT bumped by things that carry no cells, including a bare CURSOR MOVE, which the projection does carry. Adopting it as-is would freeze a moved cursor. The deliverable there is the axis matrix (print, cursor, DECTCEM, DECSCUSR, OSC 4/11/12, alt-screen, resize, scrollback), not the plumbing.
REJECTED, with reasons, so it is not re-proposed: a host-side projection cache keyed on the row generations already on the wire. Same axis matrix as L3, strictly worse failure mode.
STILL TRUE FROM R217: what a projection costs in TIME or allocations is unmeasured; this meter counts cells. L2's allocation count would be the first instrument to answer half of it.
The design record for all three levers lives in claudedocs/DESIGN-R218-GRID-COST-RESPONSE.md, which is gitignored -- so this entry is the durable half.

R219.decision_summary: R219: build R218's second lever -- a projected cell BORROWS its cluster instead of allocating one. The producer's cluster is a SmolStr (inline, O(1) to clone) but pinion's TermCell.cluster is a Cow<'static, str>, and the obvious to_string() always lands in the Owned arm. That is ONE HEAP ALLOCATION PER CELL, on a path that runs per pane per served frame, charging the same price for a blank space as for an emoji -- and a terminal's cells are overwhelmingly blanks and printable ASCII. Naming that range as one 'static literal and indexing it removes essentially all of it: 0x20..=0x7e in code-point order, plus the empty string a wide cluster's trailer carries. ONE literal rather than a table of 95, because a table is 95 chances to mistype an entry while a contiguous run's indexing is verified exhaustively by a single loop. Anything outside the range -- a wide CJK glyph, an emoji, a combining cluster, DEL, a C0 control -- still owns its string, which is the honest boundary: this borrows what it can NAME, not what it hopes. The value is byte-for-byte what to_string() produced, since Cow compares, hashes and serializes by CONTENT, so no consumer can observe which arm a cell took. THE HALF THAT REACHES PAST THIS CRATE IS THE CLONE: a borrowed Cow clones by copying a pointer, and a display client does not project at all -- it CLONES a buffer it already holds, per pane, per painted frame (WireHost::live_cells). So a lever designed against the daemon's projection pays off hardest on the CLIENT's paint path, which R218's design named but could not price. Unlike R218's gate this changes no control flow and has no staleness surface: same value, different ownership, so there is nothing a future reader has to keep true.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-grid/src/lib.rs: PRINTABLE_ASCII (one 95-code-point 'static literal) + cluster(&str) -> Cow<'static, str>, called from term_cell and from preedit_cell so the IME overlay takes the same path. A control byte underflows the index and DEL runs off its end, so both fall through to the owned arm rather than borrowing a wrong glyph.

crates/sprag-grid/tests/allocs.rs (new): a counting global allocator in a binary of its own -- ONE test, because the allocator is binary-wide and a second test's count would be polluted by whatever the first was doing on another harness thread. Workspace 1120 -> 1124.

Three unit tests at the ARM rather than the cost: the static run indexes to itself at every one of its 95 positions, the borrow/own boundary is stated as a test rather than a comment, and a projected ASCII cell carries the borrow through.
verification_bullets: MEASURED, by counting allocations rather than wall-clock: a 40x24 ASCII projection 986 -> 26 allocations; the same screen at 160 cols 3866 -> 26. Twenty-six is two for the buffer's own vectors plus one per ROW, which is the claim.

THE CLAIM IS STATED AS AN EQUALITY, not a threshold: two screens of the same height and four times the cells must allocate the SAME number of times. That needs no tuned constant and fails loudly the moment a per-cell allocation returns -- the wide screen simply costs four times the narrow one.

THE CLONE, which is what a display client actually pays: 962 -> 2 allocations at 40 cols, 3842 -> 2 at 160. Revert-proved INDEPENDENTLY, with the projection assertions neutralised first, since they fail earlier under the same fault and would otherwise mask it.
REVERT-PROVED: restore cluster.to_string() and the projection equality fails 986 vs 3866, the clone equality fails 962 vs 3842, and the arm test fails at the first cell. Restored, all green.

NON-VACUITY / the boundary: a screen of wide CJK glyphs still allocates per cell and the test asserts it does -- without that, the equality above would read the same on a counter that had simply stopped.
Wall-clock was NOT used, deliberately: the round that repaid the emulator's throughput debt found it drifting more than 20% run to run on this machine even for an allocation-free control.
Gates green: fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, rustdoc --document-private-items, workspace 1124 tests, live smoke 86 passed / 0 failed over five runs.
carry_forward_bullets: L3 remains the only unbuilt lever of the R218 design, and the only one with a real failure surface: the client still refetches ALL panes on every poll wake. A per-pane projection epoch would gate it, but Emulator::generation is deliberately NOT bumped by changes that carry no cells -- including a bare CURSOR MOVE, which the projection DOES carry. Adopting it as-is freezes a moved cursor. The deliverable is the axis matrix (print, cursor, DECTCEM, DECSCUSR, OSC 4/11/12, alt-screen, resize, scrollback), not the plumbing.

NOT MEASURED: what any of this is worth in TIME. Two rounds have now priced this path in counts -- projections, cells, allocations -- precisely because counts are reproducible on a shared machine; converting them into a latency budget still needs an instrument nobody has built and a box nobody else is using.

The borrow covers printable ASCII only. A CJK-heavy or emoji-heavy workload still allocates per cell, and extending the table is NOT the answer, since an unbounded range cannot be named statically. If that workload ever matters, the shape to reach for is interning at the producer, not a longer literal here.

sprag-grid now has TWO permanent meters, tests/meter.rs and tests/allocs.rs. Both are integration binaries for the same reason -- process-wide state -- and anything else measuring either has to keep that.
R219.publishable_decision_summary: R219: build R218's second lever -- a projected cell BORROWS its cluster instead of allocating one. The producer's cluster is a SmolStr (inline, O(1) to clone) but pinion's TermCell.cluster is a Cow<'static, str>, and the obvious to_string() always lands in the Owned arm. That is ONE HEAP ALLOCATION PER CELL, on a path that runs per pane per served frame, charging the same price for a blank space as for an emoji -- and a terminal's cells are overwhelmingly blanks and printable ASCII. Naming that range as one 'static literal and indexing it removes essentially all of it: 0x20..=0x7e in code-point order, plus the empty string a wide cluster's trailer carries. ONE literal rather than a table of 95, because a table is 95 chances to mistype an entry while a contiguous run's indexing is verified exhaustively by a single loop. Anything outside the range -- a wide CJK glyph, an emoji, a combining cluster, DEL, a C0 control -- still owns its string, which is the honest boundary: this borrows what it can NAME, not what it hopes. The value is byte-for-byte what to_string() produced, since Cow compares, hashes and serializes by CONTENT, so no consumer can observe which arm a cell took. THE HALF THAT REACHES PAST THIS CRATE IS THE CLONE: a borrowed Cow clones by copying a pointer, and a display client does not project at all -- it CLONES a buffer it already holds, per pane, per painted frame (WireHost::live_cells). So a lever designed against the daemon's projection pays off hardest on the CLIENT's paint path, which R218's design named but could not price. Unlike R218's gate this changes no control flow and has no staleness surface: same value, different ownership, so there is nothing a future reader has to keep true.

R220.decision_summary: R220: build R218's last and riskiest lever -- a display client refetches only the panes whose cells would actually differ. After R218 the daemon projects nothing it does not return, so the remaining waste moved to the CLIENT, which refetched all N panes on every poll wake although a wake means only that SOMETHING in the session changed. The gate is a ProjectionToken the host puts on the pane list a client already reads every wake, so the arrangement costs ZERO extra requests. THE TOKEN CARRIES THE PROJECTION'S INPUTS RATHER THAN A SUMMARY OF THEM: the per-row damage stamps VERBATIM (not a maximum, not a hash), the cursor built by the projection's own project_cursor, the screen kind, the width and the history depth. Carrying the vector is the decision that makes this sound -- it is exact, it cannot collide, and it needs no monotonic accumulator maintained correctly somewhere else. The stamps are ALREADY load-bearing, since pinion's TextGrid re-rasterizes only rows whose stamp advanced, so the gate inherits an invariant the system must already satisfy instead of adding a second one beside it. The design named the cursor as the axis a naive generation counter would miss; building it found a SECOND: OSC 12 sets the cursor colour and the emulator documents it as deliberately damaging no cell, yet the projection carries that colour. Both are covered by taking the cursor from project_cursor itself, so the token and the projection cannot disagree about what a cursor is. ONLY ONE DIRECTION IS PROMISED AND ONLY ONE IS NEEDED: equal token implies equal frame is the safety property a skip may rely on; the converse is false (writing a character over an identical one stamps its row) and asserting it would be wrong. Every imprecision in the arrangement is arranged to cost a redundant fetch, never a stale pane.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-grid: ProjectionToken + projection_token(&Screen, &Palette), beside the projection whose inputs it names. It reuses project_cursor and screen_kind -- the projection's OWN functions -- so the two cannot drift apart. tests/token.rs is the axis matrix: 18 real VT drivers, each asserted twice.

crates/sprag-host/src/workspace.rs: the panes slot carries the token, read under the SAME workspace lock as the pane list so it describes the same moment as the rest of the entry. ADDITIVE -- its absence means fetch anyway, so an older daemon costs a redundant fetch and never a stale pane.

crates/sprag-gui/src/wire.rs: stale_panes() is the gate, PURE so the policy is tested without a socket; fetch_frames now takes ids; merge_panes stores the query's token ONLY beside a frame the wake actually fetched. Workspace 1124 -> 1130, smoke 86 -> 88.
verification_bullets: LIVE, over a real socket with the real client attached: driving output into ONE pane of three costs 1 projection / 646 cells -- exactly that pane's area. Revert-proved by disabling the gate: 6 projections / 2516 cells, which is two whole 1258-cell sets. Smoke 88 passed / 0 failed, five runs.
The live claim uses R217's DIVISIBILITY argument run the other way round: a multiple of the DRIVEN pane and NOT of the set. The same asymmetric split that proved the fan-out now proves its absence.

THE AXIS MATRIX asserts the implication over a battery rather than spot-checking fields, so a forgotten input shows up as a driver that left the token equal and the frame different, whatever the reason -- including reasons nobody enumerated.

EVERY TOKEN FIELD IS REVERT-PROVED BY ITS OWN AXIS, and finding those axes corrected the design twice. Neutralising the cursor fails on a bare cursor move. Neutralising the row generations fails on OSC 4. Neutralising `cols` fails only on a width resize ON THE ALTERNATE SCREEN, because the main-screen path REFLOWS and restamps every row -- the alt path copies stamps, leaving width the only thing that moved. Neutralising `scrollback_len` fails only on ED 3, which drops history and stamps no row.

THOSE LAST TWO FIELDS WERE UNPROVEN AT FIRST and the battery passed without them. Rather than delete them, the two axes that reach them were found and added -- and the second forced a correction to the property itself: the token guards the whole FRAME (cells plus PaneScrollFacts), not just the projection, because ED 3 changes the history depth a client's scrollbar reads while leaving every cell alone.

THE CLIENT-SIDE INVARIANT has its own pair of tests: a pane whose fetch was skipped or missed KEEPS the token its held frame was taken under, and only a pane that was actually refetched adopts the query's. Adopting it beside an older frame would make the next wake compare equal and skip again, forever -- the exact shape of a frozen pane.

They were re-verified against the pin during this round and all three hold, and R218's behaviour was independently confirmed by measurement anyway. The lesson is that a citation is only worth what the reader checked: name the rev and verify the path.

R221.decision_summary: R221: measure the thing three rounds refused to claim -- what this path costs in TIME -- and let the answer say whether the previous three were aimed at the right term. R217 through R220 priced the grid path in COUNTS (projections, cells, allocations) because a count is reproducible on a machine somebody else is also using, and every one of them closed by naming a latency budget as the instrument nobody had built. This is that instrument, and it is a TOOL rather than a test: a duration threshold on a shared box is a flake by construction, which is exactly why the guards in tests/ are counts and why a timing cannot join them. `sprag-latency` refuses to run without --release, and serves its request rows IN-PROCESS through `handle_request`, the same entry point the transport calls, so the numbers are the daemon's with the wire's excluded. THE ANSWER IS THAT ALL THREE LEVERS WERE AIMED AT HALF A PERCENT OF THE COST. A one-pane cells fetch -- the client's steady-state read, the unit R220 exists to skip -- costs about 4 ms, a quarter of a 60 Hz frame, and the projection that R218 gated and R219 made allocation-free is 0.47% to 0.64% of it. The reply is 570583 bytes for 1920 cells, 297 bytes per cell, because every cell carries its foreground and background as fully expanded RGBA objects; that figure is identical on every run, being a count rather than a time. Building the reply through a `serde_json::Value` DOM -- `to_value` in the pane external's cells arm -- costs 2.2 to 3.0 ms by itself, and encoding the same frame directly is 6.3x to 7.5x cheaper than the DOM plus its printing. So the grid work is not the cost centre and never was: the wire encoding is, and the largest correction available is the removal of an intermediate rather than any new algorithm. NONE OF THAT IS BUILT HERE, DELIBERATELY. The round was asked for a measurement, and the fix is a front with an upstream half that the standing rule says to report rather than work around. THE INSTRUMENT IS ALSO A RESULT, because it refuted two of its own hypotheses before it could be trusted: its first draft reported a subject at 0.02 us, which is BELOW this box's clock floor, and pinning to the fastest core -- the obvious answer to a hybrid P-core/E-core CPU -- made the run-to-run spread WORSE rather than better. What survived is a sharper rule than the one it was built for: a control cancels only the noise it shares, and only while it is steadier than its subject.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-host/src/bin/sprag-latency.rs (new): eleven subjects -- the projection, a clone whose clusters can be borrowed and one whose clusters must be owned, the projection token, the three separable halves of the reply encoding, and four real requests -- each reported as a minimum and a median over 101 timed spans, each span repeating the subject enough times to stand well clear of the clock's floor, and each preceded by its OWN measurement of a fixed 64 KiB copy so a row can be read as a ratio rather than as a microsecond only this box can produce.

It is a tool and not a test, and it refuses to run without --release, because a debug build is not the code that ships and a duration threshold in tests/ would be green on a quiet machine and red on a busy one. No library code is touched: the round adds a measurement and moves no behaviour, so workspace tests stay at 1130 and the live smoke stays at 88.

The estimator's bounds are printed at the point of use rather than kept in somebody's memory -- the clock floor, the repetition count for every row, the control's spread across the battery, and a closing statement that one run is not a measurement and that every conclusion drawn must clear that band by orders of magnitude.
verification_bullets: THE HEADLINE, over ten runs: a one-pane 80x24 cells fetch costs 3.9 to 5.4 ms in-process, 23% to 33% of a 60 Hz frame, while the projection inside it costs 21 to 29 us. The projection's SHARE of the request carrying it -- a ratio taken inside a single run, which is the only reproducible quantity here -- was 0.47% to 0.64% on every one of the ten.

THE SIZE IS THE REASON FOR THE TIME, and the size is exact: 570583 bytes for 1920 cells, identical on all ten runs, 297 bytes per cell, each carrying fg and bg as expanded RGBA objects. A byte count is a count, so unlike every duration in this round it repeats to the digit.

THE INTERMEDIATE IS SEPARABLE AND PRICED: building the reply's serde_json Value costs 2.2 to 3.0 ms, printing that DOM 0.50 to 0.65 ms, and encoding the same frame directly 0.41 to 0.50 ms -- a 6.3x to 7.5x penalty for the DOM, measured within each run so the machine's drift cannot manufacture it.

WHAT THE THREE LEVERS ARE WORTH IN TIME, and the ranking is not the one the counts implied: R220's fetch gate saves a whole fetch per unchanged pane, about 4 ms each, so 8 to 11 ms on a three-pane wake with one pane changed. R218's method gate saves the projections a non-cells request no longer runs, about 60 to 90 us. R219's borrow saves 14 to 21 us per pane per painted frame. Three orders of magnitude separate the first from the third.

THE INSTRUMENT REFUTED TWO OF ITS OWN HYPOTHESES AND BOTH ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN DROPPED. The first draft reported the projection token at 0.02 us, below this box's Instant floor -- the number was the clock's resolution wearing the subject's name, fixed by piloting each subject and repeating it inside the timed span. And pinning to the fastest P-core, the obvious response to a hybrid CPU, made the spread WORSE (85%), so core assignment is not what drives the drift.

A CONTROL CANCELS ONLY THE NOISE IT SHARES, AND ONLY WHILE IT IS STEADIER THAN ITS SUBJECT -- measured in both directions. The 64 KiB copy took nine of eleven rows from 26-50% cross-run spread down to 5-16%. Pairing the reply-building rows with an allocation-heavy control instead, on the reasoning that a denominator should share its subject's bottleneck and those rows are allocator-bound, made them worse: the DOM build went 16% to 53% and the cells fetch 30% to 68%, because dividing by a denominator noisier than the numerator adds variance.

Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, rustdoc --document-private-items with private-intra-doc-links denied (the new binary carries the same crate-root allow as the crate's other two), workspace 1130 tests passed / 0 failed, live GUI smoke 88 passed / 0 failed.
carry_forward_bullets: THE ENCODER IS THE FRONT THIS ROUND OPENS AND DOES NOT BUILD, and it has two independent halves. sprag's half: the cells frame puts pinion's GridBuffer on the wire through its derived Serialize, so one cell costs 297 bytes; a compact frame encoding -- the shape scene/snapshot already uses for the same data, 40706 bytes for THREE panes against 570605 for one -- needs no upstream change at all. pinion's half: at the pinned rev 89f39fbd, IntrospectValue is Null/Bool/Int/Float/Text(String)/Json(serde_json::Value), with no variant carrying already-encoded JSON, so any answer larger than a scalar MUST be materialised as a Value first. That is 2.2 to 3.0 ms of a 4 ms request, it is an upstream ask, and it is reported rather than worked around.

UNATTRIBUTED, and named as such: about 1.0 to 1.6 ms of the cells request is neither the projection nor either encoding half the tool can isolate. It is the dispatch's own envelope work. Calling it unaccounted rather than folding it into a neighbour is what keeps the split honest.

STILL NOT MEASURED: the socket. Every request row is served in-process, so a real client's wall clock adds a round trip nobody has priced. The GUI's paint path is unpriced too; the clone rows stand in for what it pays per pane per frame.

WHAT ANY NUMBER HERE IS WORTH IS TWO SIGNIFICANT FIGURES. Absolute minima move 26% to 50% between runs of the same binary, and no amount of sampling inside a run reduces that. The reproducible quantity is a RATIO taken inside one run, which is why every conclusion above is stated as a share or a multiple, and why the guards in tests/ remain counts.

R222.decision_summary: R222: build the sprag half of the encoder front R221 named and priced, and let the instrument say in one run what it was worth. R221 found that three rounds of grid-cost work had been aimed at half a percent of a cells fetch: the cost was the REPLY, 570536 bytes for 1920 cells, because a projected GridBuffer crossed the wire through pinion's derived Serialize and every cell spelled its foreground and background as fully expanded RGBA objects and its attributes as eight named booleans. Size is what the time was made of, since a serde_json Value DOM costs what its node count costs. THE CORRECTION IS NOT A FASTER ENCODER BUT ENCODING LESS, and the shape to encode in was already in the same daemon: scene/snapshot has always reported a terminal grid as line text plus style runs. A terminal cell varies along two axes that compress completely differently -- its cluster changes at almost every column of a line of text and repeats hundreds of times across a blank one, while its style changes a handful of times per screen and comes from a vocabulary of a few values per frame. So the two are encoded SEPARATELY by the same mechanism: each line carries two run lists tiling its columns exactly, and a style run names an entry in a frame-wide interned table rather than carrying a style. Folding the axes into one run key would have broken a run at every character and re-spelled the whole style per glyph. A run carries only its LENGTH and not its start column, because the runs tile the line exhaustively and a start is derivable; snapshot does carry start, and correctly, because its consumer addresses columns directly while this one is a decoder. THE SEAM IS ONE ATTRIBUTE: CellFrame's cells field takes serde(with), so the field is the same GridBuffer to every reader on both ends and nothing downstream knows the difference -- which is what keeps CellFrame the ONE definition of the frame's wire shape rather than adding a second address beside it. THE ENCODING COSTS, taken as ratios INSIDE each run since that is the only reproducible form a duration has on this box: building the reply's serde_json Value DOM is 30-35x cheaper, printing the cells alone 14-15x cheaper. Both are now measured by sprag-latency itself, which prices pinion's derived shape beside the run-length one in the same breath.

EXACTNESS IS A STRUCTURAL GUARD, NOT AN ENUMERATED ONE: the round-trip is asserted with GridBuffer's own PartialEq over a 24-driver VT battery, live and at three history offsets, so a cell field this codec has never heard of fails the moment the projection populates it. TermCell is non_exhaustive, so no exhaustive destructuring exists to catch it at compile time and this is the strongest guard the type allows.

THE SIZE CLAIM IS AN EQUALITY, not a tuned threshold: the same text on a 40-column and a 400-column screen produces the SAME run count and the same style count. Ten times the cells, not one more run. A per-cell term returning would simply make the wide screen cost more.

FOUR REVERT-PROOFS MEASURED. Dropping underline_color from the style fails the battery on the SGR-58 axis. THE FIFTH REVERT-PROOF REFUTED ITS OWN TEST FIRST. R223.decision_summary: R223: make the ops sprag already performs reachable from a shell, and design the client that would let those ops be reached from another machine. The debt register's H4 said six pane operations existed on the wire or as MCP tools with no CLI verb, and called it pure surface work. It was, and it is done: panes, split-window, kill-pane, resize-pane, send-keys and capture-pane now drive the same actions the GUI and the agent surface already drove, so a scriptable multiplexer is finally scriptable. THE PART WORTH RECORDING IS NOT THE VERBS BUT WHAT WRITING THEM PROVED FALSE. The register listed select-pane among the ops awaiting exposure, mapping it to the pane-input focus action. That action reports a DEC 1004 focus edge to a pane's child on behalf of a client whose own focus moved; it makes no pane current, and the daemon has no active-pane concept for it to make current. So select-pane is not unexposed, it is UNBUILT, and the register's mechanically-derived rival counts move against sprag by one. The lesson generalises past this item: those counts held because they were derived from the RIVALS' source, and the error was in the one column derived from a memory of sprag's OWN surface. Two flags are unbuilt in the same way and are refused by name rather than accepted and ignored, because a split-window -h that silently appends puts the pane somewhere the caller did not ask for. The round's second half is H1, the terminal client -- the gap that means you cannot ssh to a box and attach to a sprag session, which all three rivals can. It is DESIGNED AND NOT BUILT, deliberately, because the register calls it design-first and because the design's central measurement was wrong on its first pass in a way that would have shaped the whole front.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-host/src/bin/sprag.rs: six pane-subject verbs -- panes, split-window, kill-pane, resize-pane, send-keys, capture-pane -- over the SPAWN, CLOSE, RESIZE, KEY and TEXT actions and the panes and full_text slots that already served them. No daemon mechanism was added and none was needed; every one of these ops existed on the wire or as an MCP tool and simply could not be reached from a shell.

A rule where there had been two habits: a WINDOW command's -t SESSION stays REQUIRED, because a window lives in a session and there is no useful default for which session's window list was meant, while a PANE command's -t is OPTIONAL, because an unscoped request already has a scope -- the daemon's default session. That is what find and run already did; the six new verbs join them rather than inventing a third convention, and the rule is written down at the module head so the next verb does not have to guess.

The scope shaping that four call sites had each spelled for themselves is now one pair of functions, and the pane-id pre-flight that find and run had each open-coded is one function those two now call as well. Two of the new verbs address a pane's OWN external by path, where a wrong id is an unknown ADDRESS rather than a pane-level refusal, so the pre-flight is what makes their error about panes at all.
verification_bullets: SIX REVERT-PROOFS MEASURED, each by removing the mechanism and watching the named guard fail. Sending a key name through the text action instead of the key action leaves marker-oneEnter on the screen and fails the echo count. Sending literal text through the key action makes a multi-character token an unknown key and fails the first assertion. Making the direction flags a no-op fails the refusal test. Dropping the local zero check lets 0x30 reach the daemon, which refuses it with a message blaming the pane. Defaulting a missing dimension fails the both-dimensions test. Removing the pane pre-flight from capture-pane turns no pane 9999 into NoExternalAtPath -- a raw address error saying nothing about panes, which is exactly what the pre-flight exists to prevent and is now proven rather than asserted.

THE STRONGEST TEST IS ONE CHAIN THROUGH A REAL PTY: the boot pane runs cat, so send-keys -l types marker-one and the terminal echoes it ONCE while the line is unfinished, and capture-pane reads that back; then send-keys Enter completes cat's line-buffered read, cat writes the line back, and a SECOND copy appears. One fixture therefore separates the text language from the key language, which no single combined send could do.

BUILDING IT FALSIFIED THE REGISTER THAT ASKED FOR IT. The debt register listed select-pane as a wire action awaiting a CLI verb, mapped to the pane-input focus action. Read at the source, focus reports a DEC private mode 1004 focus EDGE to the child on behalf of a display client whose own focus moved; it makes no pane current. A grep over sprag-terminal and sprag-host for active_pane, current_pane and focused_pane finds nothing -- the daemon has no active-pane concept at all. So tmux commands sprag has drops 21 to 20, missing rises 71 to 72, and the verified itemized total 165 to 166. A select-pane built on focus would have sent a program a focus-in report while no client had focused it.

TWO FLAGS ARE UNBUILT RATHER THAN UNEXPOSED, and the CLI says so by name instead of accepting them: split-window -h and -v, and resize-pane's relative forms. sprag's spawn APPENDS a pane; the direction a pane splits in is a layout gesture a display client authors and installs, and there is no direction-taking split on the wire. Accepting the flag and ignoring it would put the pane somewhere the caller did not ask for, silently; authoring the tree in the CLI would put a second layout author beside the GUI's.

Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, rustdoc --document-private-items with private-intra-doc-links denied, workspace 1138 -> 1145 tests passed / 0 failed, live GUI pixel smoke 88 passed / 0 failed.
carry_forward_bullets: H1, THE TERMINAL CLIENT, IS DESIGNED AND NOT BUILT -- claudedocs/DESIGN-H1-TERMINAL-CLIENT.md, gitignored like every design doc here. The architecture question was whether the TUI reimplements the wire client or shares one, and the code already answers it: WireHost, the entire client half of topology B, names pinion_shell zero times and depends only on pinion-core, serde_json, base64 and the sprag crates. Sharing costs a MOVE of about 9400 lines into a GPU-free sprag-client crate; reimplementing would create a second client of a wire whose whole point is that there is one vocabulary.

THE MEASUREMENT BEHIND THAT DESIGN WAS WRONG ON ITS FIRST PASS AND THE CORRECTION IS THE MORE USEFUL FACT. Three of the five crates I treated as GPU markers carry no vello, wgpu or winit at all. Worse, one of the two real ones lies when asked in isolation: cargo tree -p pinion-runtime reports 16 GPU dependencies, while the same crate inside sprag-host's tree resolves to ZERO, because a standalone query activates default features and the workspace unifies them away. The honest question is never whether a crate pulls the GPU stack in isolation but what THIS workspace resolves for the crate under test -- and that number for the headless daemon is zero, which is the mechanical proof of the headless-host split the architecture has always claimed.

AND THE SECOND MEASUREMENT WOULD HAVE MISLED TOO, HAD IT BEEN THE MEMBERSHIP TEST. With the corrected markers, 19 of 25 GUI modules and 20241 lines name no GPU crate -- but most are WIDGETS emitting pinion scene nodes, useless to a TUI. Compiles-without-the-GPU and belongs-in-the-shared-crate are different questions, and only the second decides membership: the shared crate is the seven modules whose SUBJECT is the host relationship, not the display.

FOUR PIECES ARE GENUINELY NEW and everything else is a sprag-client call: a decoder from the local terminal's input bytes to the wire's W3C key vocabulary, a GridBuffer to termwiz Surface painter, a character-cell layouter over the same ratio tree the GUI reads in pixels, and the client's own event loop. The decode-then-re-encode is a correctness argument, not a purity one -- the host owns the pane's live input modes and the TUI's terminal is in different ones, so forwarding raw bytes would deliver the wrong encoding silently. termwiz supplies the first two and is already in the lock at the version sprag-vt uses, with input, terminal, render and surface all ungated, so the front needs no new third-party dependency.

THE FRONT INHERITS H4's FINDING AS A DEPENDENCY. A TUI user will expect prefix-% and prefix-quote, so slice 4 needs the split action the daemon does not have -- the same gap split-window -h refuses. And a third client makes R222's missing version handshake worse: a stale sprag-tui on a remote box against an updated daemon is exactly the skew nothing negotiates.

STILL OPEN, unchanged by this round: PINION-PR79 (IntrospectValue has no pre-encoded-JSON variant), the 142-261 us of a cells request that is neither the projection nor either encoding half, the unpriced socket, and the version handshake.

One fixture therefore separates the text language from the key language, which no single combined send could do.

BUILDING IT FALSIFIED THE REGISTER THAT ASKED FOR IT. The debt register listed select-pane as a wire action awaiting a CLI verb, mapped to the pane-input focus action. Read at the source, focus reports a DEC private mode 1004 focus EDGE to the child on behalf of a display client whose own focus moved; it makes no pane current. A grep over sprag-terminal and sprag-host for active_pane, current_pane and focused_pane finds nothing -- the daemon has no active-pane concept at all. So tmux commands sprag has drops 21 to 20, missing rises 71 to 72, and the verified itemized total 165 to 166. A select-pane built on focus would have sent a program a focus-in report while no client had focused it.

TWO FLAGS ARE UNBUILT RATHER THAN UNEXPOSED, and the CLI says so by name instead of accepting them: split-window -h and -v, and resize-pane's relative forms. sprag's spawn APPENDS a pane; the direction a pane splits in is a layout gesture a display client authors and installs, and there is no direction-taking split on the wire. Accepting the flag and ignoring it would put the pane somewhere the caller did not ask for, silently; authoring the tree in the CLI would put a second layout author beside the GUI's.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: H1, THE TERMINAL CLIENT, IS DESIGNED AND NOT BUILT -- claudedocs/DESIGN-H1-TERMINAL-CLIENT.md, gitignored like every design doc here. The architecture question was whether the TUI reimplements the wire client or shares one, and the code already answers it: WireHost, the entire client half of topology B, names pinion_shell zero times and depends only on pinion-core, serde_json, base64 and the sprag crates. Sharing costs a MOVE of about 9400 lines into a GPU-free sprag-client crate; reimplementing would create a second client of a wire whose whole point is that there is one vocabulary.

THE MEASUREMENT BEHIND THAT DESIGN WAS WRONG ON ITS FIRST PASS AND THE CORRECTION IS THE MORE USEFUL FACT. Three of the five crates I treated as GPU markers carry no vello, wgpu or winit at all. Worse, one of the two real ones lies when asked in isolation: cargo tree -p pinion-runtime reports 16 GPU dependencies, while the same crate inside sprag-host's tree resolves to ZERO, because a standalone query activates default features and the workspace unifies them away. The honest question is never whether a crate pulls the GPU stack in isolation but what THIS workspace resolves for the crate under test -- and that number for the headless daemon is zero, which is the mechanical proof of the headless-host split the architecture has always claimed.

AND THE SECOND MEASUREMENT WOULD HAVE MISLED TOO, HAD IT BEEN THE MEMBERSHIP TEST. With the corrected markers, 19 of 25 GUI modules and 20241 lines name no GPU crate -- but most are WIDGETS emitting pinion scene nodes, useless to a TUI. Compiles-without-the-GPU and belongs-in-the-shared-crate are different questions, and only the second decides membership: the shared crate is the seven modules whose SUBJECT is the host relationship, not the display.

FOUR PIECES ARE GENUINELY NEW and everything else is a sprag-client call: a decoder from the local terminal's input bytes to the wire's W3C key vocabulary, a GridBuffer to termwiz Surface painter, a character-cell layouter over the same ratio tree the GUI reads in pixels, and the client's own event loop. The decode-then-re-encode is a correctness argument, not a purity one -- the host owns the pane's live input modes and the TUI's terminal is in different ones, so forwarding raw bytes would deliver the wrong encoding silently. termwiz supplies the first two and is already in the lock at the version sprag-vt uses, with input, terminal, render and surface all ungated, so the front needs no new third-party dependency.

THE FRONT INHERITS H4's FINDING AS A DEPENDENCY. A TUI user will expect prefix-% and prefix-quote, so slice 4 needs the split action the daemon does not have -- the same gap split-window -h refuses. And a third client makes R222's missing version handshake worse: a stale sprag-tui on a remote box against an updated daemon is exactly the skew nothing negotiates.

STILL OPEN, unchanged by this round: PINION-PR79 (IntrospectValue has no pre-encoded-JSON variant), the 142-261 us of a cells request that is neither the projection nor either encoding half, the unpriced socket, and the version handshake.

R224.decision_summary: R224: build the first slice of H1 -- take the wire client out of the GUI, and make GPU-freedom a gate rather than an intention. The design R223 wrote said the shared client would be a MOVE and not a rewrite, on the evidence that WireHost names pinion_shell zero times. This is that move, and the evidence held: git records the change as a rename and both crates compiled on the first attempt. THE SLICE EXISTS TO PRODUCE ONE MECHANICAL FACT rather than to deliver a feature, because everything the terminal client will be rests on that fact and nothing about it should be a matter of opinion: a crate that cannot link a GPU stack can be built on a headless server and attached to over ssh, and a crate that merely happens not to link one today cannot be relied on for that tomorrow. So the property is a test. It shells out to cargo tree because the manifest lists direct dependencies while the hazard is transitive, and it names three GPU crates rather than one because a client could acquire a window without acquiring a painter. THE ROUND ALSO CORRECTED ITS OWN DESIGN, which is the reason to slice at all. The design named seven modules for the shared crate; six of them reference GUI modules in CODE, which the import-level measurement behind that list could not see, and only wire.rs moved. Its three references to GUI modules turn out to be documentation links with nothing behind them. So the membership rule is neither what compiles nor what a module is about, but what it actually references -- the third version of a rule that has now been wrong twice, and the only one derived from the code rather than from a proxy for it.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-client (new lib): the display-independent half of a display client. Its whole content today is WireHost, moved verbatim from crates/sprag-gui/src/wire.rs -- git records it as a RENAME, which is the shape the design predicted. The crate root states the membership rule and the GPU-free property, and re-exports WireHost as the ONE public address so the module can stay private and no second spelling exists.

crates/sprag-client/tests/gpu_free.rs (new): the gate. It shells out to cargo tree rather than reading the manifest, because the manifest lists DIRECT dependencies and the hazard is transitive. It matches the crate NAME as the first token of each --prefix none line rather than searching the line, so a path containing the word winit cannot raise a false alarm, and it carries a vacuity guard asserting sprag-host is present, because a tree that failed to parse would otherwise pass while proving nothing.

crates/sprag-gui: keeps its twelve widget and shell modules and now depends on the new crate; one import line changed. Its crate doc says where the wire client went and why. The blank line the removed mod declaration left behind is gone.

Fifteen doc links inside WireHost's public documentation became code spans. Every sentence is intact; only the navigation from a public doc into a module internal is gone, which is the thing the lint exists to forbid.
verification_bullets: THE GATE, and it is the property the whole front rests on: cargo tree -p sprag-client -e normal yields ZERO of vello, wgpu and winit, over a closure of 204 crates against sprag-gui's 344. That check now lives in tests/gpu_free.rs instead of in whoever remembers to run it.

THE GATE'S OWN REVERT-PROOF CAUGHT ME FIRST, and this is the finding to keep. Adding pinion-shell to the manifest and expecting a failure is the obvious way to prove the gate bites -- and the first attempt appended the line after the dev-dependencies header, so it landed as a DEV dependency, which -e normal correctly excludes, and the test stayed green. The proof had routed around the mechanism it was named after. Moved under dependencies it fails as it should, naming winit, vello and wgpu. That is R222's fifth-revert-proof lesson recurring one round later in a different disguise: a test can be aimed at the right seam and still not touch it.

NOTHING REGRESSED: workspace 1145 -> 1146, and the +1 is the gate itself -- the 28 wire tests MOVED rather than multiplied. Live GUI pixel smoke 88 passed / 0 failed, so the real client still paints real cells off a wire client that now lives in another crate. fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, and rustdoc --document-private-items all green.

THE DESIGN'S MEMBERSHIP LIST WAS TOO GENEROUS BY SIX MODULES AND ABOUT 4900 LINES. It named seven modules whose subject is the host relationship; only wire.rs moved. The other six reference GUI modules in CODE, which an import-level measurement cannot see: command.rs names nine of them, slotview.rs seven including view, attention.rs four including view. wire.rs names three -- clipboard_osc, slotview and view -- and ALL THREE ARE DOC LINKS WITH NO CODE BEHIND THEM, which is the entire reason both crates compiled on the first try.

THE bin-TO-lib MOVE SWITCHED A DOC GATE ON. -D rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links is a structural false positive on a BIN, where sprag's binaries carry a crate-root allow, and a REAL gate on a LIB. Fifteen links from WireHost's public docs into module internals became errors the moment the module changed crates. The crate-root allow was CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: every sprag crate is publish = false, including sprag-vt where the lib gate is enforced, so "this one is internal" would have been an excuse rather than a distinction.

AND THE CITATION GATE REFUSED THE COMMIT over two section_missing citations -- the new crate doc wrote a rival-register theme name as a section reference, and the section sigil made it look like a citation into the design SSOT. The theme is not a section. Both are gone, along with a link target that pointed at a URL describing nothing.
carry_forward_bullets: THE MEMBERSHIP RULE HAS BEEN CORRECTED TWICE NOW AND THE THIRD VERSION IS THE ONE TO USE. Not "compiles without the GPU" -- that admits every widget, since pinion's paint helpers are GPU-free. Not "its subject is the host relationship" -- that admitted six modules that reference the GUI in code. The rule is WHAT A MODULE ACTUALLY REFERENCES, and by it the shared crate is one module today. The other six reach the GUI through SlotView, and SlotView reaches view; untangling that is its own slice, wanted only if the terminal client turns out to need those policies.

SLICES 2 THROUGH 5 ARE UNBUILT. Slice 2 maps a GridBuffer onto a termwiz Surface and paints one pane read-only. Slice 3 is the GATE for the whole front: the local terminal's input bytes decoded to the wire's W3C key vocabulary, resize, and a PTY harness that types into a real sprag-tui and reads the child's answer back -- nothing weaker proves ssh-attach works. Slice 4 is multi-pane and needs the split action the daemon does not have. Slice 5 is sprag attach --tui and --remote.

WHAT THE EXTRACTION DID NOT DECIDE: whether the six coupled modules should follow. The terminal client needs OSC 52 and OSC 8 policy eventually, and both currently sit behind SlotView. Deciding that before slice 2 has said what a TUI actually reads would be designing against a guess.

STILL OPEN, unchanged: PINION-PR79, the 142-261 us unattributed dispatch envelope, the unpriced socket, and the version handshake -- which a third client makes more urgent, since a stale sprag-tui on a remote box against an updated daemon is exactly the skew nothing negotiates.

R225.decision_summary: R225: build H1's second slice -- put a session's cells onto a real terminal -- and let running the binary find what reading it could not. The slice's stated job was a mapping and a viewer, and both landed: a pure function from a pinion GridBuffer to termwiz Changes, and a sprag-tui that attaches to a sprag-term session, paints its first pane, and repaints when the host says something moved. The design's open hypothesis was that pinion's cell vocabulary maps onto termwiz's without loss, and MEASURED it is one-to-one on every axis but two. The first exception is intensity, where pinion carries bold and dim as independent flags and termwiz carries one three-valued axis -- lossless in practice only because sprag's own emulator makes the two mutually exclusive at the SGR, which is a fact about the producer rather than about the types. The second is the one that mattered: pinion's column widths and termwiz's are computed by DIFFERENT unicode implementations, so a painter that assumes they agree is one disagreement away from a whole row of garbage. THE ROUND'S TWO REAL FINDINGS BOTH CAME FROM TESTS THAT DROVE SOMETHING REAL RATHER THAN SOMETHING BUILT TO AGREE. A hand-built cell test passed while the emulator-driven battery failed, because a double-counted wide cluster only displaces from the SECOND one on. And the binary, which every test had been green around, could not attach at all on its first live run.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-tui (new): the character-cell half of a display client. grid_changes maps a GridBuffer onto termwiz Changes -- cells batched into same-attribute runs, each anchored at an absolute column, with the cursor emitted last so the terminal's cursor comes to rest where the PANE's is. It is a pure function, so every test of it runs with no terminal at all.

crates/sprag-tui/src/bin/sprag-tui.rs (new): the client. It attaches through the SAME WireHost sprag-gui uses -- which is the whole return on H1 slice 1 -- and its loop is a real select rather than a poll: the host's change notification and the local terminal both arrive at one blocking poll_input, the host side through termwiz's terminal waker, so an idle client costs nothing. It restores the terminal from a panic hook BEFORE the message is printed, because Drop already restores it but cannot fix the ORDER, and a panic printed inside an alternate screen leaves with it.

crates/sprag-tui/tests/gpu_free.rs (new): the same gate sprag-client carries, on the package that actually ships to a headless box. It is a separate file rather than a shared helper because a GPU dependency added to THIS manifest would never appear in sprag-client's tree, and the shared gate would stay green while the binary stopped building where it is meant to run.

The membership rule from R224 held without argument: the painter is NOT in sprag-client. The shared crate hands out GridBuffers and knows nothing about the unit a frontend measures them in -- pixels there, character cells here -- which is the same reason the GUI's reflow module stayed put.
verification_bullets: THE BINARY COULD NOT ATTACH ON ITS FIRST LIVE RUN, AND NOTHING WRITTEN COULD HAVE TOLD ME. Under a PTY nobody had set a winsize on, the terminal reports 0x0; the client forwarded that zero; and the host's dimension parser rejects a non-positive dimension, so the entire attach failed with Invalid params and a message naming nothing about a size. That is not a harness artifact -- an ssh session before its first window-change looks the same. Fixed by substituting the conventional 80x24 for an unknown size, the same substitution tmux calls default-size and sprag-term itself already makes, applied at BOTH the boot dimensions and the local surface because BufferedTerminal sizes itself from the same raw answer.

LIVE, END TO END, UNDER A REAL PTY: the client booted, created a session the daemon counted as having one attached client, and painted its pane at 80x24. A marker driven into that pane from ANOTHER process -- the sprag CLI over the socket -- appeared in what the terminal received, which is the change-notification-to-repaint chain proven rather than described. The alternate screen was entered once and left once, the pane's cursor became the terminal's at row 3 column 34, and the quit key exited 0.

THE EMULATOR-DRIVEN BATTERY CAUGHT A BUG THE HAND-BUILT TEST COULD NOT. A wide cluster's columns were counted twice -- once for the head claiming both, once for its trailer claiming its own -- which is invisible with ONE wide cluster and displaces everything from the second one on. The unit test had one; the battery printed three Korean syllables and failed. This is exactly why the design asked for a driven battery: a hand-built cell is one I invented, and it agreed with me.

TWO GUARDS, BOTH REVERT-PROVEN, AND THE SECOND PROOF FAILED FIRST. Neutering the width cross-check displaces the cell after an over-wide cluster, as claimed. The orphan-trailer guard's first proof PASSED with the guard removed, because the test put the orphan at column 0 -- where a skipped first cell leaves the run empty and the next cell restarts it at its own absolute column, masking the displacement completely. Moved inside a run, it fails as it should. A test can name the right mechanism and still not touch it.

The width cross-check itself is a guard whose live trigger I could NOT find: a battery of combining sequences, an emoji, a ZWJ family, and two East-Asian ambiguous-width characters all agree between unicode-width and termwiz's tables today. So it is proven against a directly-constructed disagreement rather than a discovered one, and the fidelity assertion -- every cell the projection placed at a column is on the screen at that column -- is checked against the projection's OWN column assignment, so it stays honest if either implementation moves.

Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, rustdoc --document-private-items, workspace 1146 -> 1169 tests passed / 0 failed, live GUI pixel smoke 88 passed / 0 failed. The bin-to-lib doc gate fired again exactly as it did last round, on two public docs linking into module internals; the citation gate refused the commit over two design-document section references written with the section sigil, which is the same near-miss as last round in a new file.
carry_forward_bullets: SLICE 3 IS THE GATE FOR THE WHOLE FRONT and nothing about this slice weakens that: local terminal input decoded to the wire's W3C key vocabulary, resize reaching the host, and a PTY harness that types into a real sprag-tui and reads the child's answer back. This round's live drive is a manual one-shot, which verifies nothing on its own -- it found a defect, which is a different thing from proving an absence.

THE PANE IS NOT RESIZED, DELIBERATELY. A local resize resizes the local surface only, so the view is cropped or margined but never corrupted. A read-only client that resized a pane would be reshaping other clients' windows for a view it cannot type into, and the resize belongs in the slice where both halves can be proven together.

TWO NAMES ARE NOW WRONG AND BOTH ARE OPERATOR-VISIBLE: the shared client reads SPRAG_GUI_HOST_SOCK for the host socket and SPRAG_GUI_SESSION for the session to attach, and a terminal client reading GUI-named variables is the extraction of R224 showing through. A rename needs a compatibility alias and touches the smoke tool, so it is named here rather than done silently.

The client's quit keys -- q and Ctrl-C -- are PROVISIONAL and say so in code. Once keys reach the pane, q belongs to the program running in it, and the client's own commands move behind the fixed prefix table of slice 4. Raw mode is what makes this a decision at all: with the line discipline off, Ctrl-C is a byte rather than a signal.
