R243.decision_summary: R243: `window-size manual` + `resize-window` — the value R241 declined to offer, behind a reason that was a true statement about cost and said nothing about what the omission cost. That reason: `manual` needs a stored size and a verb that writes it, and an option value naming a rule nothing performs is this front's recurring defect. Every word holds. Probed first — R241's own rule, and R242's finding that a true reason can hide a defect — the omission's cost turned out to be measurable and irreversible from the user's side: a session with panes at 100x30 and nobody attached was reflowed to 80x24 the instant any client attached, went to 60x20 when that client resized, and STAYED at 60x20 after it detached, because the honest answer with nobody watching is to leave the panes alone. A long-running program's wrap width was set by whoever last glanced at the session, permanently, with no value of the option able to hold it. Reading also moved the design off the prior round's own wording: the stored size is NOT per session. It is `tile`'s second argument and `tile`'s first is a WINDOW's tree, so the rectangle belongs beside the tree it measures — on `Window`, in the snapshot, restored with the arrangement. The other decision is what `manual` means with nothing pinned, and it is not `None`: `None` means no window, which sends both frontends to their no-window fallback of sizing panes from their own surface — the two-authority defect R242 removed, re-reachable by one `set-option`. It defers to the DEFAULT policy instead, which also makes `set-option window-size manual` on its own a change the user cannot see.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-terminal/src/registry.rs: `Window::manual_size` / `set_manual_size`, plus `resize_window` on `Session` and `SessionRegistry` beside `rename_window`, and a read-only `SessionRegistry::window` to match `window_mut`. The field lives on the WINDOW, not the session, and the reason is a property of the function that consumes it: a pane's size is `tile(tree, window)`, and `tile`'s tree is a WINDOW's, so the rectangle it is laid out over belongs beside the tree it measures. R241's own sentence about what `manual` would need said "a per-session size", and that was the one word in it worth correcting. The setter deliberately does NOT bump `layout_revision`: that number says a client's projection of the ARRANGEMENT is stale, and the arrangement is untouched here — the same tree over a different rectangle. Bumping it would invalidate every client's layout cache to deliver news about something else.

crates/sprag-terminal/src/snapshot.rs: `WindowSnapshot::manual_size`, `#[serde(default)]` so the addition is additive (the rule `argv` and `remote` already follow — a pre-field snapshot loads un-pinned, which is exactly what those daemons did). It has to be here because a reboot is precisely the moment there is no client to ask: every pane already carries its own `cols`/`rows`, but those are READINGS taken at snapshot time and the first client to attach overwrites them, while this is a DECISION no set of pane sizes can reconstruct (they are a tiling of it, not it).

crates/sprag-host/src/window.rs: `WindowSize::Manual`, and `arbitrate` takes a third input. THE design decision of the round is what it answers with `manual` set and nothing pinned: not `None`. `None` means "no window", which sends both frontends to their no-window fallback of sizing panes from their own surface — the two-authority defect R242 removed, re-reachable by one `set-option`. It defers to `WindowSize::DEFAULT` instead, so `set-option window-size manual` on its own is a change the user cannot see: they have named a source and the source is empty until `resize-window` writes it. The `Latest | Manual` arm that implements the deferral is held to `DEFAULT` by its own test rather than by a comment.

crates/sprag-host/src/window.rs: `retile` reads the pin off the window it is about to tile, and takes the scope and the pin under ONE registry lock. Two locks would let a window switch land between them and lay one window's tree out over another window's pinned rectangle — the same class as the lock-in-a-match-scrutinee R242 paid for, one indirection along.

crates/sprag-host/src/wire.rs + workspace.rs: `RESIZE_WINDOW_ACTION` (`{window?, cols?, rows?}`) — both dimensions pin, neither un-pins, and HALF is refused whole, the rule `client/size` already follows. It writes a stored fact and touches no PTY; the panes follow through the invoke BOUNDARY's re-derivation, so a pinned window and a derived one reach the panes by one path. Thirteen actions became fourteen and the boundary did not have to learn anything.

crates/sprag-host/src/bin/sprag.rs: `sprag resize-window -t SESSION [window] {-x COLS -y ROWS | -u}`. tmux's relative forms and its `-a`/`-A` are NOT offered, and the reason is a fact rather than a size preference: each computes a new rectangle from a current one, and this CLI holds neither input — reading them here would put a SECOND arbitration in a client, which is the defect this whole front has been removing. The verb pins under ANY policy and NAMES the gap on stderr when the policy in force is not `manual`, read from the user's own file. Refusing the natural order (pin, then choose to use it) would fail for no mechanical reason, and a stored value that silently does nothing is what this front keeps finding.

crates/sprag-host/src/options.rs: `manual` joins `WINDOW_SIZE_VALUES` on the same terms as the other three, because it now names a rule the daemon performs. What it does with an empty source is `arbitrate`'s to state, not the table's: an empty source is not an unperformed rule.
verification_bullets: THE COST OF THE OMISSION WAS MEASURED BEFORE ANY DESIGN, and the numbers are what shaped the round. A live daemon, one pane, no config: boot 40x6; a client attaches and resizes to 100x30, pane 100x30; the client DETACHES, pane holds 100x30 and the window goes null; a second client attaches at its terminal's own 80x24 and the pane becomes 80x24 INSTANTLY, before the user has done anything; it resizes to 60x20, pane 60x20; it detaches, and the pane STAYS 60x20. So the program the user had arranged at 100x30 was reflowed by a transient client and left there, and no value of `window-size` could hold it. R241 had recorded `manual` as needing machinery; this is what not having it cost.

THE PTY GATE IS TWO REAL CLIENTS' WORTH OF MACHINERY ON ONE LIVE SESSION, and every number in it is chosen so no fallback can be mistaken for a pass: the pin (111x33) is not the boot pane (40x6), not the attaching client's pseudoterminal (80x24) and not the area it resizes to (60x20). Claim 1 is the discriminating one — with NO client attached, the pin moves the panes, and every other policy answers "no window" in that state, so this alone separates a `manual` the daemon performs from a value the table accepts. Then a real `sprag-tui` on a real pseudoterminal attaches and reports 60x20, and the panes stay pinned; the wait is on `sprag list-clients` showing the client's own area, because "the pane did not move" means nothing until the report has LANDED. It holds through a settle window, and it survives the DETACH, which is its own re-derivation path.

THE UN-PIN IS ITS OWN GATE, and it is the only direction that can tell a governed report from an absent one: `-u` with a client attached hands the window back and the panes take the CLIENT's area — which is also the live proof that `manual` with nothing pinned defers to the default policy rather than answering "no window".

THE GUI IS GATED SEPARATELY AND THE CLAIM IS NOT THE SAME ONE. R242 proved a window is IN the arbitration; this proves the one policy that takes the arbitration AWAY from it still governs it, which a reasoning-only argument would have skipped — a GUI reports what its panes measured, `manual` ignores that report, and "the pin wins" depends on the client not re-asserting its own measurement. Five checks in the live headless smoke, pinned 20 cols and 8 rows LARGER than the window measured for itself: the pin becomes the session's window over the client's report, every pane grows past what the window measured, the window paints PART of every pinned pane, the pin is not pulled back, and `-u` returns every pane to exactly what the window measured.

SIX REVERT-PROOFS MEASURED, FIVE RED. `arbitrate` ignoring the pin fails a unit test, both PTY gates, the CLI gate and three of the five smoke checks. `retile` not READING the pin (passing None) fails both PTY gates — 22 of the suite's 24 still pass, so that call is the whole path. The pin not RESTORED, and separately not CAPTURED, each fail the registry round-trip with `None` where `Some((123, 45))` was asserted — both ends of the chain proved separately. The CLI's note removed fails the CLI gate on an empty stderr.

THE SIXTH REVERT-PROOF PASSED, AND IT IS RECORDED AS A LIMIT RATHER THAN FIXED. Deleting the `announce` from the `resize_window` action leaves the whole PTY suite green, including the two tests written for that action, because the re-derivation resizes panes, a pane resize marks it dirty, and the dirty path bumps. That is R241's `client/size` finding repeating one action along. The announce is kept for the earlier, contracted wake and because every sibling action announces, and its doc now says it is not independently falsifiable and why — the chain it would otherwise rest on holds only while a window change always changes some pane's size, which is false for a window of nothing but floats and false for a re-pin the tiling absorbs.

THE CLI GATE CAUGHT A REAL MISTAKE IN ITS OWN FIRST DRAFT, and the mistake is the invariant working. It gave the isolated config home to the CLI alone, so the verb stored the pin and printed no note — its own view of the file said `manual` — while the daemon went on arbitrating under the default and the panes never moved. No option crosses the wire, so the DAEMON reads `window-size` itself and the test has to hand it the same file. The gate now flips the policy through the real `set-option`, which also shows the daemon picking the change up with nothing restarted.

THE ARTEFACT WAS RUN AND ITS OUTPUT READ, repeatedly with the input changed. `show-options window-size` off no daemon; the refusal listing all four values for a word that names no rule; the file after `set-option`. Then a live daemon: pinning with no client attached moved the pane 80x24 -> 120x40 -> 90x25 -> 100x28 by name; `-u`; half a size, a zero, `-u` with dimensions and an unknown window each refused with their own reason. Then a real reboot with `--daemon`: `manual_size` on disk, and the pane back at 111x33. That last reading was CONFOUNDED and the confound was found rather than reported as a pass — the snapshot's own per-pane `cols`/`rows` were also 111x33, so it could not tell a live pin from a restored reading. The discriminating measurement forces the pane elsewhere and watches the next action boundary pull it back (111x33), with the un-pinned control staying where it was put (40x10).

carry_forward_bullets: A REASON THAT NAMES ITS OWN COST IS STILL NOT A MEASUREMENT OF WHAT THE OMISSION COSTS. R241 declined `manual` because it needs a stored size and a verb, and because an option value naming a rule nothing performs is this front's recurring defect. Both true, and the second is a rule worth keeping. What neither says is that without it a long-running program's wrap width is set by whoever last glanced at the session and left — measured, three attaches deep, and irreversible from the user's side. This is R242's finding a second time in a row, which makes it a habit rather than an anecdote: when a previous round's boundary is the thing you are building against, probe the FAILURE, not the reason.

A STORED THING BELONGS BESIDE THE FUNCTION THAT CONSUMES IT, AND THAT IS WHERE THE DESIGN CAME FROM RATHER THAN FROM THE PRIOR ROUND'S WORDING. R241 wrote "a per-session size" and it reads as settled. A long-running program's wrap width was set by whoever last glanced at the session, permanently, with no value of the option able to hold it. Reading also moved the design off the prior round's own wording: the stored size is NOT per session. It is `tile`'s second argument and `tile`'s first is a WINDOW's tree, so the rectangle belongs beside the tree it measures — on `Window`, in the snapshot, restored with the arrangement. Round 10.decision_summary: Extract the plugin extension API (the README #1 concern) from two real consumers: PaneAccess (data API) + a Plugin/Driver behavior-vs-substrate split, validated by the orchestrator plus a new pipe plugin.
changes_bullets: Renamed sprag-orchestrator -> sprag-plugin; it is now the plugin substrate, split into modules: access (PaneAccess + WorkspacePaneAccess + KeyStroke/PaneRow/InjectError), plugin (Plugin::step + Step + Verdict), driver (Driver + Guardrails + Outcome/OutcomeState), and the bundled orchestrator + pipe plugins. Pinion-free.

PaneAccess is the extension API: pane_ids / pane_collapsed / pane_rows (generation+text in one locked snapshot, killing a TOCTOU race) / inject (returns bytes). WorkspacePaneAccess over Arc<Mutex<Workspace>> is the single read+inject path, so plugins stop reaching into SessionHandle directly (review finding D, read-path unification).

Split the orchestrator loop: the Driver owns the SCE statechart (flattened to idle->running->{converged,exhausted,failed}) plus the guardrails (max_iterations/max_injected_bytes moved off OrchestrationSpec onto Guardrails); Plugin::step owns perceive/act/judge. The orchestrator (fixed-stimulus drive) and a new Pipe (relay a source pane's newly-damaged rows into a destination pane; never self-converges, guardrails bind) both impl Plugin.

The Pipe is the second consumer that proves the abstraction generalizes: same damage-generation primitive as the orchestrator's observe, but a plugin-owned cursor (after-last-relay vs before-last-stimulus). act/judge were collapsed into one step (so the statechart's internal phases do not leak into the plugin contract); inject returns the byte count feeding the Driver's cost guardrail.
verification_bullets: 59 workspace tests pass. The orchestrator's four tests pass unchanged in intent via Driver::run(&mut Orchestrator, panes) -- the regression gate proving the extraction preserved behavior; plus two WorkspacePaneAccess tests and the pipe proof test (seed source, relay into destination, exhaust on the iteration budget). cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean.

The design was pressure-tested by a Plan agent that corrected five points before implementation: a single step (not act/judge), pane_rows folding text+generations to remove a TOCTOU race, inject returning the byte count, the flattened statechart, and deferring the host-External base to the exposure round.

Crate rename was contained (nothing depended on sprag-orchestrator yet); build stayed green at each phase. SCE needed nothing new (same usage as Round 8); pinion's vendored SCE remained content-identical to canonical.
carry_forward_bullets: Exposure round: OrchestratorExternal / a plugin host over RPC -- start/observe a Driver::run off the serve thread (background execution), so external AI peers drive plugins as scene-as-data -- and extract the shared host-External base (backends/repaint/thread_ownership/Debug/arg-parse) from the now three Externals at that point.

AI-tool adapters (claude/aider in panes with structured I/O) + bidirectional A<->B relay + character-level delta diffing (the pipe relays whole rows on a generation bump today) are the real AI<->AI layer beyond this substrate.
PaneAccess additions (cell/style read, scrollback) stay additive until a consumer needs them (YAGNI).

Round 11.decision_summary: Expose plugins over RPC, completing the plugin-platform contract: a PluginsExternal runs plugins on background threads (non-blocking serve) tracked in a shared RunRegistry, plus the shared host-External boilerplate extraction.
changes_bullets: New PluginsExternal (sprag-host): scene/invoke run (a plugin discriminator orchestrator|pipe, submit-time pane validation -> synchronous Rejected, DEFAULT_GUARDRAILS, spawns a background Driver::run that writes the terminal RunState) + scene/query runs/plugins; the plugin Outcome is rendered to JSON in the host so sprag-plugin stays serde-free. Added as the sprag_plugins child of workspace_scene.

Run registry: the long-lived state is a shared Arc<Mutex<RunRegistry>> owned by serve and threaded via a HostState{workspace,runs,previews,revision} bundle -- NOT owned by the per-request PluginsExternal, which is a throwaway projection rebuilt each request (the critical bug a Plan agent caught). Each run carries its own Arc<Mutex<RunState>> cell so reading the registry never blocks behind a run; sweep joins finished threads (is_finished, non-blocking; a panic becomes Panicked); join_all on RunRegistry Drop and serve shutdown reaps threads (bounded by guardrails).

E-extraction: a sprag-host-local rpc_external_impl! macro (mirroring pinion's query_proxy_external_impl!, but &[Rpc]-only) plus a shared lock and arg helpers (as_object/require_pane_id/require_str/opt_str/opt_dim) in a new external module; SpragPaneExternal and WorkspaceExternal rewritten onto them (each keeps its own ExternalIntrospect and Debug).

Producer correctness: Workspace::close now returns the removed Pane so the caller drops it (TerminalSession::drop's kill/wait/join) OUTSIDE the workspace lock, so a close can no longer stall an in-flight plugin run contending on that lock.
verification_bullets: 64 workspace tests pass: a background converged run over RPC (poll query(runs) to done), a synchronous Rejected for an unknown target pane, a non-blocking responsiveness test (a sleep pane's slow run does not delay an immediate snapshot), a Driver Err->Failed unit test via a mock PaneAccess (no threads), the registry submit/sweep/join lifecycle, and the existing host/producer suites. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean.

Bin end-to-end (sprag-term -- cat): scene/invoke /sprag_plugins/external/run returns a run id; scene/query plugins returns [orchestrator, pipe]; query runs shows the run reaching done with outcome converged (iterations 1, injected_bytes 5).

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent which caught the registry-ownership bug and refined the reaping (is_finished join), shutdown (join_all on Drop), and guardrail-default model. pinion/SCE needed nothing new.
carry_forward_bullets: Interactive cancel (designed, deferred): an Arc<AtomicBool> trigger checked atop Driver::run's loop firing a cancel event to a new cancelled statechart final + OutcomeState::Cancelled -- the terminal state stays in the chart (SCE dogfood), the flag is only the trigger. Without it, host shutdown blocks until in-flight runs finish (the honest cost).
AI-tool adapters (claude/aider in panes with structured I/O) as the real AI<->AI plugins over this exposed substrate; bidirectional A<->B relay; character-level delta diffing for the pipe.
Live per-iteration run progress and run GC from the registry are deferred until a consumer needs them (YAGNI; Outcome already carries iterations/injected_bytes).

changes_bullets: New crate file crates/sprag-plugin/src/agent.rs: the one-shot Agent plugin (AgentSpec{prompt, eof, timeout}). step() injects prompt + Enter + (Ctrl-D/EOF if eof) via the R6 sprag-input encoder, waits for the pane child to finish, then captures the damaged-row delta since the prompt as the reply. Pinion-free.

Completion via child-exit, not output quiescence: new PaneAccess::pane_eof (WorkspacePaneAccess reads TerminalSession::is_eof under the workspace lock; NO sprag-terminal change, is_eof was already public via Pane::session()). is_eof's 'all bytes applied once EOF observed' contract makes the capture race-free and defeats the prompt-echo/think-time race a debounce would hit (the injected prompt echoes back before the model starts replying).

Host wiring (sprag-host/plugins.rs): PluginsExternal 'agent' run arm (require pane + prompt; optional eof/timeout_ms), BoxedPlugin::Agent variant, PLUGINS gains 'agent'. No new pinion RPC methods and no new SCXML states/events — the Agent maps to Verdict::Converged after one step on the existing idle->running->converged statechart.

Round 13.decision_summary: Bidirectional AI<->AI: a Dialogue plugin runs two one-shot AI endpoints (claude -p) in alternating turns, spawning a fresh pane per turn via a new pane-lifecycle extension, capturing the threaded transcript.
changes_bullets: New crate file crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs: the Dialogue plugin. Each step() is one turn — spawn the active endpoint as a fresh pane with the OTHER side's last message as its argv prompt (claude -p "<msg>"; message-as-argv, not stdin, so there is no cooked-mode echo to strip and the fresh pane's whole screen is the reply), await child-exit (R12 pane_eof), capture the reply, close the pane, hand the reply to the other side. Never self-converges; the Driver's max_iterations IS the turn budget (ends Exhausted with the transcript as payload — the Pipe pattern). Pinion-free.

Pane-lifecycle extension: new PaneLifecycle sub-trait {spawn(argv, cols, rows)->PaneId, close(id)->bool} reached via PaneAccess::lifecycle()->Option<&dyn PaneLifecycle> (default None) — kept OFF the read/inject surface every plugin depends on (interface segregation, zero ripple to Orchestrator/Pipe/Agent/test-doubles). WorkspacePaneAccess impls it over Workspace::spawn/close; new InjectError::Spawn. A RAII PaneGuard closes the per-turn pane on EVERY exit path (no leaked PTY/child even on a mid-step failure); close binds the removed Pane so its blocking Drop runs OUTSIDE the workspace lock (R11 lesson).
Honest accounting: Dialogue injects nothing (the message rides as argv), so Step.injected_bytes is 0 and the turn budget is purely max_iterations — no faking a byte cost into the guardrail.

Host wiring (sprag-host/plugins.rs): PluginsExternal 'dialogue' run arm (endpoint_a/endpoint_b argv arrays + seed + optional cols/rows/timeout_ms; NO target-pane validation — Dialogue creates its own panes), BoxedPlugin::Dialogue, PLUGINS += 'dialogue', a require_string_array argv helper. The transcript rides the R12 captured()/RunState.output seam. No new pinion RPC methods, no new SCXML states/events.
verification_bullets: 76 workspace tests pass (+8): access lifecycle_spawn_and_close_roundtrip + lifecycle_spawn_rejects_empty_argv; dialogue multi_turn_single_endpoint_threads_the_message, bidirectional_turns_alternate_endpoints (A:x -> B:A:x -> A:B:A:x -> B:A:B:A:x), leaves_no_leftover_panes, closes_the_pane_when_a_turn_times_out (the PaneGuard leak regression), no_lifecycle_fails_cleanly (NoPanes -> Failed); rpc runs_a_dialogue_plugin_to_done_with_a_transcript (background run, threaded transcript in output, only the initial pane survives). cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean.

Genuine AI<->AI verified manually: the #[ignore]d dialogue::tests::two_real_claudes_converse ran two real 'claude -p' turns and captured a non-empty transcript (~10.8s). Offline coverage uses deterministic printf fake endpoints; the turn-threading logic is pinned by bidirectional_turns_alternate_endpoints so the live test only proves the real-CLI end to end.

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent: confirmed NO pinion/SCE change (a never-converge/exhaust-on-budget plugin is the existing Pipe shape on the existing statechart). changes_bullets: crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs: Dialogue is now STATEFUL — replaced current_message (last reply only) with history: Vec<String> of "<label>: <reply>". Each turn renders a prompt = a one-line instruction naming the current speaker + the seed + the labelled transcript so far (render_prompt; exactly one \n per logical line, no trailing newline), spawns the endpoint with that prompt as its final argv element, captures the reply, collapses it to one line, and appends "<label>: <reply>". captured() = history.join("\n"). DialogueSpec gains label_a/label_b (default A/B).

The R13 pane-lifecycle/PaneGuard/pane_eof/capture machinery is reused unchanged; the statechart is untouched (still never-converge -> Exhausted, transcript = payload).

Multi-line replies are collapsed to a single line (split_whitespace().join(" ")) so a reply cannot inject unlabelled lines into the next turn's prompt (a correctness flaw the Plan agent caught; invisible to single-line fakes).

Round 15.decision_summary: Interactive cancel: a run-lifecycle cancel signal ends a run in a new SCE 'cancelled' statechart final; the host cancels a run over RPC and shutdown aborts in-flight runs promptly.
changes_bullets: orchestration.scxml: added a `cancel` transition out of `running` to a new `<final id="cancelled"/>` — SCE regenerated OrchestrationEvent::Cancel / OrchestrationState::Cancelled (another statechart final, the SCE dogfood). driver.rs: new OutcomeState::Cancelled; Driver::run checks panes.cancelled() at the loop TOP (fires Cancel before stepping, so a cancel pre-empts the next step); outcome() maps Cancelled explicitly, above the Failed wildcard.

Cancel rides the handle the Driver and every plugin already share: new PaneAccess::cancelled() default-false (a RUN-lifecycle signal, documented as not pane-scoped; same default-off pattern as lifecycle(), zero ripple to test doubles). WorkspacePaneAccess holds an Arc<AtomicBool> read with Acquire; new with_cancel(workspace, flag) for the host (new() keeps a never-set flag, so existing call sites are unchanged).

The three plugins' wait loops (Orchestrator::observe, Agent::await_reply, Dialogue::await_reply) check cancelled() each ~10ms poll and bail; crucially a cancelled step returns Verdict::Continue WITHOUT converging or recording a junk turn (so cancel strictly dominates a would-be Converged/partial reply) and the Driver loop-top then ends Cancelled. Dialogue's PaneGuard still reaps the per-turn pane on the cancel path.

Host: each run gets an Arc<AtomicBool>; spawn_run builds WorkspacePaneAccess::with_cancel and stores a clone in the RunRegistry (RunRecord.cancel). New PluginsExternal `cancel {id}` action (rides scene/invoke; synchronous Rejected for an unknown id) -> RunRegistry::cancel(id) stores the flag (Release). New RunRegistry::cancel_all(); serve shutdown and RunRegistry::Drop now cancel_all() BEFORE join_all(), so in-flight runs abort promptly (fixes R11's shutdown-blocks honest cost). outcome_to_json maps Cancelled -> "cancelled". No pinion change.
verification_bullets: 79 workspace tests pass (+4), all deterministic (cancel is provider-independent, no network): driver driver_ends_cancelled_without_running_a_step (loop-top pre-empts the step — Cancelled, 0 iterations, no failure); dialogue cancel_mid_turn_ends_cancelled_with_no_leak_or_junk (threaded — a sleep endpoint cancelled mid-await aborts in <5s, OutcomeState::Cancelled, the per-turn pane reaped, transcript None); rpc cancels_a_running_plugin_over_rpc (cancel {id} -> run reaches done=cancelled; unknown id rejects synchronously); rpc shutdown_cancels_in_flight_runs_promptly (cancel_all+join_all returns in <5s on a looping sleep-pane run, reaped cancelled). cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean.

SCE codegen verified before building the rest: adding the cancel transition + cancelled final regenerated OrchestrationEvent::Cancel / OrchestrationState::Cancelled and is_in_final_state() covers Cancelled; the Driver uses only the existing Engine API (process_event/is_in_final_state/get_current_state).

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent: confirmed NO pinion/SCE change. It caught the mid-step masking bug (a cancelled await must NOT return Converged or push a junk turn -> the plugins return Continue and record nothing), the outcome() wildcard silently mapping Cancelled->Failed (-> explicit arm above the wildcard), and the memory ordering (Acquire/Release, not Relaxed).

Round 17.decision_summary: Textbook remediation of the AI layer: fix the smells the session review found — RunContext cancel seam, shared poll_until, coherent cost guardrail, lossless capture, single-source screen text, and SSOT/comment sync — without reworking the verified-clean foundation.
changes_bullets: Cancel seam (ISP fix): removed PaneAccess::cancelled (a run-lifecycle signal smuggled onto a pane-scoped trait); new RunContext in crates/sprag-plugin/src/run.rs threaded into Plugin::step and Driver::run, built host-side from the run's Arc<AtomicBool>. Each client now depends only on what it uses.

De-duplicated the await loops: the three hand-rolled bounded-cancellable waits (Orchestrator::observe, Agent::await_reply, Dialogue's await) collapse to one shared run::poll_until returning a Waited enum; shared POLL_INTERVAL + DEFAULT_REPLY_TIMEOUT constants (the per-plugin copies are gone).

Coherent cost guardrail: Step.injected_bytes -> Step.cost, Guardrails.max_injected_bytes -> max_cost; Dialogue now reports its argv prompt bytes (was a hardcoded 0), so the budget binds every plugin in one currency rather than being inert for the heaviest one.

Lossless capture: Dialogue stops flattening replies (removed split_whitespace().join) — replies are kept verbatim in a structured Vec<Turn>, rendered blank-line-delimited (render_turn) so code/lists/multi-line answers survive and turn boundaries stay clear.

Single-source screen text + corrections: Screen::full_text (sprag-vt) is the one definition, read by both in-process pane_full_text and a NEW RPC full_text query on the pane External (RPC peers and plugins now see the same screen, scrollback included). ED-3 (ESC[3J) now clears scrollback (was a no-op under a now-false comment). InjectError -> PaneError (covers spawn); BoxedPlugin -> PluginKind. DESIGN §3/§5 got corrective caveats (scrollback modeled; status current through R16).
verification_bullets: 89 workspace tests pass (sprag-vt 19, sprag-plugin 20 +2 ignored, sprag-host 30, sprag-input 11, sprag-terminal 5, sprag-grid 4); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. New/reworked tests: port ed3_clears_scrollback + full_text_*; rpc full_text_query_includes_scrolled_off_lines; the dialogue accumulation/long-reply tests made format-robust (parse strictly-increasing counts; verbatim newline needles).
Both live AI paths re-verified AFTER the refactor: the #[ignore]d drives_real_claude and two_real_claudes_converse passed (~15.8s) — genuine single-shot and stateful AI<->AI behaviour preserved.

Driven by a session review: two independent adversarial agents (a refactoring lens and an architecture lens) plus direct SSOT verification of the §sections. R17 addresses every must-fix/major they raised (await-loop duplication, cancelled()-on-PaneAccess ISP violation, inert cost guardrail, lossy Dialogue capture, stale EraseScrollback comment, read-path divergence) while leaving the foundation they verified as textbook (layering, SCE dogfood, concurrency/ownership, the PaneLifecycle sub-trait) untouched.
carry_forward_bullets: Real token/$ cost accounting is now structurally ready: the cost channel is named `cost`, and full_text survives scrolling so `claude -p --output-format json` usage is parseable. Switching Dialogue to JSON couples reply extraction to JSON parsing — design the extraction (result field -> next message, usage -> cost).
--resume optimization for Dialogue (avoid the O(n^2) whole-history resend and the MAX_ARG_STRLEN single-arg ceiling).

Agent capture is still visible-screen damage-delta (it injects into a non-fresh pane); a shared one-shot-exchange abstraction could unify Agent/Dialogue further IF a third consumer appears — poll_until already shares the wait, so don't over-abstract before then.

Driver::run is still thread+poll-blocking; an event/wake model is the ceiling for many concurrent long-lived runs (a named risk, not yet due). The DESIGN §section BODIES still describe R1-R5 (corrective caveats added); a full rewrite or a new §6 for the AI-orchestration layer is deferred.

Round 18.decision_summary: Replace the byte-proxy cost in the AI dialogue with real billed tokens parsed from `claude -p --output-format json`, reading the envelope from a new raw-stdout producer tap (the grid corrupts the wrapped single-line JSON) and degrading gracefully on any parse failure.
changes_bullets: sprag-terminal raw tap (crates/sprag-terminal/src/session.rs): TerminalSession gains a bounded, HEAD-anchored RawCapture (Arc<Mutex>, RAW_CAPTURE_CAP=256 KiB) the reader thread tees into in the SAME loop iteration as emulator.advance, so once is_eof holds every byte is BOTH captured and rendered (the grid's completeness guarantee extended to the source stream). SessionHandle::raw_output()/TerminalSession::raw_output() snapshot (bytes, truncated). Head-anchored (append-until-cap then latch truncated) because a JSON envelope is parsed from its START -- a tail ring would drop the opening brace; the cap is the oversized-degradation point. The lock() helper was generalized to any Mutex<T>.

PaneAccess::pane_raw_output (crates/sprag-plugin/src/access.rs): new pane_raw_output(id)->Option<(Vec<u8>,bool)>, DEFAULT None (interface segregation, like lifecycle() -- the three PaneAccess test doubles compile untouched); WorkspacePaneAccess returns the handle's raw snapshot. Documented as a distinct read (source bytes) from the pane_*_text family (rendered grid: wrapped, trailing-trimmed, control-stripped) -- NOT a read-path divergence (R17 unified the grid-text read), a legitimately different datum.

Reply parser (new crates/sprag-plugin/src/reply.rs): parse_claude_json(&[u8])->Option<ClaudeReply{text:Option<String>,tokens:Option<u64>,is_error:bool}>, Value-walked (serde_json added to sprag-plugin as foreign-tool PERCEPTION, not type serialization -- the public surface stays serde-free, no derives). Brace-span ({..}) extraction tolerates a trailing newline / kernel ONLCR \r\n / framing noise. tokens = usage.input_tokens + usage.output_tokens (cache_creation/cache_read excluded -- large and bursty, would void a token budget). Requires a result/usage signature so a random JSON object is not claimed; any failure -> None.

ReplyFormat + Dialogue cost/capture (crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs): new ReplyFormat{Text(default), ClaudeJson} per-endpoint (DialogueSpec.format_a/format_b, mirroring label_a/label_b -- deferred the Endpoint-struct refactor). decode_reply: Text reads the rendered full_text (unchanged); ClaudeJson reads pane_raw_output, parses it, and on success records the result-text + real tokens. Graceful degradation: a truncated/over-cap/unparsable envelope falls back to the raw lossy text + the prompt-byte proxy cost -- never a PaneError, so a broken reply never fails the turn; the cancel path keeps the prompt-byte cost. Step.cost is now real tokens for a ClaudeJson turn.

Cost-unit contract (plugin.rs Step::cost / driver.rs Guardrails::max_cost docs): retired the 'one currency / bytes' framing for 'each plugin's natural spend unit; a run drives exactly ONE plugin so the caller sizes max_cost to it; the Driver stays unit-agnostic (only sums and bounds)'. NO Driver/SCXML/SCE change -- the cost channel R17 built IS the seam; only what feeds it changed.

Host (crates/sprag-host/src/plugins.rs): the dialogue run arm parses optional format_a/format_b ('text'|'claude_json'; unknown -> synchronous Rejected) via a new parse_reply_format helper; ReplyFormat re-exported from sprag-plugin.
verification_bullets: 106 workspace tests pass (+17 over R17's 89), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. New deterministic tests: sprag-terminal raw_output byte-faithful-on-a-wrapping-line + over-cap-truncation; sprag-plugin reply parser (real envelope, escaped-\n preserved, framing noise, truncated/garbage/non-envelope -> None, is_error, missing-usage, usage-without-result), pane_raw_output round-trip, dialogue claude_json real-token-cost (cost==2 turns x 50) + token-bound guardrail (50-token budget exhausts in 1 turn) + graceful-degradation-on-bad-JSON (records raw text, does NOT Fail); sprag-host runs_a_claude_json_dialogue_with_real_token_cost (cost==100 over RPC, clean result not raw envelope) + rejects_an_unknown_reply_format.

Live AI re-verified: the #[ignore]d two_real_claudes_converse ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns (~22s) and accumulated real token cost = 18214 (a byte proxy would be a few hundred); the transcript carried the clean result text (no input_tokens envelope leak) and a coherent count -- the real-PTY check that the envelope parses off the raw source with no stderr/spinner/wrap pollution.

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent (read every touched file first): confirmed the raw-stdout tap is the correct seam over the lossy grid (pane_full_text injects a wrap-\n at every row; trailing-trim drops interior spaces in result), the cost unit is total tokens (exact integer, keeps the 64*1024 default guardrail sane) not micro-USD, ReplyFormat is per-endpoint fields not an Endpoint-struct refactor (deferred), serde_json-for-perception does not breach the serde-free contract, and the eof-ordering tee is the correctness linchpin. NO pinion / SCE / SCXML / sprag-vt change.
carry_forward_bullets: --resume for Dialogue: reuse the session_id the JSON envelope already carries (parsed but unused this round) to avoid the O(n^2) whole-history argv resend + the MAX_ARG_STRLEN single-arg ceiling -- the natural next round, directly synergizing with this one.

Agent token cost: Agent still reports injected bytes and reads the visible damage-delta. The raw tap is clean only for Dialogue's FRESH-pane argv model -- Agent injects into a non-fresh pane, so its raw stdout interleaves the cooked-mode prompt echo with the reply. A shared one-shot-exchange abstraction could let Agent adopt parse_claude_json once a clean reply-region read exists.

total_cost_usd ($) is parsed off the envelope but not surfaced: Outcome carries one integer cost (tokens). A $ display channel belongs on the captured-content (display) side, not the guardrail, if wanted later.

The Endpoint{argv, format, label} struct refactor (collapse the endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b field sprawl into one cohesive per-side struct) is the recommended dedicated follow-up now that ReplyFormat proved the per-endpoint concept.
Raw capture is bounded at 256 KiB head-anchored: a >256 KiB single reply truncates -> parse fails -> graceful byte-proxy fallback (a documented bound, not silent corruption).

NO Driver/SCXML/SCE change -- the cost channel R17 built IS the seam; only what feeds it changed.

Host (crates/sprag-host/src/plugins.rs): the dialogue run arm parses optional format_a/format_b ('text'|'claude_json'; unknown -> synchronous Rejected) via a new parse_reply_format helper; ReplyFormat re-exported from sprag-plugin.
publishable_verification_bullets: 106 workspace tests pass (+17 over R17's 89), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. New deterministic tests: sprag-terminal raw_output byte-faithful-on-a-wrapping-line + over-cap-truncation; sprag-plugin reply parser (real envelope, escaped-\n preserved, framing noise, truncated/garbage/non-envelope -> None, is_error, missing-usage, usage-without-result), pane_raw_output round-trip, dialogue claude_json real-token-cost (cost==2 turns x 50) + token-bound guardrail (50-token budget exhausts in 1 turn) + graceful-degradation-on-bad-JSON (records raw text, does NOT Fail); sprag-host runs_a_claude_json_dialogue_with_real_token_cost (cost==100 over RPC, clean result not raw envelope) + rejects_an_unknown_reply_format.

Live AI re-verified: the #[ignore]d two_real_claudes_converse ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns (~22s) and accumulated real token cost = 18214 (a byte proxy would be a few hundred); the transcript carried the clean result text (no input_tokens envelope leak) and a coherent count -- the real-PTY check that the envelope parses off the raw source with no stderr/spinner/wrap pollution.

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent (read every touched file first): confirmed the raw-stdout tap is the correct seam over the lossy grid (pane_full_text injects a wrap-\n at every row; trailing-trim drops interior spaces in result), the cost unit is total tokens (exact integer, keeps the 64*1024 default guardrail sane) not micro-USD, ReplyFormat is per-endpoint fields not an Endpoint-struct refactor (deferred), serde_json-for-perception does not breach the serde-free contract, and the eof-ordering tee is the correctness linchpin. NO pinion / SCE / SCXML / sprag-vt change.

Agent token cost: Agent still reports injected bytes and reads the visible damage-delta. The raw tap is clean only for Dialogue's FRESH-pane argv model -- Agent injects into a non-fresh pane, so its raw stdout interleaves the cooked-mode prompt echo with the reply. A shared one-shot-exchange abstraction could let Agent adopt parse_claude_json once a clean reply-region read exists.

total_cost_usd ($) is parsed off the envelope but not surfaced: Outcome carries one integer cost (tokens). A $ display channel belongs on the captured-content (display) side, not the guardrail, if wanted later.

The Endpoint{argv, format, label} struct refactor (collapse the endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b field sprawl into one cohesive per-side struct) is the recommended dedicated follow-up now that ReplyFormat proved the per-endpoint concept.
Raw capture is bounded at 256 KiB head-anchored: a >256 KiB single reply truncates -> parse fails -> graceful byte-proxy fallback (a documented bound, not silent corruption).

Round 19.decision_summary: Neutralize the decoded-reply type name to mark the abstraction boundary surfaced by review: the decoded shape is tool-agnostic (AgentReply), while the parser and format variant stay tool-specific (parse_claude_json / ReplyFormat::ClaudeJson) because AI-tool JSON schemas are not standardized.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-plugin/src/reply.rs + lib.rs: renamed ClaudeReply -> AgentReply (the tool-agnostic decoded shape: text + tokens + is_error); parse_claude_json now returns AgentReply, and the struct/module doc generalized to 'a decoded agent reply, independent of which tool produced it'. The parser parse_claude_json and the per-endpoint ReplyFormat::ClaudeJson stay claude-named ON PURPOSE -- they encode claude's specific envelope schema (result / usage.input_tokens), and a generic 'Json' name would be a false abstraction since no cross-tool AI-JSON standard exists.

Made the extension path for a second print-mode-JSON agent explicit: add a ReplyFormat variant + a parser mapping that tool's envelope onto the SAME AgentReply + one decode_reply match arm + one host arg mapping (~30 lines). The raw-stdout tap (pane_raw_output), the cost channel (Step::cost), and the graceful-degradation fallback are already tool-agnostic, so no new result type and no foundation change. An interactive-TUI agent (non print-mode) remains the harder, separately-tracked capture problem.
verification_bullets: Pure rename, no behavior change: 106 workspace tests pass, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean; grep confirms zero ClaudeReply references remain. Prompted by a design question (could the R18 cost path serve a non-claude agent?) -- the answer is yes via the enum+parser seam, and the result type is now named so the shape reads as generic while the parser reads as specific.

Round 20.decision_summary: Make a ClaudeJson Dialogue resume each side's server session (claude -p --resume <session_id>) and send only the peer's last message, replacing the O(n^2) whole-history resend; a resume that returns no session id self-heals to the fresh whole-history path.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-plugin/src/reply.rs: AgentReply gains session_id: Option<String>, extracted from the envelope's session_id key (previously unread). A real-CLI probe confirmed the id is STABLE across a resume, so a side keeps ONE id for the whole run.

crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs: Dialogue holds sessions: [Option<String>; 2] indexed by turn%2 and selected by the SAME parity branch as endpoint/label/format (one SSOT, no drifting second branch). A side's FIRST turn (session None) and every Text endpoint take the UNCHANGED whole-history render_prompt; a ClaudeJson side that already holds a session RESUMES: argv gets ['--resume', id] before the prompt, and the prompt is a new render_resume_prompt = just the peer's last turn (render_turn(history.last())) since the server holds this side's prior context. History still accumulates for the transcript and the fresh/Text path.

decode_reply / decode_claude_json now return a named DecodedTurn{text, cost, session_id} (was a (String,u64) tuple). step() stores the id on every reply that carries one (idempotent; an is_error reply WITH an id is still a continuable session), and RESETS the side to None only when a RESUME turn returns NO id (bad/expired id, or a garbled envelope) -- self-healing to the whole-history fresh path on the next same-side turn. A broken resume never fails the turn (the R18 graceful-degradation philosophy).

Resume is automatic and internal -- gated by ReplyFormat::ClaudeJson + session presence, so NO new spec field, NO RPC arg, NO sprag-host change. NO statechart change (the Step{cost,verdict} contract is unchanged; verdict stays Continue every turn). Only sprag-plugin (reply.rs + dialogue.rs) changed; lib.rs re-exports unchanged (the new AgentReply field rides the existing export).
verification_bullets: 109 workspace tests pass (+3 over R19's 106), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. New network-free tests: reply extracts_session_id_when_present + missing_session_id_yields_none; dialogue claude_json_resumes_after_the_first_turn (an argv-self-inspecting fake proves --resume appears on turn 2+ of EACH side but not turn 1) + resume_failure_self_heals_to_fresh (a fake emitting non-JSON on a --resume call -> the side resets and its next turn parses cleanly again). All prior tests unchanged -- the Text and json_fake paths emit no session_id so they stay on the fresh path.

Live AI re-verified: two_real_claudes_converse (now exercising --resume on turns 2-3) ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns (~14s) with a coherent count ACROSS the resumed turns (proves the server preserved context via --resume). Real token cost = 9129, roughly HALF of R18's 18214 for the same 4-turn conversation -- direct evidence resume cut the per-turn input tokens (delta-only prompts vs whole-history resend).

Probe-grounded (real 2-turn CLI run): claude -p --output-format json --resume <id> works with the prompt as the final positional arg; the session_id is stable across resume; context is preserved (a resumed turn recalled a fact from turn 1). Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent: it endorsed the single-parity-index session shape, the DecodedTurn struct over a tuple, and SHARPENED the resume-failure trigger to 'reset only when a resume turn returns no session_id', NOT on is_error:true-with-id (a tool-side error on a live session is still continuable). NO pinion/SCE/SCXML/host change.
carry_forward_bullets: The real claude behavior for a bad/expired --resume id is UNVERIFIED at the CLI -- the deterministic self-heal test covers the MECHANISM (no-session-id-on-a-resume-turn -> reset), and the detector is robust to both a valid {is_error, no-session} envelope and a non-JSON error. Pin it only if a live bad-id case surfaces.

render_resume_prompt sends the peer's last turn labelled; the turn-0/1 fresh prompt established the per-side instruction in each server session, so the minimal resume prompt relies on that persisting (probe-confirmed). If a future model drifts without re-instruction, re-add a tiny per-turn framing to the resume prompt.
Agent (one-shot) does not use resume; a future multi-turn Agent could reuse this per-side session pattern. Agent token cost + clean reply-region capture remains the separate backlog item.
The Endpoint{argv, format, label} struct refactor (collapse endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b into one per-side struct) is still the recommended cohesion follow-up.

Round 21.decision_summary: R21 remediation of the AI layer: a typed Cost (Bytes vs Tokens, one unit per plugin) replaces the unit-mixing u64 cost and retires the byte proxy; raw-byte capture moves off PaneAccess into a PaneRawCapture sub-trait; and the empty-result envelope leak, the unused AgentReply.is_error field, and stale cost/SSOT docs are fixed.
changes_bullets: Typed cost (plugin.rs/driver.rs): new enum Cost{Bytes(u64),Tokens(u64)} on Step::cost; the Driver accumulates Option<Cost> (one unit per run, a mid-run unit change is debug-asserted via Cost::try_add), Guardrails::max_cost and Outcome::cost become Option<Cost>, and budget_exhausted compares like-with-like via Cost::reaches. The byte-relay plugins (Orchestrator/Pipe/Agent) report Cost::Bytes; Dialogue is uniformly TOKEN-denominated, so the byte proxy (prompt_cost/fallback_cost) is fully RETIRED -- a Text endpoint, a degraded ClaudeJson reply, and a cancelled turn all report Tokens(0) (no measured spend), with max_iterations as the liveness floor.

Host (sprag-host/plugins.rs): DEFAULT_GUARDRAILS split into DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS / DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES / DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS(200k); PluginKind::default_cost() carries each plugin's unit; build_plugin now runs BEFORE parse_guardrails, which reads a bare wire max_cost in that unit (cost_in_unit_of); outcome_to_json emits a self-describing {cost, unit} so a peer reads the cost without knowing the plugin.

RawOutput struct (sprag-terminal/session.rs): the raw-capture (Vec<u8>,bool) tuple is now a named RawOutput{bytes,truncated}, re-exported and destructured at every seam (session.rs, access.rs, dialogue.rs) -- named like PaneRow.

PaneRawCapture sub-trait (sprag-plugin/access.rs): pane_raw_output moved OFF PaneAccess (the scene-as-data extension surface) into a PaneRawCapture trait reached via raw_capture()->Option<&dyn PaneRawCapture>, mirroring PaneLifecycle/lifecycle(). The core invariant 'a plugin reads structured screen data, never raw bytes' is now STRUCTURAL -- only a plugin that asks for the capability can reach raw bytes; Dialogue reaches it via panes.raw_capture().

Empty-result leak (dialogue.rs decode_claude_json): a cleanly-parsed envelope with an empty/missing result now records an EMPTY turn (reply.text.unwrap_or_default()), not the whole JSON envelope; the raw-text fallback is confined to the parse-FAILED arm, so a result-less reply no longer leaks usage/session_id into the transcript or the next prompt. Real tokens are still billed.

YAGNI + doc/SSOT: dropped the unused AgentReply.is_error field + its parse (no consumer read it -- self-heal keys on session_id); the error-envelope test now asserts text/tokens still extract through the ignored key. Restored the cache-token-exclusion rationale (large/bursty would void a token budget) on tokens/parse_tokens; corrected Step::cost's 'positive/monotonic' doc to 'non-negative, Tokens(0) possible, iterations is the liveness guarantee'; fixed render_turn's doc (the blank-line join is at the call sites, not in render_turn); threaded Guardrails through the dialogue test run_with() helper so the cost-binding test stops inlining a Driver.
verification_bullets: 110 workspace tests pass (+1: clean_empty_result_records_an_empty_turn_not_the_envelope), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. Cost tests migrated to the typed value: claude_json_degrades_on_unparsable_reply flips from cost>0 (the old byte proxy) to Some(Cost::Tokens(0)); claude_json_reply_reports_real_token_cost asserts Some(Cost::Tokens(100)); the orchestrator byte-budget test asserts Some(Cost::Bytes(n)); the RPC dialogue test asserts cost==100 AND unit=='tokens'.

Live-verified (touches the AI path): two_real_claudes_converse, now under typed Cost, ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns (~14s) and accumulated real token cost Some(Tokens(9095)) -- coherent with R20's ~9129 -- with a clean transcript and no envelope leak. The typed-tokens path works end-to-end with real claude.

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent, then SHARPENED in an adversarial review: the agent recommended a two-balance (parallel bytes+tokens) budget to accommodate a heterogeneous Dialogue, but a from-first-principles pass identified the byte proxy as the root smell -- retiring it makes 'one plugin = one unit' structurally TRUE, so a single typed Cost (not two parallel balances) is the more textbook, SSOT-respecting seam, closer to this round's original 'Driver refuses to sum across units' intent. Confirmed NO SCXML / SCE-codegen change (orchestration.scxml is datamodel=null; the cost accumulator is plain Rust around the engine).
carry_forward_bullets: Deferred WITH rationale: per-pane OPT-IN raw capture (today every TerminalSession carries a 256 KiB-capable RawCapture buffer even for a shell/cat pane that never reads it) -- it crosses into the producer crate's spawn signature, so it stays an R22 candidate; PaneRawCapture now makes it implementable with no further API churn (raw_capture() can return None for an opt-out pane).

Conversation/session collaborator extraction from the Dialogue god-plugin (the fresh->resumed->reset session lifecycle is a hand-rolled state machine that belongs in SCE -- the dogfood) plus the Endpoint{argv,format,label} struct (collapsing endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b): still deferred.

Interactive-TUI agent seam + a ReplyDecoder trait the PLUGIN supplies (vs the closed in-crate ReplyFormat enum), due when a 2nd AI-tool adapter lands -- the architecture lens called that the north star's defining event. Typed Cost already clarifies its contract: a decoder returns Cost, not u64.

Agent still reports Cost::Bytes (injected) and reads the visible damage-delta (it injects into a non-fresh pane); a clean reply-region read + parse_claude_json adoption is the natural 'third consumer' that would justify a shared one-shot-exchange abstraction.

total_cost_usd ($) display channel belongs on the captured-content side, not the guardrail. pinion R1.6 GPU glyph paint LANDED (R991/384f2f4) so the GUI windowed-host is newly unblocked for GPU text, but pending the cursor slice + the whole TUI backend; sprag still builds NO bespoke renderer.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: Deferred WITH rationale: per-pane OPT-IN raw capture (today every TerminalSession carries a 256 KiB-capable RawCapture buffer even for a shell/cat pane that never reads it) -- it crosses into the producer crate's spawn signature, so it stays an R22 candidate; PaneRawCapture now makes it implementable with no further API churn (raw_capture() can return None for an opt-out pane).

Conversation/session collaborator extraction from the Dialogue god-plugin (the fresh->resumed->reset session lifecycle is a hand-rolled state machine that belongs in SCE -- the dogfood) plus the Endpoint{argv,format,label} struct (collapsing endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b): still deferred.

Interactive-TUI agent seam + a ReplyDecoder trait the PLUGIN supplies (vs the closed in-crate ReplyFormat enum), due when a 2nd AI-tool adapter lands -- the architecture lens called that the north star's defining event. Typed Cost already clarifies its contract: a decoder returns Cost, not u64.

Agent still reports Cost::Bytes (injected) and reads the visible damage-delta (it injects into a non-fresh pane); a clean reply-region read + parse_claude_json adoption is the natural 'third consumer' that would justify a shared one-shot-exchange abstraction.

total_cost_usd ($) display channel belongs on the captured-content side, not the guardrail. pinion R1.6 GPU glyph paint LANDED (R991/384f2f4) so the GUI windowed-host is newly unblocked for GPU text, but pending the cursor slice + the whole TUI backend; sprag still builds NO bespoke renderer.

Round 21.1.decision_summary: Post-R21 adversarial session review (refactoring + architecture lenses + direct SSOT cross-check) found R21 mechanically sound and the single-typed-Cost decision correct, but NOT fully textbook; the R21.1 clearance fixes the shared must-fix + the majors.
changes_bullets: Dead-API + open/closed (plugin.rs/plugins.rs): both reviewers independently flagged `Cost::amount()` as dead public API while the host re-matched variants inline. Added `Cost::unit() -> &'static str` (the single variant->label mapping), and `outcome_to_json` now does `outcome.cost.map_or((0,None), |c| (c.amount(), Some(c.unit())))` — so the host NEVER names a `Cost` variant. A new cost unit now edits only plugin.rs + `PluginKind::default_cost` (the legitimate plugin->unit map), not the host's render/parse.

Silent fail-open (plugin.rs): `Cost::reaches`'s unit-mismatch arm returned `false` with no guard — a disarmed spend guardrail failing silently. Added a `debug_assert!(false, ...)` (matching `accumulate`'s `try_add` guard) so a mismatch screams in debug and still reports not-reached (iteration-bounded) in release.

Self-describing guardrail wire (plugins.rs/rpc.rs): replaced the unit-BLIND bare `max_cost` (a dialogue caller could load a byte-intended number as a 64x-looser TOKEN bound with no feedback) with self-describing `max_bytes` XOR `max_tokens`, validated against the plugin's unit via `Cost::unit()` — wrong unit / both keys -> synchronous `Rejected` (new `parse_max_cost`, removed `cost_in_unit_of`). New test `rejects_a_wrong_unit_guardrail`; 6 RPC wire sites migrated.

Honest docs (plugins.rs): the module header + `parse_guardrails` no longer claim a cost bound that a `Tokens(0)`-only (print-mode Text) dialogue cannot deliver — they now state iterations are its sole effective bound, by design. `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS` is documented as a COARSE backstop (cache tokens excluded; the iteration cap is primary), not a precise spend bound.

Stale-doc sweep (dialogue.rs/reply.rs): rewrote the PUBLIC `ReplyFormat::Text`/`ClaudeJson` docs (still said 'prompt-byte proxy' / 'degrades to the byte proxy' — false after R21 retired it; now `Tokens(0)`), fixed a degrades-test comment that CONTRADICTED its own `Tokens(0)` assertion, and swept the remaining byte-proxy mentions in reply.rs module/parse docs and the test contrast comments.
verification_bullets: 111 workspace tests pass (+1: rejects_a_wrong_unit_guardrail; sprag-host 33, sprag-plugin 37 +2 ignored), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. R21.1 touches only docs, a new Cost::unit(), the release-inert reaches debug-guard, and the host wire (fully covered by the deterministic RPC tests) -- it does NOT touch the token decode/accumulate path R21 already live-verified, so the live AI test was consciously not re-run (unchanged, covered).

Driven by two independent adversarial reviewers (a refactoring lens + an architecture lens) over `git diff f1688a3 9b03d2a` plus a direct SSOT grep. They CONVERGED on the dead `amount()` + the stale byte-proxy docs (both must-fix). The architecture lens explicitly RULED the R21 single-typed-Cost decision correct over the Plan agent's two-balance (two-balance bakes 'exactly two units forever' into the Driver/Guardrails shape -- the real open/closed violation). The clearance addressed every must-fix and major they raised.
carry_forward_bullets: is_error (architecture lens, deferred WITH rationale): the review flagged that R21 dropped `AgentReply.is_error` -- the one structured ERROR bit in the tool-agnostic decoded shape -- as an implicit capability narrowing (a future 'stop the dialogue when a side errors' policy would want it). Decision: KEEP it removed (the project's own YAGNI / no-dead-surface rule; re-adding a consumer-less bool re-introduces the exact smell R21 removed), and re-add `is_error` + its parse line TOGETHER with the error-aware-orchestration policy that consumes it. The error-envelope parse-tolerance test already proves the flag's key does not derail parsing when it returns.

Cost open/closed is now clean: a hypothetical `Cost::Dollars` edits only plugin.rs (the enum + amount/unit/try_add/reaches arms, all next to the type) and `PluginKind::default_cost` (the plugin->unit assignment) -- the host's outcome rendering and guardrail parsing are variant-name-free via `unit()`/`amount()`.

The Outcome::cost `Option<Cost>` double-optionality (None only on a cancel-at-loop-top, 0-step run) was reviewed and kept: seeding a concrete zero needs a unit the Driver lacks when max_cost is None, so Option is the honest model.

Round 22.decision_summary: Decompose the Dialogue god-plugin into an Endpoint struct (collapsing the parallel endpoint/label/format field pairs) and a Session collaborator whose fresh/resumed/reset server-session lifecycle is sprag's second SCE statechart (the dogfood), unblocked by an upstream SCE +Send fix on Engine's boxed callbacks.
changes_bullets: Endpoint struct (sprag-plugin/dialogue.rs): collapsed the six parallel fields endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b into Endpoint{argv,label,format} and DialogueSpec.endpoints: [Endpoint; 2]; the turn%2 parity now selects ONE Endpoint so argv/label/format cannot drift apart. DialogueSpec::new(argv_a,argv_b,seed) keeps its signature (defaults labels A/B + ReplyFormat::Text); Endpoint re-exported (a public field type).

Session collaborator (new sprag-plugin/session.rs + session.scxml): a per-endpoint server-session lifecycle modeled as a 2-state REACTIVE SCE statechart (states fresh/resumed, events opened/absent, NO <final>, datamodel=null) — sprag's SECOND SCE machine after the Driver's orchestration.scxml (the dogfood generalizing the build to N machines). Session{engine: Engine<SessionPolicy>, id} holds the id String beside the engine (a null datamodel cannot hold it, like the Driver's counters beside its lifecycle machine). resuming()->Option<&str> is Some iff resumed; record(Option<String>) folds a decoded id into the lifecycle, ordered store-then-Opened / Absent-then-clear.

Dialogue integration: replaced sessions:[Option<String>;2] + the hand-rolled match decoded.session_id { Some=>store, None if resume=>reset, None=>{} } with sessions:[Session;2] + Session::record. The resume gate format==ClaudeJson && session.is_some() collapsed to resuming().is_some() (state==resumed) — SUBSUMED because a Text turn decodes to no id so its Session stays fresh forever. The reset rule (a resume returning no id => fresh) is now the resumed--absent-->fresh transition. step() clones argv/label/format and the resume id out before the spawn (borrow discipline).

The state<->id invariant: after every record, (state==resumed) <=> id.is_some(), debug_asserted — LOAD-BEARING, a Plan-agent + adversarial design pass identified it as what makes the new state-based resume/reset gate equivalent to the old intent-based resume bool (documented in session.rs).

build/codegen (build.rs, lib.rs, driver.rs): build.rs compiles BOTH statecharts via a STATECHARTS stem list and generalizes the inner-attr strip to each generated file; the sm module split into sm::orchestration + sm::session submodules (each its own include! so the duplicate generated use lines stay isolated); driver.rs import path updated; PluginKind::Dialogue boxed (the two embedded session engines made it a clippy large_enum_variant).

Host (sprag-host/plugins.rs): the dialogue build arm bridges the FLAT wire keys (endpoint_a/label_a/format_a — the RPC protocol is UNCHANGED) into endpoints[0/1]; the Endpoint struct is an in-Rust cohesion fix, not a wire regrouping (the intra-struct drift hazard it prevents does not exist on the wire).

Upstream SCE unblock (stop-and-report rule, NOT worked around): Engine

was !Send because its completion_callback / on_http_send boxed closures lacked a +Send bound, blocking a plugin holding a Session engine from being moved into sprag's R11 background-run worker thread (the Driver dodges this by building its engine in-thread; a submit-time-built plugin cannot). Reported upstream and fixed in SCE (+Send bound => Engine

: Send when P is), pinned via the pinion vendor submodule bump 57e06f1e -> 3078f8bf7.
verification_bullets: 116 workspace tests pass (sprag-plugin 42 +2 ignored incl. 5 new Session unit tests: starts-fresh, an-id-opens-resume, id-less-stays-fresh, idempotent-latest-id, lost-resume-self-heals; sprag-host 33; sprag-vt 19; sprag-input 11; sprag-terminal 7; sprag-grid 4). cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean after boxing the large Dialogue variant.

Live-verified (the resume seam moved into the SCE Session, so the AI path was re-run): two_real_claudes_converse ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns THROUGH the new Session state machine and accumulated real token cost Some(Tokens(9129)) — coherent with R20/R21 (~9129/9095) and ~half R18's whole-history 18214, confirming --resume still cuts per-turn tokens via delta-only prompts driven by the SCE lifecycle.

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent (verdict sound-with-changes, "no upstream gap halts" — which proved false at integration: the Engine !Send gap surfaced only at the host thread boundary and was fixed upstream). Confirmed SCE codegens AND runs a REACTIVE no-<final> statechart (the 5 Session tests exercise the live Engine end-to-end), confirmed the state<->id invariant underpins the gate equivalence, ruled Session (not a broader Conversation) the honest reusable seam, and kept the wire flat. The dogfood is justified by the multi-machine build proof + the legible lifecycle, NOT the 2-state complexity.
carry_forward_bullets: Session is the reusable resume collaborator: a future single-endpoint multi-turn Agent can hold one Session (resuming()/record()) to adopt --resume without copy-pasting the lifecycle. Promote Session from pub(crate) to pub WHEN that real second consumer lands (no premature public API).

A broader Conversation collaborator (two-party history + prompt rendering) was deliberately NOT extracted: it is Dialogue-specific (an Agent reuses the session lifecycle, not the transcript), so extracting it now would be a speculative/wrong abstraction. render_prompt/render_resume_prompt/decode_reply stay in dialogue.rs.
The Endpoint{argv,label,format} struct landed; a future per-endpoint knob (a model name, a temperature) is a new Endpoint field touched in one place, not a 4th parallel xxx_a/xxx_b pair.
Interactive-TUI agent seam + a ReplyDecoder trait the PLUGIN supplies (vs the closed in-crate ReplyFormat enum) remains the north star's defining event, due when a 2nd AI-tool adapter lands.

Agent still reports Cost::Bytes + reads the visible damage-delta; a clean reply-region read + parse_claude_json adoption + (now) a reusable Session is the natural third consumer that would justify a shared one-shot-exchange abstraction.

SCE Engine

is now Send (the +Send callback bound): an SCE state machine can live in any worker-movable value, removing the prior constraint that engines be Driver-in-thread only.

Round 26.decision_summary: Round 26: land the resize -> PTY reflow consumer of pinion's R1006 view-time viewport-size seam (use_viewport_size), closing PINION-REQUIREMENTS PR-6 on the sprag side - sprag-gui is pinion's first viewport-dependent producer.
changes_bullets: sprag-gui: pure grid_dims(viewport,cell)->(cols,rows) is the single SSOT for the window-drives-winsize derivation (boot spawn + reflow share it); install_reflow registers an Effect that subscribes to pinion's R1006 viewport-size Signal and reflows the boot pane (Workspace::resize) on resize, skipping the (0,0) unknown boot value and any no-change frame.

sprag-terminal: TerminalSession::resize and Workspace::resize are now &self (MasterPty::resize is &self; the emulator is Mutex-guarded), so a shared &Workspace reached through an Rc in the reflow Effect reflows without &mut; the (cols,rows) cache fields are dropped and dimensions() reads the emulator screen (single source - a latent dual-source repair).

The reflow is a real side-effect (TIOCSWINSZ), so it lives in an Effect (gated out of dry_run/snapshot paint by the R1006 seam), never the pure view; the Effect reads the captured Signal directly (not use_viewport_size), so it never resolves Owner::current and is robust to the set scope.

Round 27.decision_summary: Round 27: make the GUI terminal interactive - route focused keystrokes to the boot pane's PTY through the same SpragPaneExternal invoke('key', ...) wire the headless RPC path drives (one input substrate, R2.6 / section 2 #2).

Round 28.decision_summary: Round 28: give the GUI terminal an accessible node (WidgetA11y::access_node was empty) - one neutral focusable Group region tagged ROOT_TAG, named by the pane command, carrying the screen full_text as its value, focus-gated; a screen reader / AccessKit tree can now read the terminal (the AI path stays scene/snapshot).
changes_bullets: sprag-gui: access_node returns one terminal_a11y_node (pure helper) over the boot pane - AriaRole::Group (not TextInput: pinion has no terminal/log role, and a textbox would advertise caret/set-value edit affordances the PTY-keystroke widget does not implement), name = "Terminal: <command>", value = AccessValue::Text(screen full_text), focused = (focus == ROOT_TAG).
The screen text reuses Screen::full_text - the same SSOT string the RPC full_text query and the plugin capture read, so the AT and the AI see one notion of the screen (scrollback + visible).
The node tag is ROOT_TAG, shared with the keyboard focus gate (apply_key) and the paint-root container, so AT focus + bounds + the key focus gate share one identity.

Closes the walking-skeleton slice PTY -> emulator -> GridBuffer -> Scene::TextGrid -> scene/snapshot, GPU-free via pinion_rpc::snapshot
Headless winsize: the producer sets the TextGrid node rect from screen dims x CellMetric (no window, no layout pass)
Workspace: added sprag-terminal member and the pinion-rpc path dependency
publishable_verification_bullets: 19 tests pass (sprag-vt 10, sprag-grid 4, sprag-terminal 5); cargo clippy clean on all sprag crates
End-to-end smoke test: /bin/sh printf output travels through a real PTY to the TextGridSnapshot
Confirmed pinion-rpc and pinion-runtime carry no vello/winit/wgpu dependency, substantiating the headless claim
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: Live RPC server bin (stdin/stdout JSON-RPC) so an external AI can query a running session
Input encoding (keys -> PTY bytes) and mouse hit-test remain sprag-owned (PINION-REQUIREMENTS R2.6/R1.8)
Windowed host via pinion_shell::run + compute_layout once human GUI rendering is wanted
Decide scrollback projection (R1.4 gap) when a consumer first needs it

Round 30.decision_summary: Round 30: session-review remediation of R26-R29 (four-reviewer + grep audit) - extract a boot_pane() SSOT accessor unifying single-pane selection (5 sites / 3 absence idioms -> 1) and correct overstated/stale docs; no behavior change. The data-flow SSOT, concurrency, and pinion-boundary consumption were cleared as textbook.
changes_bullets: sprag-gui: TerminalView::boot_pane() -> &Pane is the one site answering "which pane?" - view / access_node / scroll_view / the reflow Effect / pane_handle all route through it (was 5 panes().first() sites with 3 different absence idioms: .expect / else-return / filter-map), unified to the documented boot-pane invariant so the multi-pane round generalizes pane selection in one place.

sprag-terminal: resize/dimensions docs corrected - they overstated atomicity (the PTY winsize ioctl precedes the emulator update by one uncontended lock, so a SIGWINCH-racing child may transiently observe the new winsize first; transient, visual-only, self-healing).

Doc/staleness: window title no longer round-pinned (omitted R28/R29); the "read-only behavior" comment reworded (frozen final screen, not a loss of interactivity); the a11y Group-over-Generic choice documented (a Generic container drops the accessible name).
verification_bullets: Four independent adversarial reviewers (architecture / SSOT / concurrency / pinion-boundary) + a repo-wide grep audit. Cleared as textbook: projection / winsize / screen-text / key-encoding / dimensions SSOT; no race / deadlock / leak / UAF (reader thread + Mutex + Drop graph traced); idiomatic seam consumption (the apply_key hand-roll is justified - forward_key_to_external cannot carry modifiers and has the wrong verdict mapping); the GUI is a faithful secondary path, never a second authority.

sprag-grid 6 + sprag-host 34 + sprag-gui 11 + sprag-terminal 8 = 59 tests pass; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean; cargo doc no new broken links; headless screenshot byte-identical (121434) - the refactor is behavior-preserving.

Deferred (named, not hidden): scroll-during-output drift (proper fix = content-anchor needs producer-side scrollback-growth reactivity; the bounded FIFO has no stable line identity a pure view can track); main.rs modularization (762 lines, best paid at the multi-pane round); full-cell scrollback (R16 text-only model).
carry_forward_bullets: Multi-pane round: generalize boot_pane() -> active_pane() + per-pane tags (the ROOT_TAG singleton has 26 refs) + focused-pane input routing; modularize main.rs (terminal / reflow / input / a11y / view) at the same time.
Scroll content-anchoring: expose scrollback growth reactively from the producer (sprag-vt) so the GUI can pin the view to absolute content under output, removing the v1 bottom-relative drift.
Mouse / pointer->cell (R1.8) needs a pinion seam (a click delivered to a TextGrid widget with cell coords) - a separate spec-round, on the pinion side of the boundary.

Round 31.decision_summary: Round 31: IME-composed input (Hangul / CJK) routed to the PTY via a new literal-text seam. A composed commit is finished text, not a keystroke, so it must bypass the W3C key encoder: a sibling invoke("text", ...) action on SpragPaneExternal writes the committed UTF-8 directly to the child, and TerminalViewer::apply_composition (a WidgetCore override, focus-gated on ROOT_TAG, a faithful mirror of apply_key) drives it. Preedit stays off-grid, rendered by the platform IME; an inline on-grid preedit overlay is a later round.
changes_bullets: sprag-host: SpragPaneExternal gains a "text" invoke action (inject_text) writing literal UTF-8 to the PTY with no key-encoding - the seam for IME commits and paste, the same scene/invoke wire the AI peer drives (§2 #2). parse_text_args accepts a bare string or a {text:...} object (symmetric with the key parser); empty text is a no-op success (the IME cancel-via-empty-commit shape). The introspect schema lists text beside key.

sprag-gui: TerminalViewer::apply_composition (WidgetCore override) routes CompositionEvent::Commit to invoke("text", ...), focus-gated on ROOT_TAG and snapping the scrollback view to the live bottom - a faithful mirror of apply_key. Start/Update (preedit) and Cancel are not consumed; the platform IME renders the in-progress composition itself.

A composition commit is text, not a keystroke, so it deliberately bypasses sprag-input::encode (W3C key -> control bytes); the literal-text path is the textbook seam rather than fabricating synthetic keystrokes.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace: all pass, 0 failed; 4 new tests - apply_composition_routes_committed_ime_text_to_the_pane (e2e: committed Hangul echoes back through a live cat PTY in cooked mode), parses_bare_string_text, parses_object_text, non_string_text_is_type_mismatch; the focus-gate, preedit (Update), and empty-commit cases asserted as deterministic no-ops.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean (exit 0); validate-workspace T1 orphan=0; entries 31 -> 32.

Audit-first against pinion: WidgetCore::apply_composition(scene, focused, event)->bool (default false) override confirmed; ShellCore::apply_composition sources focused via focus.focused() and runs V::apply_composition inside root_owner.run (so use_scroll_offset resolves an Owner); winit WindowEvent::Ime -> winit_ime_to_composition -> Commit is wired in pinion-shell app.rs; IntrospectValue::Text(String) is the literal payload variant.
carry_forward_bullets: Multi-pane: generalize boot_pane() -> active_pane() + per-pane tags (the ROOT_TAG singleton) + focused-pane input routing (key + composition + future mouse); modularize the 762-line main.rs (terminal / reflow / input / a11y / view) at the same time.

Scroll content-anchoring: expose scrollback growth reactively from the producer (sprag-vt) so the GUI pins the view to absolute content under output, removing the v1 bottom-relative drift. Full-cell scrollback (the R16 text-only history model loses colors) folds in here.

IME inline preedit overlay: the platform IME renders the in-progress composition off-grid; an on-grid preedit overlay (plus set_ime_cursor_area positioning) is a later round. Mouse / pointer->cell is now unblocked pinion-side (R1008 px_to_cell + R1009 named-key + R1010 focus-ring opt-out); the remaining sprag work is the pane mouse-report consumer (byte encoding + per-pane routing).

Round 32.decision_summary: Round 32: behavior-preserving modularization of the single sprag-gui main.rs into five concern-scoped modules (terminal/reflow/input/a11y/view) — the refactor-first step R30's carry required before the multi-pane round; no behavior change (135 tests unchanged, screenshot byte-identical 121434).
changes_bullets: main.rs slimmed to the crate-level docs, the five `mod` declarations, the forge renderer macro (crate-root-required), ROOT_TAG/WINDOW_W/WINDOW_H, the TerminalViewer struct, and the WidgetCore/WidgetView impl that delegates to the module helpers (use_terminal/install_reflow/route_key/route_composition/view) — no logic in main beyond wiring.

terminal.rs: the terminal model and config — TerminalView{workspace,metric,font_size_px} + boot_pane/pane_handle, use_terminal (the Owner::cache self-create hook), grid_dims (the window->winsize SSOT), pane_command/split_command, parse_font_size/font_size_px.
